v: There was a man in the land of Uz[^1] whose name was Job. That man was blameless[^2] and upright; he feared God and turned away from evil.
אִ֛ישׁ הָיָ֥ה בְאֶֽרֶץ־ע֖וּץ אִיּ֣וֹב שְׁמ֑וֹ וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֗וּא תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר וִירֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֥ר מֵרָֽע׃
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
וַיִּוָּ֥לְדוּ ל֛וֹ שִׁבְעָ֥ה בָנִ֖ים וְשָׁל֥וֹשׁ בָּנֽוֹת׃

His livestock numbered seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred female donkeys, and he had a great many servants. That man was the greatest of all the people of the East.[^3]

וַיְהִ֣י מִ֠קְנֵהוּ שִֽׁבְעַ֨ת אַלְפֵי־צֹ֜אן וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֣י גְמַלִּ֗ים וַחֲמֵ֨שׁ מֵא֤וֹת צֶֽמֶד־בָּקָר֙ וַחֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אֲתוֹנ֔וֹת וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיְהִי֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא גָּד֖וֹל מִכָּל־בְּנֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃
His sons used to go and hold a feast in the house of each one in turn,[^4] and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
וְהָלְכ֤וּ בָנָיו֙ וְעָשׂ֣וּ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אִ֣ישׁ יוֹמ֑וֹ וְשָׁלְח֗וּ וְקָרְאוּ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת *אחיתיהם **אַחְיֽוֹתֵיהֶ֔ם לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת עִמָּהֶֽם׃

When the days of feasting had run their course, Job would send for them and purify them.[^5] He would get up early in the morning and offer burnt offerings for each one of them, for Job thought, "Perhaps my children[^6] have sinned and cursed[^7] God in their hearts." This is what Job always did.

וַיְהִ֡י כִּ֣י הִקִּיפֽוּ֩ יְמֵ֨י הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֜ה וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח אִיּ֣וֹב וַֽיְקַדְּשֵׁ֗ם וְהִשְׁכִּ֣ים בַּבֹּקֶר֮ וְהֶעֱלָ֣ה עֹלוֹת֮ מִסְפַּ֣ר כֻּלָּם֒ כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר אִיּ֔וֹב אוּלַי֙ חָטְא֣וּ בָנַ֔י וּבֵרֲכ֥וּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בִּלְבָבָ֑ם כָּ֛כָה יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אִיּ֖וֹב כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃ פ
One day the sons of God[^8] came to present themselves before the LORD,[^9] and the Accuser[^10] also came among them.
וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּב֥וֹא גַֽם־הַשָּׂטָ֖ן בְּתוֹכָֽם׃
The LORD said to the Accuser, "Where have you come from?" The Accuser answered the LORD, "From roaming the earth and walking about on it."
וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֖ן מֵאַ֣יִן תָּבֹ֑א וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׂטָ֤ן אֶת־יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מִשּׁ֣וּט בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵֽהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּֽהּ׃
The LORD said to the Accuser, "Have you considered[^11] my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth, a blameless and upright man who fears God and turns away from evil."
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֔ן הֲשַׂ֥מְתָּ לִבְּךָ֖ עַל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין כָּמֹ֙הוּ֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֥ר מֵרָֽע׃
The Accuser answered the LORD, "Is it for nothing that Job fears God?
וַיַּ֧עַן הַשָּׂטָ֛ן אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַֽחִנָּ֔ם יָרֵ֥א אִיּ֖וֹב אֱלֹהִֽים׃
Have you not put a hedge around him and his household and everything he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock have spread out over the land.
הֲלֹֽא־*את **אַ֠תָּה שַׂ֣כְתָּ בַעֲד֧וֹ וּבְעַד־בֵּית֛וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֖וֹ מִסָּבִ֑יב מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יָדָיו֙ בֵּרַ֔כְתָּ וּמִקְנֵ֖הוּ פָּרַ֥ץ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
But stretch out your hand now and touch everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face."[^12]
וְאוּלָם֙ שְֽׁלַֽח־נָ֣א יָֽדְךָ֔ וְגַ֖ע בְּכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֥א עַל־פָּנֶ֖יךָ יְבָרֲכֶֽךָּ׃
The LORD said to the Accuser, "Very well, everything he has is in your power.[^13] Only do not stretch out your hand against him." Then the Accuser went out from the presence of the LORD.
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֗ן הִנֵּ֤ה כָל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ רַ֣ק אֵלָ֔יו אַל־תִּשְׁלַ֖ח יָדֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּצֵא֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן מֵעִ֖ם פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
One day, when Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their oldest brother,
וַיְהִ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וּבָנָ֨יו וּבְנֹתָ֤יו אֹֽכְלִים֙ וְשֹׁתִ֣ים יַ֔יִן בְּבֵ֖ית אֲחִיהֶ֥ם הַבְּכֽוֹר׃
a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing beside them,
וּמַלְאָ֛ךְ בָּ֥א אֶל־אִיּ֖וֹב וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַבָּקָר֙ הָי֣וּ חֹֽרְשׁ֔וֹת וְהָאֲתֹנ֖וֹת רֹע֥וֹת עַל־יְדֵיהֶֽם׃
and the Sabeans[^14] swooped down and took them. They struck down the servants[^15] with the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
וַתִּפֹּ֤ל שְׁבָא֙ וַתִּקָּחֵ֔ם וְאֶת־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים הִכּ֣וּ לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וָֽאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃
While he was still speaking, another came and said, "The fire of God[^16] fell from the sky and burned up the sheep and the servants and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
ע֣וֹד ׀ זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֗ר וְזֶה֮ בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַר֒ אֵ֣שׁ אֱלֹהִ֗ים נָֽפְלָה֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתִּבְעַ֥ר בַּצֹּ֛אן וּבַנְּעָרִ֖ים וַתֹּאכְלֵ֑ם וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

While he was still speaking, another came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three raiding parties[^17] and made a raid on the camels and took them. They struck down the servants with the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."

ע֣וֹד ׀ זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֗ר וְזֶה֮ בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַר֒ כַּשְׂדִּ֞ים שָׂ֣מוּ ׀ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֗ים וַֽיִּפְשְׁט֤וּ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּים֙ וַיִּקָּח֔וּם וְאֶת־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים הִכּ֣וּ לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃
While he was still speaking, another came and said, "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their oldest brother,
עַ֚ד זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֔ר וְזֶ֖ה בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַ֑ר בָּנֶ֨יךָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֤יךָ אֹֽכְלִים֙ וְשֹׁתִ֣ים יַ֔יִן בְּבֵ֖ית אֲחִיהֶ֥ם הַבְּכֽוֹר׃
and suddenly a great wind came from across the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It fell on the young people,[^18] and they died, and I alone have escaped to tell you."

וְהִנֵּה֩ ר֨וּחַ גְּדוֹלָ֜ה בָּ֣אָה ׀ מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַמִּדְבָּ֗ר וַיִּגַּע֙ בְּאַרְבַּע֙ פִּנּ֣וֹת הַבַּ֔יִת וַיִּ[t]פֹּ֥ל עַל־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים וַיָּמ֑וּתוּ וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃
Then Job got up, tore his robe and shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshiped.[^19]
וַיָּ֤קָם אִיּוֹב֙ וַיִּקְרַ֣ע אֶת־מְעִל֔וֹ וַיָּ֖גָז אֶת־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃
He said, "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I will return there.[^20] The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. May the name of the LORD be blessed."
וַיֹּאמֶר֩ עָרֹ֨ם *יצתי **יָצָ֜אתִי מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמִּ֗י וְעָרֹם֙ אָשׁ֣וּב שָׁ֔מָה יְהוָ֣ה נָתַ֔ן וַיהוָ֖ה לָקָ֑ח יְהִ֛י שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה מְבֹרָֽךְ׃
In all this Job did not sin, and he did not accuse God of wrongdoing.[^21]
בְּכָל־זֹ֖את לֹא־חָטָ֣א אִיּ֑וֹב וְלֹא־נָתַ֥ן תִּפְלָ֖ה לֵאלֹהִֽים׃ פ

n.1: A region east or southeast of Israel, perhaps in Edom (Lamentations 4:21) or northern Arabia.
n.2: Hebrew *tam*: whole, complete, a person of integrity. Also in verse 8.
n.3: Literally "the sons of the east", the peoples east of Israel.
n.4: Literally "in the house of each one, his day": perhaps each son's birthday (compare 3:1), or each one in turn.
n.5: Literally "make them holy". He had them prepare to come before God.
n.6: Literally "my sons".
n.7: Literally "blessed". Here and in verse 11, 2:5 and 2:9, the Hebrew says "bless" in place of "curse", to avoid writing the words "curse God".
n.8: Literally "the sons of God" (Hebrew *bene ha-elohim*): heavenly beings who serve in God's court, as in 2:1 and 38:7 (compare Genesis 6:2; Psalm 29:1). The Greek Septuagint reads "the angels of God".
n.9: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.10: Hebrew *ha-satan*, "the adversary, the accuser", with the article: a title rather than a name. Traditionally "Satan".
n.11: Literally "set your heart on".
n.12: Literally "if he will not bless you to your face". On "bless" for "curse", see verse 5. The form "if not" is that of an oath: "I swear he will".
n.13: Literally "in your hand".
n.14: Hebrew *Sheva*, Sheba, a people of Arabia.
n.15: Or "the young men". Also in verses 16 and 17.
n.16: Probably lightning. Or "a tremendous fire".
n.17: Literally "set three heads".
n.18: Hebrew *ne'arim*, the word translated "servants" in verses 15–17.
n.19: Or "bowed down", as in worship.
n.20: Perhaps to the earth, pictured as the mother of all (compare Psalm 139:15), or to the grave.
n.21: Literally "he did not give unseemliness to God". Hebrew *tiflah*: what is unfitting or offensive.

v: One day the sons of God[^1] came to present themselves before the LORD,[^2] and the Accuser[^3] also came among them to present himself before the LORD.
וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּב֤וֹא גַֽם־הַשָּׂטָן֙ בְּתֹכָ֔ם לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־יְהוָֽה׃
The LORD said to the Accuser, "Where have you come from?" The Accuser answered the LORD, "From roaming the earth and walking about on it."
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֔ן אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּבֹ֑א וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׂטָ֤ן אֶת־יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מִשֻּׁ֣ט בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּֽהּ׃

The LORD said to the Accuser, "Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth, a blameless and upright man who fears God and turns away from evil. He still holds firmly to his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him for no reason."[^4]

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֗ן הֲשַׂ֣מְתָּ לִבְּךָ֮ אֶל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּוֹב֒ כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין כָּמֹ֜הוּ בָּאָ֗רֶץ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וְעֹדֶ֙נּוּ֙ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּת֔וֹ וַתְּסִיתֵ֥נִי ב֖וֹ לְבַלְּע֥וֹ חִנָּֽם׃
The Accuser answered the LORD, "Skin for skin![^5] A man will give everything he has for his life.
וַיַּ֧עַן הַשָּׂטָ֛ן אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר ע֣וֹר בְּעַד־ע֗וֹר וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָאִ֔ישׁ יִתֵּ֖ן בְּעַ֥ד נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
But stretch out your hand now and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will surely curse you to your face."[^6]
אוּלָם֙ שְֽׁלַֽח־נָ֣א יָֽדְךָ֔ וְגַ֥ע אֶל־עַצְמ֖וֹ וְאֶל־בְּשָׂר֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֥א אֶל־פָּנֶ֖יךָ יְבָרֲכֶֽךָּ׃
The LORD said to the Accuser, "Very well, he is in your power. Only spare his life."
וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֖ן הִנּ֣וֹ בְיָדֶ֑ךָ אַ֖ךְ אֶת־נַפְשׁ֥וֹ שְׁמֹֽר׃
So the Accuser went out from the presence of the LORD, and he struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
וַיֵּצֵא֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן מֵאֵ֖ת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־אִיּוֹב֙ בִּשְׁחִ֣ין רָ֔ע מִכַּ֥ף רַגְל֖וֹ *עד **וְעַ֥ד קָדְקֳדֽוֹ׃
Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself with as he sat among the ashes.
וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ חֶ֔רֶשׂ לְהִתְגָּרֵ֖ד בּ֑וֹ וְה֖וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּתוֹךְ־הָאֵֽפֶר׃
His wife said to him, "Are you still holding firmly to your integrity? Curse God[^7] and die!"
וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ עֹדְךָ֖ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּתֶ֑ךָ בָּרֵ֥ךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וָמֻֽת׃
But he said to her, "You are talking like a foolish woman.[^8] Shall we accept the good from God, and not accept the bad?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֗יהָ כְּדַבֵּ֞ר אַחַ֤ת הַנְּבָלוֹת֙ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי גַּ֣ם אֶת־הַטּ֗וֹב נְקַבֵּל֙ מֵאֵ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאֶת־הָרָ֖ע לֹ֣א נְקַבֵּ֑ל בְּכָל־זֹ֛את לֹא־חָטָ֥א אִיּ֖וֹב בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו׃ פ

When Job's three friends heard about all this trouble that had come on him, they came, each from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite.[^9] They arranged to meet and come to show him sympathy[^10] and comfort him.

וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת ׀ רֵעֵ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב אֵ֣ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֮ הַבָּ֣אָה עָלָיו֒ וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֔וֹ אֱלִיפַ֤ז הַתֵּימָנִי֙ וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֔י וְצוֹפַ֖ר הַנַּֽעֲמָתִ֑י וַיִּוָּעֲד֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו לָב֥וֹא לָנֽוּד־ל֖וֹ וּֽלְנַחֲמֽוֹ׃
When they looked up from a distance, they did not recognize him. They wept aloud, and each one tore his robe, and they threw dust into the air over their heads.[^11]
וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֤ם מֵרָחוֹק֙ וְלֹ֣א הִכִּירֻ֔הוּ וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ וַֽיִּקְרְעוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מְעִל֔וֹ וַיִּזְרְק֥וּ עָפָ֛ר עַל־רָאשֵׁיהֶ֖ם הַשָּׁמָֽיְמָה׃
Then they sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.
וַיֵּשְׁב֤וּ אִתּוֹ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעַ֣ת לֵיל֑וֹת וְאֵין־דֹּבֵ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ דָּבָ֔ר כִּ֣י רָא֔וּ כִּֽי־גָדַ֥ל הַכְּאֵ֖ב מְאֹֽד׃

n.1: Literally "the sons of God": heavenly beings who serve in God's court (see 1:6). The Greek Septuagint reads "the angels of God".
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *ha-satan*, "the adversary, the accuser", with the article: a title rather than a name. Traditionally "Satan".
n.4: Literally "to swallow him up". *For no reason* is Hebrew *chinnam*, the word the Accuser used in 1:9, "for nothing".
n.5: A proverb whose exact sense is uncertain, perhaps "one skin for another": a person will give up anything to save his own skin.
n.6: Literally "if he will not bless you to your face". The Hebrew says "bless" in place of "curse" (see 1:5 and 1:11).
n.7: Literally "Bless God". The Hebrew says "bless" in place of "curse" (see 1:5).
n.8: Hebrew *nevalot*, "foolish women", in the sense of senseless and godless.
n.9: *Teman* was a region of Edom (Genesis 36:11, 34). *Shuah* was a son of Abraham and Keturah (Genesis 25:2). Where *Naamah* was is not known.
n.10: Literally "to shake the head for him", a gesture of grief and sympathy.
n.11: Literally "they threw dust on their heads toward the sky", a sign of mourning.

v: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed the day he was born.[^1]
אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן פָּתַ֤ח אִיּוֹב֙ אֶת־פִּ֔יהוּ וַיְקַלֵּ֖ל אֶת־יוֹמֽוֹ׃ פ
Job said:[^2]
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, 'A boy has been conceived!'
יֹ֣אבַד י֭וֹם אִוָּ֣לֶד בּ֑וֹ וְהַלַּ֥יְלָה אָ֝מַ֗ר הֹ֣רָה גָֽבֶר׃
That day, let it be darkness! Let God[^3] above not seek it out, and let no light shine on it.
הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֗וּא יְֽהִ֫י חֹ֥שֶׁךְ אַֽל־יִדְרְשֵׁ֣הוּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְאַל־תּוֹפַ֖ע עָלָ֣יו נְהָרָֽה׃
Let darkness and deep darkness[^4] claim it;[^5] let a cloud settle over it; let the blackness of the day[^6] terrify it.
יִגְאָלֻ֡הוּ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְ֭צַלְמָוֶת תִּשְׁכָּן־עָלָ֣יו עֲנָנָ֑ה יְ֝בַעֲתֻ֗הוּ כִּֽמְרִ֥ירֵי יֽוֹם׃
That night, let thick darkness seize it! Let it not rejoice[^7] among the days of the year; let it not come into the count of the months.
הַלַּ֥יְלָה הַהוּא֮ יִקָּחֵ֢ה֫וּ אֹ֥פֶל אַל־יִ֭חַדְּ בִּימֵ֣י שָׁנָ֑ה בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר יְ֝רָחִ֗ים אַל־יָבֹֽא׃
Yes, let that night be barren; let no shout of joy come into it.
הִנֵּ֤ה הַלַּ֣יְלָה הַ֭הוּא יְהִ֣י גַלְמ֑וּד אַל־תָּבֹ֖א רְנָנָ֣ה בֽוֹ׃
Let those who curse days curse it, those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.[^8]
יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ אֹרְרֵי־י֑וֹם הָ֝עֲתִידִ֗ים עֹרֵ֥ר לִוְיָתָֽן׃
Let the stars of its dawn[^9] be dark; let it wait for light that does not come, and let it not see the eyelids of the morning,[^10]
יֶחְשְׁכוּ֮ כּוֹכְבֵ֢י נִ֫שְׁפּ֥וֹ יְקַו־לְא֥וֹר וָאַ֑יִן וְאַל־יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה בְּעַפְעַפֵּי־שָֽׁחַר׃
because it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb[^11] and hide trouble from my eyes.
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א סָ֭גַר דַּלְתֵ֣י בִטְנִ֑י וַיַּסְתֵּ֥ר עָ֝מָ֗ל מֵעֵינָֽי׃
Why did I not die at birth,[^12] come out of the womb and breathe my last?
לָ֤מָּה לֹּ֣א מֵרֶ֣חֶם אָמ֑וּת מִבֶּ֖טֶן יָצָ֣אתִי וְאֶגְוָֽע׃
Why were there knees to receive me, or breasts for me to nurse?
מַ֭דּוּעַ קִדְּמ֣וּנִי בִרְכָּ֑יִם וּמַה־שָּׁ֝דַ֗יִם כִּ֣י אִינָֽק׃
For now I would be lying down in quiet; I would be asleep, and then I would be at rest
כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה שָׁכַ֣בְתִּי וְאֶשְׁק֑וֹט יָ֝שַׁ֗נְתִּי אָ֤ז ׀ יָנ֬וּחַֽ לִֽי׃
with kings and counselors of the earth, who rebuilt ruins for themselves,[^13]
עִם־מְ֭לָכִים וְיֹ֣עֲצֵי אָ֑רֶץ הַבֹּנִ֖ים חֳרָב֣וֹת לָֽמוֹ׃
or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
א֣וֹ עִם־שָׂ֭רִים זָהָ֣ב לָהֶ֑ם הַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים בָּתֵּיהֶ֣ם כָּֽסֶף׃
Or why was I not hidden away like a stillborn child,[^14] like infants who never see the light?
א֤וֹ כְנֵ֣פֶל טָ֭מוּן לֹ֣א אֶהְיֶ֑ה כְּ֝עֹלְלִ֗ים לֹא־רָ֥אוּ אֽוֹר׃
There the wicked stop their raging, and there the weary find rest.[^15]
שָׁ֣ם רְ֭שָׁעִים חָ֣דְלוּ רֹ֑גֶז וְשָׁ֥ם יָ֝נ֗וּחוּ יְגִ֣יעֵי כֹֽחַ׃
Prisoners are at ease together; they no longer hear the voice of the slave driver.
יַ֭חַד אֲסִירִ֣ים שַׁאֲנָ֑נוּ לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ ק֣וֹל נֹגֵֽשׂ׃
The small and the great are there alike, and the slave is free from his master.
קָטֹ֣ן וְ֭גָדוֹל שָׁ֣ם ה֑וּא וְ֝עֶ֗בֶד חָפְשִׁ֥י מֵאֲדֹנָֽיו׃
Why does he[^16] give light to the one who suffers, and life to the bitter in soul,
לָ֤מָּה יִתֵּ֣ן לְעָמֵ֣ל א֑וֹר וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃
who long for death, but it does not come, who dig for it more than for hidden treasure,
הַֽמְחַכִּ֣ים לַמָּ֣וֶת וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וַֽ֝יַּחְפְּרֻ֗הוּ מִמַּטְמוֹנִֽים׃
who would rejoice and shout for joy,[^17] who would be glad to find the grave?
הַשְּׂמֵחִ֥ים אֱלֵי־גִ֑יל יָ֝שִׂ֗ישׂוּ כִּ֣י יִמְצְאוּ־קָֽבֶר׃
Why give light to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?[^18]
לְ֭גֶבֶר אֲשֶׁר־דַּרְכּ֣וֹ נִסְתָּ֑רָה וַיָּ֖סֶךְ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בַּעֲדֽוֹ׃
For sighing comes to me in place of my food,[^19] and my groans pour out like water.
כִּֽי־לִפְנֵ֣י לַ֭חְמִי אַנְחָתִ֣י תָבֹ֑א וַֽיִּתְּכ֥וּ כַ֝מַּ֗יִם שַׁאֲגֹתָֽי׃
For what I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened to me.
כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד פָּ֭חַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵ֑נִי וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָ֝גֹ֗רְתִּי יָ֣בֹא לִֽי׃
I have no ease, I have no quiet, I have no rest, and turmoil has come."
לֹ֤א שָׁלַ֨וְתִּי ׀ וְלֹ֖א שָׁקַ֥טְתִּי וְֽלֹא־נָ֗חְתִּי וַיָּ֥בֹא רֹֽגֶז׃ פ

n.1: Literally "cursed his day". Here the Hebrew uses the ordinary word for "curse" (*qillel*).
n.2: Literally "Job answered and said", a common way of beginning a speech.
n.3: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 23.
n.4: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.5: Literally "redeem it", that is, take it back as their own. Hebrew *ga'al*. Some take the verb as a different *ga'al*, "defile it".
n.6: Hebrew *kimrire yom*, a phrase of uncertain meaning: perhaps "the darkenings of the day", such as an eclipse, or "the bitterness of the day".
n.7: The Hebrew vowel points read "let it not rejoice". The same consonants can be read "let it not be joined", which fits the parallel line.
n.8: A sea monster, a figure of chaos in the poetry of the ancient Near East (40:25 (41:1 in most English Bibles); Psalm 74:14; Isaiah 27:1). Those who "curse days" may be sorcerers thought able to bring disaster. Some interpreters read *yam*, "the Sea", for *yom*, "day", in the first line, as a parallel to Leviathan.
n.9: Hebrew *neshef*, "twilight", here the twilight before dawn.
n.10: The first rays of the sun, pictured as the opening eyelids of the dawn.
n.11: Literally "the doors of my belly".
n.12: Literally "from the womb".
n.13: Or "who built for themselves what are now ruins". Hebrew *choravot*, "ruins, desolate places". Some think of monuments or tombs built in desolate places.
n.14: Literally "Or like a hidden miscarriage I would not be".
n.15: Literally "those weary of strength".
n.16: God is meant, though the Hebrew does not name him.
n.17: Literally "who rejoice to rejoicing". Some scholars read *gal*, "a heap (of stones)", for *gil*, "rejoicing", with a small change to the Hebrew: "who would rejoice over a burial mound".
n.18: The verb echoes 1:10, where the Accuser says God has "put a hedge around" Job to protect him. Here the hedge hems him in.
n.19: Literally "before my bread": either "instead of my food" or "at my meals".

v: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"If someone ventures a word to you, will you lose patience? But who can hold back from speaking?
הֲנִסָּ֬ה דָבָ֣ר אֵלֶ֣יךָ תִּלְאֶ֑ה וַעְצֹ֥ר בְּ֝מִלִּ֗ין מִ֣י יוּכָֽל׃
Look, you have instructed many, and you have strengthened weak hands.
הִ֭נֵּה יִסַּ֣רְתָּ רַבִּ֑ים וְיָדַ֖יִם רָפ֣וֹת תְּחַזֵּֽק׃
Your words have kept the stumbling on their feet, and you have made firm the knees that gave way.
כּ֭וֹשֵׁל יְקִימ֣וּן מִלֶּ֑יךָ וּבִרְכַּ֖יִם כֹּרְע֣וֹת תְּאַמֵּֽץ׃
But now it has come to you, and you lose patience; it touches you, and you are dismayed.
כִּ֤י עַתָּ֨ה ׀ תָּב֣וֹא אֵלֶ֣יךָ וַתֵּ֑לֶא תִּגַּ֥ע עָ֝דֶ֗יךָ וַתִּבָּהֵֽל׃
Is not your fear of God[^1] your confidence, and the integrity of your ways your hope?
הֲלֹ֣א יִ֭רְאָתְךָ כִּסְלָתֶ֑ךָ תִּ֝קְוָתְךָ֗ וְתֹ֣ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ׃
Think now: who that was innocent ever perished? Where were the upright ever wiped out?
זְכָר־נָ֗א מִ֤י ה֣וּא נָקִ֣י אָבָ֑ד וְ֝אֵיפֹ֗ה יְשָׁרִ֥ים נִכְחָֽדוּ׃
As I have seen, those who plow wickedness and sow trouble reap it.
כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָ֭אִיתִי חֹ֣רְשֵׁי אָ֑וֶן וְזֹרְעֵ֖י עָמָ֣ל יִקְצְרֻֽהוּ׃
At the breath of God[^2] they perish; at the blast of his anger they come to an end.
מִנִּשְׁמַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ וּמֵר֖וּחַ אַפּ֣וֹ יִכְלֽוּ׃
The lion may roar, the fierce lion may growl, but the teeth of the young lions are broken.[^3]
שַׁאֲגַ֣ת אַ֭רְיֵה וְק֣וֹל שָׁ֑חַל וְשִׁנֵּ֖י כְפִירִ֣ים נִתָּֽעוּ׃
The lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
לַ֭יִשׁ אֹבֵ֣ד מִבְּלִי־טָ֑רֶף וּבְנֵ֥י לָ֝בִ֗יא יִתְפָּרָֽדוּ׃
Now a word came to me in secret;[^4] my ear caught a whisper of it,
וְ֭אֵלַי דָּבָ֣ר יְגֻנָּ֑ב וַתִּקַּ֥ח אָ֝זְנִ֗י שֵׁ֣מֶץ מֽ͏ֶנְהֽוּ׃
amid troubled thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people.
בִּ֭שְׂעִפִּים מֵחֶזְיֹנ֣וֹת לָ֑יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֥ל תַּ֝רְדֵּמָ֗ה עַל־אֲנָשִֽׁים׃
Dread came upon me, and trembling, and it made all my bones shake.
פַּ֣חַד קְ֭רָאַנִי וּרְעָדָ֑ה וְרֹ֖ב עַצְמוֹתַ֣י הִפְחִֽיד׃
A spirit[^5] passed before my face; the hair of my body stood on end.
וְ֭רוּחַ עַל־פָּנַ֣י יַחֲלֹ֑ף תְּ֝סַמֵּ֗ר שַֽׂעֲרַ֥ת בְּשָׂרִֽי׃
It stood still, but I could not make out its appearance. A form was before my eyes; there was silence, and I heard a voice:[^6]
יַעֲמֹ֤ד ׀ וְֽלֹא־אַכִּ֬יר מַרְאֵ֗הוּ תְּ֭מוּנָה לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י דְּמָמָ֖ה וָק֣וֹל אֶשְׁמָֽע׃
'Can a mortal be righteous before God? Can a man be pure before his Maker?[^7]
הַֽ֭אֱנוֹשׁ מֵאֱל֣וֹהַ יִצְדָּ֑ק אִ֥ם מֵ֝עֹשֵׂ֗הוּ יִטְהַר־גָּֽבֶר׃
If he puts no trust in his servants, and charges his angels with error,[^8]
הֵ֣ן בַּ֭עֲבָדָיו לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ין וּ֝בְמַלְאָכָ֗יו יָשִׂ֥ים תָּהֳלָֽה׃
how much more those who live in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed as easily as a moth![^9]
אַ֤ף ׀ שֹׁכְנֵ֬י בָֽתֵּי־חֹ֗מֶר אֲשֶׁר־בֶּעָפָ֥ר יְסוֹדָ֑ם יְ֝דַכְּא֗וּם לִפְנֵי־עָֽשׁ׃
Between morning and evening they are shattered; they perish forever, and no one notices.
מִבֹּ֣קֶר לָעֶ֣רֶב יֻכַּ֑תּוּ מִבְּלִ֥י מֵ֝שִׂ֗ים לָנֶ֥צַח יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃
Is not their tent cord pulled up within them?[^10] They die, and not in wisdom.'
הֲלֹא־נִסַּ֣ע יִתְרָ֣ם בָּ֑ם יָ֝מ֗וּתוּ וְלֹ֣א בְחָכְמָֽה׃

n.1: Literally "your fear".
n.2: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 17.
n.3: Literally "The roar of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions are broken". Verses 10–11 use five different Hebrew words for lions.
n.4: Literally "was stolen to me".
n.5: Or "a wind", "a breath". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.6: Or "I heard a silent voice", "a whisper of a voice" (compare 1 Kings 19:12).
n.7: Or "Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can a man be purer than his Maker?"
n.8: Hebrew *toholah*, a word found only here, perhaps "error" or "folly".
n.9: Literally "before a moth": perhaps "like a moth", or "sooner than a moth".
n.10: The life of a person is pictured as a tent that collapses when its cord is pulled up. Hebrew *yitram* may instead mean "their excellence": "Is not their excellence taken from them?" The words of the voice may end at verse 17 rather than here.

v: "Call out now! Is there anyone who will answer you? To which of the holy ones[^1] will you turn?
קְֽרָא־נָ֭א הֲיֵ֣שׁ עוֹנֶ֑ךָּ וְאֶל־מִ֖י מִקְּדֹשִׁ֣ים תִּפְנֶֽה׃
For resentment kills the fool, and jealousy slays the simple.
כִּֽי־לֶֽ֭אֱוִיל יַהֲרָג־כָּ֑עַשׂ וּ֝פֹתֶ֗ה תָּמִ֥ית קִנְאָֽה׃
I myself have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his home.[^2]
אֲ‍ֽנִי־רָ֭אִיתִי אֱוִ֣יל מַשְׁרִ֑ישׁ וָאֶקּ֖וֹב נָוֵ֣הוּ פִתְאֹֽם׃
His children are far from safety; they are crushed in the gate,[^3] with no one to rescue them.
יִרְחֲק֣וּ בָנָ֣יו מִיֶּ֑שַׁע וְיִֽדַּכְּא֥וּ בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּֽיל׃
The hungry eat his harvest and take it even from among the thorns, and the thirsty pant after their wealth.[^4]
אֲשֶׁ֤ר קְצִיר֨וֹ ׀ רָ֘עֵ֤ב יֹאכֵ֗ל וְאֶֽל־מִצִנִּ֥ים יִקָּחֵ֑הוּ וְשָׁאַ֖ף צַמִּ֣ים חֵילָֽם׃
For trouble does not come out of the dust, and misery does not sprout from the ground.
כִּ֤י ׀ לֹא־יֵצֵ֣א מֵעָפָ֣ר אָ֑וֶן וּ֝מֵאֲדָמָ֗ה לֹא־יִצְמַ֥ח עָמָֽל׃
Rather, human beings are born to misery, as surely as sparks fly upward.[^5]
כִּֽי־אָ֭דָם לְעָמָ֣ל יוּלָּ֑ד וּבְנֵי־רֶ֝֗שֶׁף יַגְבִּ֥יהוּ עֽוּף׃
But as for me, I would appeal to God, and to God I would commit my cause.[^6]
אוּלָ֗ם אֲ֭נִי אֶדְרֹ֣שׁ אֶל־אֵ֑ל וְאֶל־אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים אָשִׂ֥ים דִּבְרָתִֽי׃
He does great things beyond searching out, wonders beyond counting.
עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת וְאֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר נִ֝פְלָא֗וֹת עַד־אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃
He gives rain on the earth and sends water on the fields.
הַנֹּתֵ֣ן מָ֭טָר עַל־פְּנֵי־אָ֑רֶץ וְשֹׁ֥לֵֽחַ מַ֝יִם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י חוּצֽוֹת׃
He sets the lowly on high, and those who mourn are lifted to safety.
לָשׂ֣וּם שְׁפָלִ֣ים לְמָר֑וֹם וְ֝קֹדְרִ֗ים שָׂ֣גְבוּ יֶֽשַׁע׃
He frustrates the plans of the crafty, so that their hands achieve no success.[^7]
מֵ֭פֵר מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת עֲרוּמִ֑ים וְֽלֹא־תַעֲשֶׂ֥ינָה יְ֝דֵיהֶ֗ם תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃
He catches the wise in their own craftiness,[^8] and the schemes of the devious are swept away.
לֹכֵ֣ד חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעָרְמָ֑ם וַעֲצַ֖ת נִפְתָּלִ֣ים נִמְהָֽרָה׃
By day they run into darkness, and at noon they grope as if it were night.
יוֹמָ֥ם יְפַגְּשׁוּ־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וְ֝כַלַּ֗יְלָה יְֽמַשְׁשׁ֥וּ בַֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃
But he saves the needy from the sword of their mouth,[^9] and from the hand of the mighty.
וַיֹּ֣שַׁע מֵ֭חֶרֶב מִפִּיהֶ֑ם וּמִיַּ֖ד חָזָ֣ק אֶבְיֽוֹן׃
So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
וַתְּהִ֣י לַדַּ֣ל תִּקְוָ֑ה וְ֝עֹלָ֗תָה קָ֣פְצָה פִּֽיהָ׃
How happy is the one whom God[^10] corrects! So do not reject the discipline of the Almighty.[^11]
הִנֵּ֤ה אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֱ֭נוֹשׁ יוֹכִחֶ֣נּֽוּ אֱל֑וֹהַּ וּמוּסַ֥ר שַׁ֝דַּ֗י אַל־תִּמְאָֽס׃
For he wounds, but he binds up; he strikes, but his hands[^12] heal.
כִּ֤י ה֣וּא יַכְאִ֣יב וְיֶחְבָּ֑שׁ יִ֝מְחַ֗ץ *וידו **וְיָדָ֥יו תִּרְפֶּֽינָה׃
He will rescue you from six troubles, and in seven no harm will touch you.[^13]
בְּשֵׁ֣שׁ צָ֭רוֹת יַצִּילֶ֑ךָּ וּבְשֶׁ֓בַע ׀ לֹא־יִגַּ֖ע בְּךָ֣ רָֽע׃
In famine he will ransom you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
בְּ֭רָעָב פָּֽדְךָ֣ מִמָּ֑וֶת וּ֝בְמִלְחָמָ֗ה מִ֣ידֵי חָֽרֶב׃
You will be hidden from the lash of the tongue, and you will not fear destruction when it comes.
בְּשׁ֣וֹט לָ֭שׁוֹן תֵּחָבֵ֑א וְֽלֹא־תִירָ֥א מִ֝שֹּׁ֗ד כִּ֣י יָבֽוֹא׃
You will laugh at destruction and famine, and you will not fear the wild animals of the earth.
לְשֹׁ֣ד וּלְכָפָ֣ן תִּשְׂחָ֑ק וּֽמֵחַיַּ֥ת הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ אַל־תִּירָֽא׃
For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field,[^14] and the wild animals of the field will be at peace with you.
כִּ֤י עִם־אַבְנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה בְרִיתֶ֑ךָ וְחַיַּ֥ת הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה הָשְׁלְמָה־לָֽ[t]ךְ׃
You will know that your tent is secure; you will inspect your home[^15] and find nothing missing.[^16]
וְֽ֭יָדַעְתָּ כִּי־שָׁל֣וֹם אָהֳלֶ֑ךָ וּֽפָקַדְתָּ֥ נָ֝וְךָ וְלֹ֣א תֶחֱטָֽא׃
You will know that your descendants will be many, and your offspring like the grass of the earth.
וְֽ֭יָדַעְתָּ כִּי־רַ֣ב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְ֝צֶאֱצָאֶ֗יךָ כְּעֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
You will come to the grave in ripe old age,[^17] as sheaves of grain are brought up in their season.
תָּב֣וֹא בְכֶ֣לַח אֱלֵי־קָ֑בֶר כַּעֲל֖וֹת גָּדִ֣ישׁ בְּעִתּֽוֹ׃
Look, we have searched this out; it is true. Hear it, and know it for yourself."
הִנֵּה־זֹ֭את חֲקַרְנ֥וּהָ כֶּֽן־הִ֑יא שְׁ֝מָעֶ֗נָּה וְאַתָּ֥ה דַֽע־לָֽךְ׃ פ

n.1: Heavenly beings (compare 15:15; Psalm 89:6–8 (89:5–7 in most English Bibles)).
n.2: Or "I declared his home cursed". The Hebrew word for "home" can also mean "pasture".
n.3: The city gate, where legal cases were heard.
n.4: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. The middle line is literally "and to (or from) thorns he takes it". *The thirsty* reads Hebrew *tsammim* as a short spelling of *tsme'im*. Elsewhere *tsammim* means "snare" (18:9): "and a snare gapes for their wealth".
n.5: Literally "and the sons of Resheph fly high". *Resheph* means "flame", and was also the name of a Canaanite god of plague. Or "as birds fly high". With a slight change of vowels, the first line can be read "human beings give birth to misery".
n.6: The first line has *El*, the second *Elohim*, both "God".
n.7: Hebrew *tushiyyah*, "success" or "sound wisdom".
n.8: 1 Corinthians 3:19 quotes this line.
n.9: Literally "from the sword, from their mouth". Their words are pictured as a sword.
n.10: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.11: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "his hand" but read "his hands".
n.13: A numerical saying: "six, and even seven" means every one of them.
n.14: That is, stones will not spoil your fields.
n.15: Or "your pasture", "your fold".
n.16: Literally "and not miss", a verb that usually means "sin".
n.17: Hebrew *kelach*, a rare word, perhaps "full vigor" or "ripe old age".

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"If only my anguish could be weighed, and my calamity laid on the scales with it!
ל֗וּ שָׁק֣וֹל יִשָּׁקֵ֣ל כַּעְשִׂ֑י *והיתי **וְ֝הַוָּתִ֗י בְּֽמֹאזְנַ֥יִם יִשְׂאוּ־יָֽחַד׃
For then it would be heavier than the sand of the seas. That is why my words have been wild.[^1]
כִּֽי־עַתָּ֗ה מֵח֣וֹל יַמִּ֣ים יִכְבָּ֑ד עַל־כֵּ֝֗ן דְּבָרַ֥י לָֽעוּ׃
For the arrows of the Almighty[^2] are in me; my spirit drinks their poison. The terrors of God[^3] are lined up against me.
כִּ֤י חִצֵּ֪י שַׁדַּ֡י עִמָּדִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲ֭מָתָם שֹׁתָ֣ה רוּחִ֑י בִּעוּתֵ֖י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַֽעַרְכֽוּנִי׃
Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass, or an ox bellow over its fodder?
הֲיִֽנְהַק־פֶּ֥רֶא עֲלֵי־דֶ֑שֶׁא אִ֥ם יִגְעֶה־שּׁ֝֗וֹר עַל־בְּלִילֽוֹ׃
Can tasteless food be eaten without salt? Is there any flavor in the white of an egg?[^4]
הֲיֵאָכֵ֣ל תָּ֭פֵל מִבְּלִי־מֶ֑לַח אִם־יֶשׁ־טַ֝֗עַם בְּרִ֣יר חַלָּמֽוּת׃
I refuse to touch them; they are like loathsome food to me.[^5]
מֵאֲנָ֣ה לִנְגּ֣וֹעַ נַפְשִׁ֑י הֵ֝֗מָּה כִּדְוֵ֥י לַחְמִֽי׃
If only my request would be granted, and God would give me what I hope for:
מִֽי־יִ֭תֵּן תָּב֣וֹא שֶֽׁאֱלָתִ֑י וְ֝תִקְוָתִ֗י יִתֵּ֥ן אֱלֽוֹהַּ׃
that God would be willing to crush me, that he would let loose his hand and cut me off!
וְיֹאֵ֣ל אֱ֭לוֹהַּ וִֽידַכְּאֵ֑נִי יַתֵּ֥ר יָ֝ד֗וֹ וִֽיבַצְּעֵֽנִי׃
Then I would still have this comfort, and I would leap for joy[^6] in pain that does not spare me: that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
וּֽ[m]תְהִי ע֨וֹד ׀ נֶ֘חָ֤מָתִ֗י וַאֲסַלְּדָ֣ה בְ֭חִילָה לֹ֣א יַחְמ֑וֹל כִּי־לֹ֥א כִ֝חַ֗דְתִּי אִמְרֵ֥י קָדֽוֹשׁ׃
What strength do I have, that I should wait? What end is ahead of me, that I should be patient?[^7]
מַה־כֹּחִ֥י כִֽי־אֲיַחֵ֑ל וּמַה־קִּ֝צִּ֗י כִּֽי־אַאֲרִ֥יךְ נַפְשִֽׁי׃
Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh bronze?
אִם־כֹּ֣חַ אֲבָנִ֣ים כֹּחִ֑י אִֽם־בְּשָׂרִ֥י נָחֽוּשׁ׃
Is it not that I have no help in myself, and any resource[^8] has been driven from me?
הַאִ֬ם אֵ֣ין עֶזְרָתִ֣י בִ֑י וְ֝תֻשִׁיָּ֗ה נִדְּחָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
One who is wasting away should have faithful love[^9] from his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.[^10]
לַמָּ֣ס מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ חָ֑סֶד וְיִרְאַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲזֽוֹב׃
My brothers have been as treacherous as a wadi,[^11] like the channels of wadis that run away,
אַ֭חַי בָּגְד֣וּ כְמוֹ־נָ֑חַל כַּאֲפִ֖יק נְחָלִ֣ים יַעֲבֹֽרוּ׃
which are dark with ice, where the snow piles up and hides itself,
הַקֹּדְרִ֥ים מִנִּי־קָ֑רַח עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ יִתְעַלֶּם־שָֽׁלֶג׃
but when they are scorched[^12] they cease; when it is hot, they vanish from their place.
בְּ֭עֵת יְזֹרְב֣וּ נִצְמָ֑תוּ בְּ֝חֻמּ֗וֹ נִדְעֲכ֥וּ מִמְּקוֹמָֽם׃
Caravans turn aside from their route;[^13] they go up into the wasteland and perish.
יִ֭לָּ֣פְתוּ אָרְח֣וֹת דַּרְכָּ֑ם יַעֲל֖וּ בַתֹּ֣הוּ וְיֹאבֵֽדוּ׃
The caravans of Tema look for water; the travelers of Sheba hope for it.[^14]
הִ֭בִּיטוּ אָרְח֣וֹת תֵּמָ֑א הֲלִיכֹ֥ת שְׁ֝בָ֗א קִוּוּ־לָֽמוֹ׃
They are put to shame because they trusted; they arrive there and are dismayed.
בֹּ֥שׁוּ כִּֽי־בָטָ֑ח בָּ֥אוּ עָ֝דֶ֗יהָ וַיֶּחְפָּֽרוּ׃
For now you have become like that;[^15] you see something terrible and are afraid.
כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה הֱיִ֣יתֶם *לא **ל֑וֹ תִּֽרְא֥וּ חֲ֝תַ֗ת וַתִּירָֽאוּ׃
Have I said, 'Give me something,' or 'Pay a bribe for me from your wealth,'
הֲ‍ֽכִי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי הָ֣בוּ לִ֑י וּ֝מִכֹּחֲכֶ֗ם שִׁחֲד֥וּ בַעֲדִֽי׃
or 'Rescue me from the hand of the enemy,' or 'Ransom me from the hand of the ruthless'?
וּמַלְּט֥וּנִי מִיַּד־צָ֑ר וּמִיַּ֖ד עָרִיצִ֣ים תִּפְדּֽוּנִי׃
Teach me, and I will be silent; make me understand where I have gone wrong.
ה֭וֹרוּנִי וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲרִ֑ישׁ וּמַה־שָּׁ֝גִ֗יתִי הָבִ֥ינוּ לִֽי׃
How painful are honest words![^16] But what does your arguing prove?[^17]
מַה־נִּמְרְצ֥וּ אִמְרֵי־יֹ֑שֶׁר וּמַה־יּוֹכִ֖יחַ הוֹכֵ֣חַ מִכֶּֽם׃
Do you mean to correct my words, and treat the words of a desperate man as wind?
הַלְהוֹכַ֣ח מִלִּ֣ים תַּחְשֹׁ֑בוּ וּ֝לְר֗וּחַ אִמְרֵ֥י נֹאָֽשׁ׃
You would even cast lots over an orphan,[^18] and bargain over your friend.
אַף־עַל־יָת֥וֹם תַּפִּ֑ילוּ וְ֝תִכְר֗וּ עַל־רֵֽיעֲכֶ֥[c]ם׃
But now, please, look at me. Would I lie to your face?
וְ֭עַתָּה הוֹאִ֣ילוּ פְנוּ־בִ֑י וְעַל־פְּ֝נֵיכֶ֗ם אִם־אֲכַזֵּֽב׃
Turn back, please; let there be no injustice. Turn back again; my righteousness is still at stake.[^19]
שֻֽׁבוּ־נָ֭א אַל־תְּהִ֣י עַוְלָ֑ה *ושבי **וְשֽׁ[m]**וּבוּ ע֝וֹד צִדְקִי־בָֽהּ׃
Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not taste what is ruinous?[^20]
הֲיֵשׁ־בִּלְשׁוֹנִ֥י עַוְלָ֑ה אִם־חִ֝כִּ֗י לֹא־יָבִ֥ין הַוּֽוֹת׃

n.1: Hebrew *la'u*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "wild", "rash" or "stammering".
n.2: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verse 14.
n.3: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verses 8 and 9.
n.4: Hebrew *rir challamut*, a phrase of uncertain meaning: perhaps "the white of an egg" or "the slime of the mallow plant".
n.5: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "They are like the sickness of my bread".
n.6: Hebrew *salad*, a verb found only here. Its meaning is uncertain: perhaps "leap for joy", or "recoil", "shudder".
n.7: Literally "that I should lengthen my soul".
n.8: Hebrew *tushiyyah*, "success, sound wisdom", as in 5:12.
n.9: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.10: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Literally "To the one melting from his friend faithful love, and the fear of the Almighty he forsakes". Or "One who withholds faithful love from his friend forsakes the fear of the Almighty".
n.11: A stream bed that runs with water in the rainy season and is dry in summer.
n.12: Hebrew *zarav*, a verb found only here, perhaps "dry up", "flow away" or "be scorched".
n.13: Or "The paths of their course twist and turn", of the streams themselves.
n.14: *Tema* and *Sheba* were trading peoples of Arabia.
n.15: The Hebrew text is written "you have become nothing" (*lo*, "not") but read "you have become (like) it" (*lo*, "to it"), that is, like the dry wadi. The meaning of the read form is uncertain.
n.16: Or "How forceful are honest words!"
n.17: Literally "What does reproving from you reprove?"
n.18: Literally "cause to fall over an orphan", probably lots for a child sold for debt.
n.19: Literally "my righteousness is still in it".
n.20: Hebrew *havvot*, "calamities, ruin", the word translated "calamity" in verse 2.

v: "Does not a human being have hard service[^1] on earth? Are not his days like the days of a hired worker?
הֲלֹא־צָבָ֣א לֶאֱנ֣וֹשׁ *על־**עֲלֵי־אָ֑רֶץ וְכִימֵ֖֗[c]י שָׂכִ֣יר יָמָֽיו׃
Like a slave who longs for the shade, like a hired worker who waits for his wages,
כְּעֶ֥בֶד יִשְׁאַף־צֵ֑ל וּ֝כְשָׂכִ֗יר יְקַוֶּ֥ה פָעֳלֽוֹ׃
so I have been given months of futility[^2] as my portion, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.
כֵּ֤ן הָנְחַ֣לְתִּי לִ֭י יַרְחֵי־שָׁ֑וְא וְלֵיל֥וֹת עָ֝מָ֗ל מִנּוּ־לִֽי׃
When I lie down I say, 'When will I get up?' But the night drags on,[^3] and I toss and turn until dawn.
אִם־שָׁכַ֗בְתִּי וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מָתַ֣י אָ֭קוּם וּמִדַּד־עָ֑רֶב וְשָׂבַ֖עְתִּי נְדֻדִ֣ים עֲדֵי־נָֽשֶׁף׃
My flesh is clothed with worms and crusts of dirt; my skin hardens, then breaks open again.[^4]
לָ֘בַ֤שׁ בְּשָׂרִ֣י רִ֭מָּה *וגיש **וְג֣וּשׁ עָפָ֑ר עוֹרִ֥י רָ֝גַ֗ע וַיִּמָּאֵֽס׃
My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.[^5]
יָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־אָ֑רֶג וַ֝יִּכְל֗וּ בְּאֶ֣פֶס תִּקְוָֽה׃
Remember that my life is a breath; my eye will never again see good.
זְ֭כֹר כִּי־ר֣וּחַ חַיָּ֑י לֹא־תָשׁ֥וּב עֵ֝ינִ֗י לִרְא֥וֹת טֽוֹב׃
The eye that sees me will see me no more; your eyes will be on me, but I will be gone.
לֹֽא־תְ֭שׁוּרֵנִי עֵ֣ין רֹ֑אִי עֵינֶ֖יךָ בִּ֣י וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃
As a cloud fades away and is gone, so one who goes down to Sheol[^6] does not come up.
כָּלָ֣ה עָ֭נָן וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ כֵּ֥ן יוֹרֵ֥ד שְׁ֝א֗וֹל לֹ֣א יַעֲלֽ͏ֶה׃
He will not return to his house again, and his place will not know him anymore.
לֹא־יָשׁ֣וּב ע֣וֹד לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹא־יַכִּירֶ֖נּוּ ע֣וֹד מְקֹמֽוֹ׃
So I will not restrain my mouth. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
גַּם־אֲנִי֮ לֹ֤א אֶחֱשָׂ֫ךְ פִּ֥י אֲ‍ֽ֭דַבְּרָה בְּצַ֣ר רוּחִ֑י אָ֝שִׂ֗יחָה בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃
Am I the sea, or the sea monster,[^7] that you set a guard over me?
הֲ‍ֽיָם־אָ֭נִי אִם־תַּנִּ֑ין כִּֽי־תָשִׂ֖ים עָלַ֣י מִשְׁמָֽר׃
When I say, 'My bed will comfort me, my couch will ease my complaint,'
כִּֽי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי תְּנַחֲמֵ֣נִי עַרְשִׂ֑י יִשָּׂ֥א בְ֝שִׂיחִ֗י מִשְׁכָּבִֽי׃
then you terrify me with dreams and frighten me with visions,
וְחִתַּתַּ֥נִי בַחֲלֹמ֑וֹת וּֽמֵחֶזְיֹנ֥וֹת תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃
so that I would choose strangling, death rather than these bones of mine.[^8]
וַתִּבְחַ֣ר מַחֲנָ֣ק נַפְשִׁ֑י מָ֝֗וֶת מֵֽעַצְמוֹתָֽי׃
I have had enough;[^9] I will not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are a breath.
מָ֭אַסְתִּי לֹא־לְעֹלָ֣ם אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה חֲדַ֥ל מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי כִּי־הֶ֥בֶל יָמָֽי׃
What is a human being, that you make so much of him, that you pay attention to him,[^10]
מָֽה־אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי־תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ׃
that you examine him every morning and test him every moment?
וַתִּפְקְדֶ֥נּוּ לִבְקָרִ֑ים לִ֝רְגָעִ֗ים תִּבְחָנֶֽנּוּ׃
How long will you not look away from me, or leave me alone long enough to swallow my spit?
כַּ֭מָּה לֹא־תִשְׁעֶ֣ה מִמֶּ֑נִּי לֹֽא־תַ֝רְפֵּ֗נִי עַד־בִּלְעִ֥י רֻקִּֽי׃
If I have sinned, what have I done to you, you watcher of humankind? Why have you made me your target? Why have I become a burden to myself?[^11]
חָטָ֡אתִי מָ֤ה אֶפְעַ֨ל ׀ לָךְ֮ נֹצֵ֢ר הָאָ֫דָ֥ם לָ֤מָה שַׂמְתַּ֣נִי לְמִפְגָּ֣ע לָ֑ךְ וָאֶהְיֶ֖ה עָלַ֣י לְמַשָּֽׂא׃
Why do you not pardon my offense and take away my guilt? For now I will lie down in the dust; you will search for me, but I will be gone."
וּמֶ֤ה ׀ לֹא־תִשָּׂ֣א פִשְׁעִי֮ וְתַעֲבִ֢יר אֶת־עֲוֺ֫נִ֥י כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה לֶעָפָ֣ר אֶשְׁכָּ֑ב וְשִׁ֖חֲרְתַּ֣נִי וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *tsava*, military service or forced labor.
n.2: Or "emptiness", "worthlessness".
n.3: The Hebrew of this phrase is uncertain. Literally "and the measuring of evening".
n.4: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Or "my skin cracks and oozes".
n.5: The word for "hope" (*tiqvah*) can also mean "thread", continuing the picture of the weaver.
n.6: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.7: Hebrew *yam*, "sea", and *tannin*, "sea monster": powers of chaos that God holds in check (Psalm 74:13; Isaiah 51:9).
n.8: Literally "rather than my bones". Or "rather than my pains".
n.9: Literally "I refuse" or "I reject", with no object stated: perhaps "I loathe my life".
n.10: Literally "set your heart on him". Compare Psalm 8:5 (8:4 in most English Bibles), which asks this question in praise.
n.11: An ancient Jewish scribal tradition counts this among places where the scribes changed the text out of reverence for God, from "a burden to you". The Greek Septuagint reads "a burden to you".

v: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י וַיֹאמַֽר׃
"How long will you say such things? The words of your mouth are a mighty wind.
עַד־אָ֥ן תְּמַלֶּל־אֵ֑לֶּה וְר֥וּחַ כַּ֝בִּיר אִמְרֵי־פִֽיךָ׃
Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty[^1] pervert what is right?
הַ֭אֵל יְעַוֵּ֣ת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְאִם־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יְעַוֵּֽת־צֶֽדֶק׃
If your children sinned against him, he handed them over to the power of their offense.[^2]
אִם־בָּנֶ֥יךָ חָֽטְאוּ־ל֑וֹ וַֽ֝יְשַׁלְּחֵ֗ם בְּיַד־פִּשְׁעָֽם׃
But if you will seek God earnestly and plead with the Almighty,
אִם־אַ֭תָּה תְּשַׁחֵ֣ר אֶל־אֵ֑ל וְאֶל־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י תִּתְחַנָּֽן׃
if you are pure and upright, then surely he will rouse himself for you and restore your rightful home.[^3]
אִם־זַ֥ךְ וְיָשָׁ֗ר אָ֥תָּה כִּי־עַ֭תָּה יָעִ֣יר עָלֶ֑יךָ וְ֝שִׁלַּ֗ם נְוַ֣ת צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
Though your beginning was small, your future will be very great.
וְהָיָ֣ה רֵאשִׁיתְךָ֣ מִצְעָ֑ר וְּ֝אַחֲרִיתְךָ֗ יִשְׂגֶּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
Ask the former generation, please, and pay attention to what their ancestors searched out.
כִּֽי־שְׁאַל־נָ֭א לְדֹ֣ר רִישׁ֑וֹן וְ֝כוֹנֵ֗ן לְחֵ֣קֶר אֲבוֹתָֽם׃
For we are only of yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are a shadow.
כִּֽי־תְמ֣וֹל אֲ֭נַחְנוּ וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע כִּ֤י צֵ֖ל יָמֵ֣ינוּ עֲלֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
Will they not teach you and tell you, and bring out words from their understanding?[^4]
הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם י֭וֹרוּךָ יֹ֣אמְרוּ לָ֑ךְ וּ֝מִלִּבָּ֗ם יוֹצִ֥אוּ מִלִּֽים׃
Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh? Can reeds flourish without water?
הֲיִֽגְאֶה־גֹּ֭מֶא בְּלֹ֣א בִצָּ֑ה יִשְׂגֶּה־אָ֥חוּ בְלִי־מָֽיִם׃
While it is still green and not yet cut, it withers before any other plant.
עֹדֶ֣נּוּ בְ֭אִבּוֹ לֹ֣א יִקָּטֵ֑ף וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָל־חָצִ֣יר יִיבָֽשׁ׃
Such are the paths of all who forget God; the hope of the godless will perish.
כֵּ֗ן אָ֭רְחוֹת כָּל־שֹׁ֣כְחֵי אֵ֑ל וְתִקְוַ֖ת חָנֵ֣ף תֹּאבֵֽד׃
His confidence snaps,[^5] and what he trusts in is a spider's web.[^6]
אֲשֶׁר־יָק֥וֹט כִּסְל֑וֹ וּבֵ֥ית עַ֝כָּב[t]ִישׁ מִבְטַחֽוֹ׃
He leans on his house, but it does not stand; he holds on to it, but it does not last.
יִשָּׁעֵ֣ן עַל־בֵּ֭יתוֹ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֑ד יַחֲזִ֥יק בּ֝֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א יָקֽוּם׃
He is like a well-watered plant in the sun, whose shoots spread out over its garden.[^7]
רָטֹ֣ב ה֭וּא לִפְנֵי־שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְעַ֥ל גַּ֝נָּת֗וֹ יֹ֭נַקְתּ֥וֹ תֵצֵֽא׃
Its roots wrap around a heap of stones; it looks for a place among the stones.[^8]
עַל־גַּ֭ל שָֽׁרָשָׁ֣יו יְסֻבָּ֑כוּ בֵּ֖ית אֲבָנִ֣ים יֶחֱזֶֽה׃
But if he is torn from his place, then it will deny him: 'I never saw you.'
אִם־יְבַלְּעֶ֥נּוּ מִמְּקוֹמ֑וֹ וְכִ֥חֶשׁ בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א רְאִיתִֽיךָ׃
See, this is the joy of his way,[^9] and out of the dust others will spring up.
הֶן־ה֭וּא מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּ֝מֵעָפָ֗ר אַחֵ֥ר יִצְמָֽחוּ׃
See, God will not reject a blameless person, or take hold of the hand of evildoers.
הֶן־אֵ֭ל לֹ֣א יִמְאַס־תָּ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יַ֝חֲזִ֗יק בְּיַד־מְרֵעִֽים׃
He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with shouts of joy.
עַד־יְמַלֵּ֣ה שְׂח֣וֹק פִּ֑יךָ וּשְׂפָתֶ֥יךָ תְרוּעָֽה׃
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more."
שֹׂנְאֶ֥יךָ יִלְבְּשׁוּ־בֹ֑שֶׁת וְאֹ֖הֶל רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verse 5.
n.2: Literally "he sent them into the hand of their offense".
n.3: Literally "the home of your righteousness".
n.4: Literally "from their heart".
n.5: Hebrew *yaqot*, a word of uncertain meaning. Perhaps "is cut off", or a noun, "is a gossamer thread".
n.6: Literally "a spider's house".
n.7: Verses 16–19 may describe the wicked person (verse 13) as a plant that flourishes for a while, or they may describe a different plant that survives.
n.8: Literally "it sees a house of stones". The meaning of this line is uncertain.
n.9: Probably ironic: "So much for the joy of his way".

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Truly, I know that it is so. But how can a mortal be in the right with God?
אָ֭מְנָם יָדַ֣עְתִּי כִי־כֵ֑ן וּמַה־יִּצְדַּ֖ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם־אֵֽל׃
If he wanted to argue his case with him, he could not answer him once in a thousand times.[^1]
אִם־יַ֭חְפֹּץ לָרִ֣יב עִמּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יַ֝עֲנֶ֗נּוּ אַחַ֥ת מִנִּי־אָֽלֶף׃
He is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has ever defied him and come out unharmed?
חֲכַ֣ם לֵ֭בָב וְאַמִּ֣יץ כֹּ֑חַ מִֽי־הִקְשָׁ֥ה אֵ֝לָ֗יו וַיִּשְׁלָֽם׃
He moves mountains, and they do not know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
הַמַּעְתִּ֣יק הָ֭רִים וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑עוּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר הֲפָכָ֣ם בְּאַפּֽוֹ׃
He shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble.
הַמַּרְגִּ֣יז אֶ֭רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ וְ֝עַמּוּדֶ֗יהָ יִתְפַלָּצֽוּן׃
He speaks to the sun,[^2] and it does not rise; he seals up the stars.
הָאֹמֵ֣ר לַ֭חֶרֶס וְלֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ח וּבְעַ֖ד כּוֹכָבִ֣ים יַחְתֹּֽם׃
He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.[^3]
נֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַ֣יִם לְבַדּ֑וֹ וְ֝דוֹרֵ֗ךְ עַל־בָּ֥מֳתֵי יָֽם׃
He made the Bear, Orion and the Pleiades,[^4] and the chambers of the south.[^5]
עֹֽשֶׂה־עָ֭שׁ כְּסִ֥יל וְכִימָ֗ה וְחַדְרֵ֥י תֵמָֽן׃
He does great things beyond searching out, wonders beyond counting.[^6]
עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת עַד־אֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר וְ֝[t]נִפְלָא֗וֹת עַד־אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃
Look, he passes by me, and I do not see him; he moves on, and I do not perceive him.
הֵ֤ן יַעֲבֹ֣ר עָ֭לַי וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶ֑ה וְ֝יַחֲלֹ֗ף וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃
Look, he snatches away; who can stop him? Who can say to him, 'What are you doing?'
הֵ֣ן יַ֭חְתֹּף מִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ מִֽי־יֹאמַ֥ר אֵ֝לָ֗יו מַֽה־תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃
God[^7] does not hold back his anger; the helpers of Rahab[^8] bowed down beneath him.
אֱ֭לוֹהַּ לֹא־יָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ *תחתו **תַּחְתָּ֥יו שָׁ֝חֲח֗וּ עֹ֣זְרֵי רָֽהַב׃
How then could I answer him, or choose my words to argue with him?
אַ֭ף כִּֽי־אָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ אֶבְחֲרָ֖ה דְבָרַ֣י עִמּ[t]וֹ׃
Even if I were in the right, I could not answer him; I would have to plead for mercy with my judge.[^9]
אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־צָ֭דַקְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶעֱנֶ֑ה לִ֝מְשֹׁפְטִ֗י אֶתְחַנָּֽן׃
If I called and he answered me, I would not believe that he was listening to my voice.
אִם־קָרָ֥אתִי וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑נִי לֹֽא־אַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּֽי־יַאֲזִ֥ין קוֹלִֽי׃
For he crushes me with a storm[^10] and multiplies my wounds for no reason.[^11]
אֲשֶׁר־בִּשְׂעָרָ֥ה יְשׁוּפֵ֑נִי וְהִרְבָּ֖ה פְצָעַ֣י חִנָּֽם׃
He will not let me catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
לֹֽא־יִ֭תְּנֵנִי הָשֵׁ֣ב רוּחִ֑י כִּ֥י יַ֝שְׂבִּעַ֗נִי מַמְּרֹרִֽים׃
If it is a matter of strength, look, he is mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon him?[^12]
אִם־לְכֹ֣חַ אַמִּ֣יץ הִנֵּ֑ה וְאִם־לְ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט מִ֣י יוֹעִידֵֽנִי׃
Even if I were in the right, my own mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me crooked.[^13]
אִם־אֶ֭צְדָּק פִּ֣י יַרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי תָּֽם־אָ֝֗נִי וַֽיַּעְקְשֵֽׁנִי׃
I am blameless. I do not care about myself;[^14] I loathe my life.
תָּֽם־אָ֭נִי לֹֽא־אֵדַ֥ע נַפְשִׁ֗י אֶמְאַ֥ס חַיָּֽי׃
It is all one; that is why I say, 'He destroys the blameless and the wicked alike.'
אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל־כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֑רְתִּי תָּ֥ם וְ֝רָשָׁ֗ע ה֣וּא מְכַלֶּֽה׃
When a scourge brings sudden death, he mocks at the despair[^15] of the innocent.
אִם־שׁ֭וֹט יָמִ֣ית פִּתְאֹ֑ם לְמַסַּ֖ת נְקִיִּ֣ם יִלְעָֽג׃
The earth is handed over to the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges. If it is not he, then who is it?
אֶ֤רֶץ ׀ נִתְּנָ֬ה בְֽיַד־רָשָׁ֗ע פְּנֵֽי־שֹׁפְטֶ֥יהָ יְכַסֶּ֑ה אִם־לֹ֖א אֵפ֣וֹא מִי־הֽוּא׃
My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away without seeing any good.
וְיָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־רָ֑ץ בָּֽ֝רְח֗וּ לֹא־רָא֥וּ טוֹבָֽה׃
They glide by like boats of reed,[^16] like an eagle swooping on its prey.
חָ֭לְפוּ עִם־אֳנִיּ֣וֹת אֵבֶ֑ה כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר יָט֥וּשׂ עֲלֵי־אֹֽכֶל׃
If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will change my expression[^17] and be cheerful,'
אִם־אָ֭מְרִי אֶשְׁכְּחָ֣ה שִׂיחִ֑י אֶעֶזְבָ֖ה פָנַ֣י וְאַבְלִֽיגָה׃
I still dread all my sufferings, for I know you will not hold me innocent.
יָגֹ֥רְתִּי כָל־עַצְּבֹתָ֑י יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־לֹ֥א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃
I will be counted guilty anyway. Why then should I struggle in vain?[^18]
אָנֹכִ֥י אֶרְשָׁ֑ע לָמָּה־זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל אִיגָֽע׃
If I washed myself with snow water[^19] and cleansed my hands with lye,
אִם־הִתְרָחַ֥צְתִּי *במו־**בְמֵי־שָׁ֑לֶג וַ֝הֲזִכּ֗וֹתִי בְּבֹ֣ר כַּפָּי[t]׃
even then you would plunge me into a pit, and my own clothes would detest me.
אָ֭ז בַּשַּׁ֣חַת תִּטְבְּלֵ֑נִי וְ֝תִֽעֲב֗וּנִי שַׂלְמוֹתָֽי׃
For he is not a man like me, that I could answer him, that we could go to court together.
כִּי־לֹא־אִ֣ישׁ כָּמֹ֣נִי אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ נָב֥וֹא יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
There is no arbiter[^20] between us, who might lay his hand on us both.
לֹ֣א יֵשׁ־בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ מוֹכִ֑יחַ יָשֵׁ֖ת יָד֣וֹ עַל־שְׁנֵֽינוּ׃
Let him take his rod away from me, and let not dread of him terrify me.
יָסֵ֣ר מֵעָלַ֣י שִׁבְט֑וֹ וְ֝אֵמָת֗וֹ אַֽל־תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃
Then I would speak without fear of him, for I am not like that in myself.[^21]
אַֽ֭דַבְּרָה וְלֹ֣א אִירָאֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־כֵ֥ן אָ֝נֹכִ֗י עִמָּדִֽי׃

n.1: Or "God would not answer him once in a thousand times". The Hebrew does not make clear who would not answer whom.
n.2: Hebrew *cheres*, a rare word for the sun.
n.3: Literally "on the backs (or heights) of the sea". The Sea (*Yam*) may be pictured as a monster that God tramples.
n.4: Hebrew *Ash*, *Kesil* and *Kimah*, constellations that cannot be identified with certainty. *Kesil* means "fool" and *Kimah* "cluster". Also in 38:31–32.
n.5: Perhaps the constellations of the southern sky.
n.6: Job repeats Eliphaz's words in 5:9.
n.7: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.8: A sea monster, a figure of chaos (26:12; Psalm 89:11 (89:10 in most English Bibles); Isaiah 51:9). This is a different Hebrew word from the name of Rahab in Joshua 2.
n.9: Or "my opponent at law". Hebrew *meshofti*.
n.10: Or "for a trifle", literally "for a hair". The Hebrew word can be read either way.
n.11: Hebrew *chinnam*, the word in 1:9 and 2:3.
n.12: Literally "who will summon me?", as if Job were quoting God.
n.13: Or "he would declare me crooked".
n.14: Literally "I do not know my soul".
n.15: Hebrew *massat*, a word of uncertain meaning: perhaps "despair", or "trial".
n.16: Hebrew *eveh*, probably papyrus. Light papyrus boats were fast on the Nile.
n.17: Literally "abandon my face".
n.18: Literally "with a breath": uselessly. Hebrew *hevel*.
n.19: The Hebrew text is written "with snow" but read "with snow water".
n.20: Hebrew *mokhiach*, one who decides between two parties in a dispute. The Greek Septuagint reads "If only there were a mediator between us", reading *lu*, "if only", for *lo*, "not".
n.21: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "for not so am I with myself": perhaps "for I know I am not guilty", or "but as things are, I cannot".

v: "I am sick of my life. I will give free rein to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
נָֽקְטָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֗י בְּחַ֫יָּ֥י אֶֽעֶזְבָ֣ה עָלַ֣י שִׂיחִ֑י אֲ֝דַבְּרָה֗ בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃
I will say to God:[^1] Do not condemn me; let me know why you contend with me.
אֹמַ֣ר אֶל־אֱ֭לוֹהַּ אַל־תַּרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי הֽ֝וֹדִיעֵ֗נִי עַ֣ל מַה־תְּרִיבֵֽנִי׃
Does it seem good to you to oppress, to reject the work of your hands and smile on the plans of the wicked?[^2]
הֲט֤וֹב לְךָ֨ ׀ כִּֽי־תַעֲשֹׁ֗ק כִּֽי־תִ֭מְאַס יְגִ֣יעַ כַּפֶּ֑יךָ וְעַל־עֲצַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים הוֹפָֽעְתָּ׃
Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?
הַעֵינֵ֣י בָשָׂ֣ר לָ֑ךְ אִם־כִּרְא֖וֹת אֱנ֣וֹשׁ תִּרְאֶֽה׃
Are your days like the days of a mortal, or your years like the years of a man,
הֲכִימֵ֣י אֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמֶ֑יךָ אִם־שְׁ֝נוֹתֶ֗יךָ כִּ֣ימֵי גָֽבֶר׃
that you search for my guilt and seek out my sin,
כִּֽי־תְבַקֵּ֥שׁ לַעֲוֺנִ֑י וּֽלְחַטָּאתִֽ[m]י תִדְרֽוֹשׁ׃
though you know that I am not guilty, and there is no one to rescue me from your hand?
עַֽל־דַּ֭עְתְּךָ כִּי־לֹ֣א אֶרְשָׁ֑ע וְאֵ֖ין מִיָּדְךָ֣ מַצִּֽיל׃
Your hands shaped me and made me, all of me, and now you destroy me.[^3]
יָדֶ֣יךָ עִ֭צְּבוּנִי וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֑וּנִי יַ֥חַד סָ֝בִ֗יב וַֽתְּבַלְּעֵֽנִי׃
Remember that you made me like clay; will you turn me back into dust?
זְכָר־נָ֭א כִּי־כַחֹ֣מֶר עֲשִׂיתָ֑נִי וְֽאֶל־עָפָ֥ר תְּשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃
Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
הֲלֹ֣א כֶ֭חָלָב תַּתִּיכֵ֑נִי וְ֝כַגְּבִנָּ֗ה תַּקְפִּיאֵֽנִי׃
You clothed me with skin and flesh and wove me together with bones and sinews.
ע֣וֹר וּ֭בָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁ֑נִי וּֽבַעֲצָמ֥וֹת וְ֝גִידִ֗ים תְּסֹכְכֵֽנִי׃
You gave me life and faithful love,[^4] and your care has watched over my spirit.
חַיִּ֣ים וָ֭חֶסֶד עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝פְקֻדָּתְךָ֗ שָֽׁמְרָ֥ה רוּחִֽי׃
Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was your purpose.[^5]
וְ֭אֵלֶּה צָפַ֣נְתָּ בִלְבָבֶ֑ךָ יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־זֹ֥את עִמָּֽךְ׃
If I sinned, you would watch me and would not acquit me of my guilt.
אִם־חָטָ֥אתִי וּשְׁמַרְתָּ֑נִי וּ֝מֵעֲוֺנִ֗י לֹ֣א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃
If I am guilty, woe to me! And if I am in the right, I cannot lift my head, so filled with shame and looking at my misery.[^6]
אִם־רָשַׁ֡עְתִּי אַלְלַ֬י לִ֗י וְ֭צָדַקְתִּי לֹא־אֶשָּׂ֣א רֹאשִׁ֑י שְׂבַ֥ע קָ֝ל֗וֹן וּרְאֵ֥ה עָנְי֥‍ִ[c]י׃
And if it is lifted up,[^7] you hunt me like a lion, and again you show your wondrous power against me.
וְ֭יִגְאֶה כַּשַּׁ֣חַל תְּצוּדֵ֑נִי וְ֝תָשֹׁ֗ב תִּתְפַּלָּא־בִֽי׃
You bring new witnesses against me and increase your anger toward me; fresh troops come against me in waves.[^8]
תְּחַדֵּ֬שׁ עֵדֶ֨יךָ ׀ נֶגְדִּ֗י וְתֶ֣רֶב כַּֽ֭עַשְׂךָ עִמָּדִ֑י חֲלִיפ֖וֹת וְצָבָ֣א עִמִּֽי׃
Why then did you bring me out of the womb? I should have perished before any eye saw me.
וְלָ֣מָּה מֵ֭רֶחֶם הֹצֵאתָ֑נִי אֶ֝גְוַ֗ע וְעַ֣יִן לֹא־תִרְאֵֽנִי׃
I would have been as though I had never been, carried from the womb to the grave.
כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־הָיִ֣יתִי אֶהְיֶ֑ה מִ֝בֶּ֗טֶן לַקֶּ֥בֶר אוּבָֽל׃
Are not my days few? Stop! Leave me alone,[^9] so that I may have a little cheer
הֲלֹא־מְעַ֣ט יָמַ֣י *יחדל **וַחֲדָ֑ל *ישית **וְשִׁ֥ית מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְאַבְלִ֥יגָה מְּעָֽט׃
before I go, never to return, to the land of darkness and deep darkness,[^10]
בְּטֶ֣רֶם אֵ֭לֵךְ וְלֹ֣א אָשׁ֑וּב אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃
a land of gloom like the blackest night, of deep darkness and disorder, where even the light is like the blackest night."
אֶ֤רֶץ עֵיפָ֨תָה ׀ כְּמ֥וֹ אֹ֗פֶל צַ֭לְמָוֶת וְלֹ֥א סְדָרִ֗ים וַתֹּ֥פַע כְּמוֹ־אֹֽפֶל׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Job speaks to God from here to the end of the chapter.
n.2: Literally "shine on the counsel of the wicked".
n.3: Literally "made me together all around, and you swallow me up".
n.4: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.5: Literally "this is with you".
n.6: Or "Look at my misery!" The Hebrew vowel points read "see" as a command. Some scholars read *reveh*, "soaked", for *re'eh*, "seeing", with a small change to the Hebrew: "soaked in my misery".
n.7: That is, my head. Literally "it rises up proudly".
n.8: Literally "changes and an army are with me". Hebrew *chalifot ve-tsava*: perhaps troops coming on in relays.
n.9: The Hebrew text is written "Let him stop! Let him leave me alone" but read "Stop! Leave me alone".
n.10: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death". Also in verse 22.

v: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַֽנַּעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Should a flood of words go unanswered? Should a great talker[^1] be proved right?
הֲרֹ֣ב דְּ֭בָרִים לֹ֣א יֵעָנֶ֑ה וְאִם־אִ֖ישׁ שְׂפָתַ֣יִם יִצְדָּֽק׃
Should your idle talk silence people? Should you mock, and no one put you to shame?
בַּ֭דֶּיךָ מְתִ֣ים יַחֲרִ֑ישׁו וַ֝תִּלְעַ֗ג וְאֵ֣ין מַכְלִֽם׃
You say, 'My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your sight.'
וַ֭תֹּאמֶר זַ֣ךְ לִקְחִ֑י וּ֝בַ֗ר הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃
But oh, that God[^2] would speak, and open his lips against you,
וְֽאוּלָ֗ם מִֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן אֱל֣וֹהַּ דַּבֵּ֑ר וְיִפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתָ֣יו עִמָּֽךְ׃
and tell you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides.[^3] Know then that God is exacting from you less than your guilt deserves.[^4]
וְיַגֶּד־לְךָ֨ ׀ תַּֽעֲלֻמ֣וֹת חָכְמָה֮ כִּֽי־כִפְלַ֢יִם לְֽת֫וּשִׁיָּ֥ה וְדַ֡ע כִּֽי־יַשֶּׁ֥ה לְךָ֥ אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵעֲוֺנֶֽךָ׃
Can you find out the deep things of God? Can you reach the limits of the Almighty?[^5]
הַחֵ֣קֶר אֱל֣וֹהַ תִּמְצָ֑א אִ֤ם עַד־תַּכְלִ֖ית שַׁדַּ֣י תִּמְצָֽא׃
They are higher than the heavens: what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol:[^6] what can you know?
גָּבְהֵ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם מַה־תִּפְעָ֑ל עֲמֻקָּ֥ה מִ֝שְּׁא֗וֹל מַה־תֵּדָֽע׃
Their measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
אֲרֻכָּ֣ה מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִדָּ֑הּ וּ֝רְחָבָ֗ה מִנִּי־יָֽם׃
If he passes by and imprisons someone, and calls an assembly for judgment, who can stop him?
אִם־יַחֲלֹ֥ף וְיַסְגִּ֑יר וְ֝יַקְהִ֗יל וּמִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃
For he knows worthless people; when he sees wickedness, will he not take note of it?[^7]
כִּי־ה֭וּא יָדַ֣ע מְתֵי־שָׁ֑וְא וַיַּרְא־אָ֝֗וֶן וְלֹ֣א יִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃
An empty-headed person will get understanding when a wild donkey's colt is born human.[^8]
וְאִ֣ישׁ נָ֭בוּב יִלָּבֵ֑ב וְעַ֥יִר פֶּ֝֗רֶא אָדָ֥ם יִוָּלֵֽד׃
If you set your heart right and spread out your hands to him,
אִם־אַ֭תָּ֗[c]ה הֲכִינ֣וֹתָ לִבֶּ֑ךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ֖ אֵלָ֣יו כַּפֶּֽךָ׃
if there is wickedness in your hand, put it far away, and do not let injustice live in your tents.
אִם־אָ֣וֶן בְּ֭יָדְךָ הַרְחִיקֵ֑הוּ וְאַל־תַּשְׁכֵּ֖ן בְּאֹהָלֶ֣יךָ עַוְלָֽה׃
Then you will lift up your face without blemish; you will stand firm[^9] and will not fear.
כִּי־אָ֤ז ׀ תִּשָּׂ֣א פָנֶ֣יךָ מִמּ֑וּם וְהָיִ֥יתָ מֻ֝צָ֗ק וְלֹ֣א תִירָֽא׃
For you will forget your misery; you will remember it like water that has flowed past.
כִּי־אַ֭תָּה עָמָ֣ל תִּשְׁכָּ֑ח כְּמַ֖יִם עָבְר֣וּ תִזְכֹּֽר׃
Your life[^10] will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.[^11]
וּֽ֭מִצָּהֳרַיִם יָק֣וּם חָ֑לֶד תָּ֝עֻ֗פָה כַּבֹּ֥קֶר תִּהְיֶֽה׃
You will feel secure, because there is hope; you will look around[^12] and lie down in safety.
וּֽ֭בָטַחְתָּ כִּי־יֵ֣שׁ תִּקְוָ֑ה וְ֝חָפַרְתָּ֗ לָבֶ֥טַח תִּשְׁכָּֽב׃
You will lie down, and no one will make you afraid; many will seek your favor.[^13]
וְֽ֭רָבַצְתָּ וְאֵ֣ין מַחֲרִ֑יד וְחִלּ֖וּ פָנֶ֣יךָ רַבִּֽים׃
But the eyes of the wicked will fail; every way of escape will be gone from them, and their only hope will be to breathe their last."
וְעֵינֵ֥י רְשָׁעִ֗ים תִּ֫כְלֶ֥ינָה וּ֭מָנוֹס אָבַ֣ד מִנְהֶ֑ם וְ֝תִקְוָתָ֗ם מַֽפַּח־נָֽפֶשׁ׃ פ

n.1: Literally "a man of lips".
n.2: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verses 6 and 7.
n.3: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "for double to sound wisdom". Hebrew *tushiyyah*, as in 5:12.
n.4: Literally "God causes you to forget some of your guilt". Or "God has overlooked some of your guilt".
n.5: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.6: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.7: Or "he sees wickedness without needing to look closely". Literally "he sees iniquity and does not consider".
n.8: Probably a proverb: the first will happen no sooner than the second. Literally "A hollow man will get a heart, and a wild donkey's colt will be born a human".
n.9: Literally "you will be cast", like metal.
n.10: Hebrew *cheled*, "lifetime, the span of life".
n.11: Or "if there is darkness, it will be like the morning". The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.
n.12: Literally "dig" or "search". Some take the verb as a different *chafar*, "be ashamed": "you were ashamed, but you will lie down in safety".
n.13: Literally "many will stroke your face".

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"No doubt you are the people who matter,[^1] and wisdom will die with you!
אָ֭מְנָם כִּ֣י אַתֶּם־עָ֑ם וְ֝עִמָּכֶ֗ם תָּמ֥וּת חָכְמָֽה׃
But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?
גַּם־לִ֤י לֵבָ֨ב ׀ כְּֽמוֹכֶ֗ם לֹא־נֹפֵ֣ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּ֑ם וְאֶת מִי־אֵ֥ין כְּמוֹ־אֵֽלֶּה׃
I have become a laughingstock to my friends, I who called on God[^2] and he answered me. A righteous, blameless man is a laughingstock!
שְׂחֹ֤ק לְרֵעֵ֨הוּ ׀ אֶֽהְיֶ֗ה קֹרֵ֣א לֶ֭אֱלוֹהַּ וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑הוּ שְׂ֝ח֗וֹק צַדִּ֥יק תָּמִֽים׃
Those at ease have contempt for disaster;[^3] it is ready for those whose feet are slipping.
לַפִּ֣יד בּ֭וּז לְעַשְׁתּ֣וּת שַׁאֲנָ֑ן נָ֝כ֗וֹן לְמ֣וֹעֲדֵי רָֽגֶל׃
The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke God are secure, those who carry their god in their hand.[^4]
יִשְׁלָ֤יוּ אֹֽהָלִ֨ים ׀ לְשֹׁ֥דְדִ֗ים וּֽ֭בַטֻּחוֹת לְמַרְגִּ֣יזֵי אֵ֑ל לַאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵבִ֖יא אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
But ask the animals, and they will teach you, the birds of the sky, and they will tell you;
וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁאַל־נָ֣א בְהֵמ֣וֹת וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וְע֥וֹף הַ֝שָּׁמַ֗יִם וְיַגֶּד־לָֽךְ׃
or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, and let the fish of the sea tell you.
א֤וֹ שִׂ֣יחַ לָאָ֣רֶץ וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ לְ֝ךָ֗ דְּגֵ֣י הַיָּֽם׃
Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD[^5] has done this?
מִ֭י לֹא־יָדַ֣ע בְּכָל־אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֥י יַד־יְ֝הוָה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּֽאת׃
In his hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of every human being.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ֭יָדוֹ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־חָ֑י וְ֝ר֗וּחַ כָּל־בְּשַׂר־אִֽישׁ׃
Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?
הֲלֹא־אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן וְ֝חֵ֗ךְ אֹ֣כֶל יִטְעַם־לֽוֹ׃
Wisdom is with the aged, and understanding comes with length of days.[^6]
בִּֽישִׁישִׁ֥ים חָכְמָ֑ה וְאֹ֖רֶךְ יָמִ֣ים תְּבוּנָֽה׃
With him are wisdom and strength; counsel and understanding are his.
עִ֭מּוֹ חָכְמָ֣ה וּגְבוּרָ֑ה ל֝֗וֹ עֵצָ֥ה וּתְבוּנָֽה׃
Look, what he tears down cannot be rebuilt; when he shuts someone in, no one can open.
הֵ֣ן יַ֭הֲרוֹס וְלֹ֣א יִבָּנֶ֑ה יִסְגֹּ֥ר עַל־אִ֝֗ישׁ וְלֹ֣א יִפָּתֵֽחַ׃
Look, if he holds back the waters, they dry up; if he sends them out, they overturn the land.
הֵ֤ן יַעְצֹ֣ר בַּמַּ֣יִם וְיִבָ֑שׁוּ וִֽ֝ישַׁלְּחֵ֗ם וְיַ֖הַפְכוּ אָֽרֶץ׃
With him are strength and sound wisdom;[^7] the one who is misled and the one who misleads are his.
עִ֭מּוֹ עֹ֣ז וְתֽ[t]וּשִׁיָּ֑ה ל֝֗וֹ שֹׁגֵ֥ג וּמַשְׁגֶּֽה׃
He leads counselors away stripped[^8] and makes fools of judges.
מוֹלִ֣יךְ יוֹעֲצִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְֽשֹׁפְטִ֥ים יְהוֹלֵֽל׃
He loosens the belt of kings and ties a loincloth around their waist.[^9]
מוּסַ֣ר מְלָכִ֣ים פִּתֵּ֑חַ וַיֶּאְסֹ֥ר אֵ֝ז֗וֹר בְּמָתְנֵיהֶֽם׃
He leads priests away stripped and overthrows those long established.
מוֹלִ֣יךְ כֹּהֲנִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְאֵ֖תָנִ֣ים יְסַלֵּֽף׃
He silences trusted advisers[^10] and takes away the discernment of elders.
מֵסִ֣יר שָׂ֭פָה לְנֶאֱמָנִ֑ים וְטַ֖עַם זְקֵנִ֣ים יִקָּֽח׃
He pours contempt on nobles and loosens the belt of the strong.[^11]
שׁוֹפֵ֣ךְ בּ֭וּז עַל־נְדִיבִ֑ים וּמְזִ֖יחַ אֲפִיקִ֣ים רִפָּֽה׃
He uncovers deep things out of darkness and brings deep darkness[^12] into the light.
מְגַלֶּ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקוֹת מִנִּי־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיֹּצֵ֖א לָא֣וֹר צַלְמָֽוֶת׃
He makes nations great, and destroys them; he enlarges nations, and leads them away.
מַשְׂגִּ֣יא לַ֭גּוֹיִם וַֽיְאַבְּדֵ֑ם שֹׁטֵ֥חַ לַ֝גּוֹיִ֗ם וַיַּנְחֵֽם׃
He takes away the understanding of the leaders of the people of the earth and makes them wander in a trackless waste.[^13]
מֵסִ֗יר לֵ֭ב רָאשֵׁ֣י עַם־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם בְּתֹ֣הוּ לֹא־דָֽרֶךְ׃
They grope in darkness without light; he makes them stagger like a drunkard.
יְמַֽשְׁשׁוּ־חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־א֑וֹר וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם כַּשִּׁכּֽוֹר׃

n.1: Literally "Truly you are the people".
n.2: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 6.
n.3: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Hebrew *lappid* usually means "torch"; here it is probably *le-pid*, "for disaster".
n.4: Or "whom God has brought into his power". The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. The first line has *El*, the second *Eloah*.
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. This is the only place where the name is used in the speeches of Job and his friends (chapters 3–37). Isaiah 41:20 has the same words.
n.6: Perhaps a question, or a saying of the friends that Job quotes: "Is wisdom with the aged…?"
n.7: Hebrew *tushiyyah*, as in 5:12.
n.8: Hebrew *sholal*, "stripped", perhaps "barefoot" or "plundered", like captives. Also in verse 19.
n.9: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Perhaps "He undoes the bonds that kings impose, and binds a cloth around their own waist", that is, he makes them captives or slaves.
n.10: Literally "He removes the lip of the trusted".
n.11: Hebrew *afiqim*, a word of uncertain meaning here, perhaps "the strong".
n.12: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.13: Literally "in a waste (*tohu*) with no road". *Tohu* is the word for the formless earth in Genesis 1:2.

v: "Look, my eye has seen all this; my ear has heard and understood it.
הֶן־כֹּ֭ל רָאֲתָ֣ה עֵינִ֑י שָֽׁמְעָ֥ה אָ֝זְנִ֗י וַתָּ֥בֶן לָֽהּ׃
What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
כְּֽ֭דַעְתְּכֶם יָדַ֣עְתִּי גַם־אָ֑נִי לֹא־נֹפֵ֖ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּֽם׃
But I would speak to the Almighty;[^1] I want to argue my case with God.
אוּלָ֗ם אֲ֭נִי אֶל־שַׁדַּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְהוֹכֵ֖חַ אֶל־אֵ֣ל אֶחְפָּֽץ׃
But you smear over the truth with lies;[^2] you are all worthless physicians.
וְֽאוּלָ֗ם אַתֶּ֥ם טֹֽפְלֵי־שָׁ֑קֶר רֹפְאֵ֖י אֱלִ֣ל כֻּלְּכֶֽם׃
If only you would keep completely silent! That would be wisdom on your part.
מִֽי־יִ֭תֵּן הַחֲרֵ֣שׁ תַּחֲרִישׁ֑וּן וּתְהִ֖י לָכֶ֣ם לְחָכְמָֽה׃
Hear now my argument; listen to the pleadings of my lips.
שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֥א תוֹכַחְתִּ֑י וְרִב֖וֹת שְׂפָתַ֣י הַקְשִֽׁיבוּ׃
Will you speak what is false on God's behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him?
הַ֭לְאֵל תְּדַבְּר֣וּ עַוְלָ֑ה וְ֝ל֗וֹ תְּֽדַבְּר֥וּ רְמִיָּֽה׃
Will you take his side?[^3] Will you argue the case for God?
הֲפָנָ֥יו תִּשָּׂא֑וּן אִם־לָאֵ֥ל תְּרִיבֽוּן׃
Would it go well with you if he examined you? Can you deceive him as one deceives a mortal?
הֲ֭טוֹב כִּֽי־יַחְקֹ֣ר אֶתְכֶ֑ם אִם־כְּהָתֵ֥ל בֶּ֝אֱנ֗וֹשׁ תְּהָתֵ֥לּוּ בֽוֹ׃
He will surely rebuke you if you secretly take sides.
הוֹכֵ֣חַ יוֹכִ֣יחַ אֶתְכֶ֑ם אִם־בַּ֝סֵּ֗תֶר פָּנִ֥ים תִּשָּׂאֽוּן׃
Will not his majesty terrify you, and dread of him fall on you?
הֲלֹ֣א שְׂ֭אֵתוֹ תְּבַעֵ֣ת אֶתְכֶ֑ם וּ֝פַחְדּ֗וֹ יִפֹּ֥ל עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
זִֽ֭כְרֹנֵיכֶם מִשְׁלֵי־אֵ֑פֶר לְגַבֵּי־חֹ֝֗מֶר גַּבֵּיכֶֽם׃
Be silent before me, and let me speak, and let come on me what may.
הַחֲרִ֣ישׁוּ מִ֭מֶּנִּי וַאֲדַבְּרָה־אָ֑נִי וְיַעֲבֹ֖ר עָלַ֣י מָֽה׃
Why should I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hands?[^4]
עַל־מָ֤ה ׀ אֶשָּׂ֣א בְשָׂרִ֣י בְשִׁנָּ֑י וְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י אָשִׂ֥ים בְּכַפִּֽי׃
Even if he kills me, I will hope in him;[^5] yet I will argue my ways to his face.
הֵ֣ן יִ֭קְטְלֵנִי *לא **ל֣וֹ אֲיַחֵ֑ל אַךְ־דְּ֝רָכַ֗י אֶל־פָּנָ֥יו אוֹכִֽיחַ׃
This too will be my salvation, for no godless person would come before him.
גַּם־הוּא־לִ֥י לִֽישׁוּעָ֑ה כִּי־לֹ֥א לְ֝פָנָ֗יו חָנֵ֥ף יָבֽוֹא׃
Listen closely to my words; let my declaration be in your ears.
שִׁמְע֣וּ שָׁ֭מוֹעַ מִלָּתִ֑י וְ֝אֽ͏ַחֲוָתִ֗י בְּאָזְנֵיכֶֽם׃
Look now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be proved right.
הִנֵּה־נָ֭א עָרַ֣כְתִּי מִשְׁפָּ֑ט יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י אֶצְדָּֽק׃
Who is there who will contend with me? For then I would be silent and die.[^6]
מִי־ה֭וּא יָרִ֣יב עִמָּדִ֑י כִּֽי־עַתָּ֖ה אַחֲרִ֣ישׁ וְאֶגְוָֽע׃
Only do not do two things to me, and then I will not hide from your face:[^7]
אַךְ־שְׁ֭תַּיִם אַל־תַּ֣עַשׂ עִמָּדִ֑י אָ֥ז מִ֝פָּנֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א אֶסָּתֵֽר׃
take your hand far away from me, and do not let dread of you terrify me.
כַּ֭פְּךָ מֵעָלַ֣י הַרְחַ֑ק וְ֝אֵ֥מָתְךָ֗ אַֽל־תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃
Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you reply to me.
וּ֭קְרָא וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה אֽוֹ־אֲ֝דַבֵּ֗ר וַהֲשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃
How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my offense and my sin.
כַּמָּ֣ה לִ֭י עֲוֺנ֣וֹת וְחַטָּא֑וֹת פִּֽשְׁעִ֥י וְ֝חַטָּאתִ֗י הֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃
Why do you hide your face and count me as your enemy?[^8]
לָֽמָּה־פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר וְתַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לָֽךְ׃
Will you frighten a windblown leaf? Will you chase dry straw?
הֶעָלֶ֣ה נִדָּ֣ף תַּעֲר֑וֹץ וְאֶת־קַ֖שׁ יָבֵ֣שׁ תִּרְדֹּֽף׃
For you write bitter charges against me and make me inherit the sins of my youth.
כִּֽי־תִכְתֹּ֣ב עָלַ֣י מְרֹר֑וֹת וְ֝תוֹרִישֵׁ֗נִי עֲוֺנ֥וֹת נְעוּרָֽי׃
You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; you mark a line around the soles of my feet.[^9]
וְתָ֘שֵׂ֤ם בַּסַּ֨ד ׀ רַגְלַ֗י וְתִשְׁמ֥וֹר כָּל־אָרְחוֹתָ֑י עַל־שָׁרְשֵׁ֥י רַ֝גְלַ֗י תִּתְחַקֶּֽה׃
And so he[^10] wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.
וְ֭הוּא כְּרָקָ֣ב יִבְלֶ֑ה כְּ֝בֶ֗גֶד אֲכָ֣לוֹ עָֽשׁ׃

n.1: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.2: Literally "you are plasterers of lies".
n.3: Literally "lift up his face", a phrase for showing partiality in court. Also in verse 10.
n.4: Both lines mean "risk my life". Or "Whatever happens, I will take my flesh in my teeth".
n.5: The Hebrew text is written "Look, he will kill me; I have no hope" (*lo*, "not") but read "I will hope in him" (*lo*, "for him"). The verb *yachal* means "hope" or "wait". Traditionally "Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him".
n.6: That is, if anyone could prove him wrong, he would fall silent and die.
n.7: Job speaks to God from here to the end of chapter 14.
n.8: In Hebrew, *oyev*, "enemy", sounds like *Iyyov*, "Job".
n.9: Literally "you engrave yourself on the roots of my feet": perhaps a mark branded on a slave's feet, or a boundary drawn around them.
n.10: The human being of 14:1. This verse may belong with chapter 14.

v: "A human being, born of woman, is short of days and full of turmoil.
אָ֭דָם יְל֣וּד אִשָּׁ֑ה קְצַ֥ר יָ֝מִ֗ים וּֽשְׂבַֽע־רֹֽגֶז׃
He comes up like a flower and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not last.
כְּצִ֣יץ יָ֭צָא וַיִּמָּ֑ל וַיִּבְרַ֥ח כַּ֝צֵּ֗ל וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֽוֹד׃
Do you really fix your eyes on such a one? Do you bring me into judgment with you?
אַף־עַל־זֶ֭ה פָּקַ֣חְתָּ עֵינֶ֑ךָ וְאֹ֘תִ֤י תָבִ֖יא בְמִשְׁפָּ֣ט עִמָּֽךְ׃
Who can bring something clean out of something unclean? No one!
מִֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן טָ֭הוֹר מִטָּמֵ֗א לֹ֣א אֶחָֽד׃
Since his days are determined, and the number of his months is with you, and you have set him limits that he cannot pass,[^1]
אִ֥ם חֲרוּצִ֨ים ׀ יָמָ֗יו מִֽסְפַּר־חֳדָשָׁ֥יו אִתָּ֑ךְ *חקו **חֻקָּ֥יו עָ֝שִׂ֗יתָ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲבֽוֹר׃
look away from him, and let him rest, so that he can enjoy his day like a hired worker.
שְׁעֵ֣ה מֵעָלָ֣יו וְיֶחְדָּ֑ל עַד־יִ֝רְצֶ֗ה כְּשָׂכִ֥יר יוֹמֽוֹ׃
For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its shoots will not fail.
כִּ֤י יֵ֥שׁ לָעֵ֗ץ תִּ֫קְוָ֥ה אִֽם־יִ֭כָּרֵת וְע֣וֹד יַחֲלִ֑יף וְ֝יֹֽנַקְתּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א תֶחְדָּֽל׃
Though its root grows old in the earth and its stump dies in the dust,
אִם־יַזְקִ֣ין בָּאָ֣רֶץ שָׁרְשׁ֑וֹ וּ֝בֶעָפָ֗ר יָמ֥וּת גִּזְעֽוֹ׃
at the scent of water it will bud and put out branches like a young plant.
מֵרֵ֣יַּח מַ֣יִם יַפְרִ֑חַ וְעָשָׂ֖ה קָצִ֣יר כְּמוֹ־נָֽטַע׃
But a man dies and lies powerless; a human being breathes his last, and where is he?
וְגֶ֣בֶר יָ֭מוּת וַֽיֶּחֱלָ֑שׁ וַיִּגְוַ֖ע אָדָ֣ם וְאַיּֽוֹ׃
As water vanishes from a lake[^2] and a river dries up and is parched,
אָֽזְלוּ־מַ֭יִם מִנִּי־יָ֑ם וְ֝נָהָ֗ר יֶחֱרַ֥ב וְיָבֵֽשׁ׃
so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, people will not wake, or be roused from their sleep.
וְאִ֥ישׁ שָׁכַ֗ב וְֽלֹא־יָ֫ק֥וּם עַד־בִּלְתִּ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם לֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ וְלֹֽא־יֵ֝עֹ֗רוּ מִשְּׁנָתָֽם׃
If only you would hide me in Sheol,[^3] conceal me until your anger is past, set me a fixed time, and then remember me!
מִ֤י יִתֵּ֨ן ׀ בִּשְׁא֬וֹל תַּצְפִּנֵ֗נִי תַּ֭סְתִּירֵנִי עַד־שׁ֣וּב אַפֶּ֑ךָ תָּ֤שִֽׁ[m]ית לִ֖י חֹ֣ק וְתִזְכְּרֵֽנִי׃
If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I would wait, until my relief[^4] should come.
אִם־יָמ֥וּת גֶּ֗בֶר הֲיִ֫חְיֶ֥ה כָּל־יְמֵ֣י צְבָאִ֣י אֲיַחֵ֑ל עַד־בּ֝֗וֹא חֲלִיפָתִֽי׃
You would call, and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.
תִּ֭קְרָא וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ךָּ לְֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ תִכְסֹֽף׃
For then you would count my steps, but not keep watch over my sin.[^5]
כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה צְעָדַ֣י תִּסְפּ֑וֹר לֹֽא־תִ֝שְׁמ֗וֹר עַל־חַטָּאתִֽי׃
My offense would be sealed up in a bag, and you would cover over my guilt.[^6]
חָתֻ֣ם בִּצְר֣וֹר פִּשְׁעִ֑י וַ֝תִּטְפֹּ֗ל עַל־עֲוֺנִֽי׃
But as a mountain falls and crumbles away,[^7] and a rock is moved from its place,
וְ֭אוּלָם הַר־נוֹפֵ֣ל יִבּ֑וֹל וְ֝צ֗וּר יֶעְתַּ֥ק מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃
as water wears away stones and its torrents wash away the soil of the earth,[^8] so you destroy the hope of a mortal.
אֲבָנִ֤ים ׀ שָׁ֥חֲקוּ מַ֗יִם תִּשְׁטֹֽף־סְפִיחֶ֥יהָ עֲפַר־אָ֑רֶץ וְתִקְוַ֖ת אֱנ֣וֹשׁ הֶאֱבַֽדְתָּ׃
You overpower him forever, and he passes away; you change his appearance and send him away.
תִּתְקְפֵ֣הוּ לָ֭נֶצַח וַֽיַּהֲלֹ֑ךְ מְשַׁנֶּ֥ה פָ֝נָ֗יו וַֽתְּשַׁלְּחֵֽהוּ׃
His children are honored, but he does not know it; they are brought low, but he does not notice them.
יִכְבְּד֣וּ בָ֭נָיו וְלֹ֣א יֵדָ֑ע וְ֝יִצְעֲר֗וּ וְֽלֹא־יָבִ֥ין לָֽמוֹ׃
He feels only the pain of his own body, and mourns only for himself."[^9]
אַךְ־בְּ֭שָׂרוֹ עָלָ֣יו יִכְאָ֑ב וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ עָלָ֥יו תֶּאֱבָֽל׃ פ

n.1: The Hebrew text is written "his limit" but read "his limits".
n.2: Hebrew *yam*, "sea", used here of a lake or body of water.
n.3: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.4: Hebrew *chalifah*, "change", as when soldiers on duty are relieved. *Hard service* is the word in 7:1.
n.5: Or "For now you count my steps; do you not keep watch over my sin?"
n.6: Literally "you would plaster over my guilt", the verb used of the friends in 13:4.
n.7: Literally "a falling mountain withers". The Hebrew of this phrase is uncertain.
n.8: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "its outpourings wash away the dust of the earth".
n.9: Literally "His flesh on him feels pain, and his soul on him mourns".

v: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge and fill his belly with the east wind?
הֶֽחָכָ֗ם יַעֲנֶ֥ה דַֽעַת־ר֑וּחַ וִֽימַלֵּ֖א קָדִ֣ים בִּטְנֽוֹ׃
Should he argue with useless talk, with words that do no good?
הוֹכֵ֣חַ בְּ֭דָבָר לֹ֣א יִסְכּ֑וֹן וּ֝מִלִּ֗ים לֹא־יוֹעִ֥יל בָּֽם׃
But you are doing away with the fear of God[^1] and hindering devotion before God.
אַף־אַ֭תָּה תָּפֵ֣ר יִרְאָ֑ה וְתִגְרַ֥ע שִׂ֝יחָ֗ה לִפְנֵי־אֵֽל׃
For your guilt teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.
כִּ֤י יְאַלֵּ֣ף עֲוֺנְךָ֣ פִ֑יךָ וְ֝תִבְחַ֗ר לְשׁ֣וֹן עֲרוּמִֽים׃
Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips testify against you.
יַרְשִֽׁיעֲךָ֣ פִ֣יךָ וְלֹא־אָ֑נִי וּ֝שְׂפָתֶ֗יךָ יַעֲנוּ־בָֽךְ׃
Were you the first human being ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
הֲרִאישׁ֣וֹן אָ֭דָם תִּוָּלֵ֑ד וְלִפְנֵ֖י גְבָע֣וֹת חוֹלָֽלְתָּ׃
Do you listen in on the council of God?[^2] Do you keep wisdom to yourself?
הַבְס֣וֹד אֱל֣וֹהַ תִּשְׁמָ֑ע וְתִגְרַ֖ע אֵלֶ֣יךָ חָכְמָֽה׃
What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not with us as well?
מַה־יָּ֭דַעְתָּ וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע תָּ֝בִ֗ין וְֽלֹא־עִמָּ֥נוּ הֽוּא׃
Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, older than your father.
גַּם־שָׂ֣ב גַּם־יָשִׁ֣ישׁ בָּ֑נוּ כַּבִּ֖יר מֵאָבִ֣יךָ יָמִֽים׃
Are the consolations of God too small for you, or a word spoken gently to you?
הַמְעַ֣ט מִ֭מְּךָ תַּנְחֻמ֣וֹת אֵ֑ל וְ֝דָבָ֗ר לָאַ֥ט עִמָּֽךְ׃
Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,[^3]
מַה־יִּקָּחֲךָ֥ לִבֶּ֑ךָ וּֽמַה־יִּרְזְמ֥וּן עֵינֶֽיךָ׃
that you turn your spirit against God and let such words come out of your mouth?
כִּֽי־תָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־אֵ֣ל רוּחֶ֑ךָ וְהֹצֵ֖אתָ מִפִּ֣יךָ מִלִּֽין׃
What is a mortal, that he could be pure, or one born of woman, that he could be righteous?
מָֽה־אֱנ֥וֹשׁ כִּֽי־יִזְכֶּ֑ה וְכִֽי־יִ֝צְדַּ֗ק יְל֣וּד אִשָּֽׁה׃
If God puts no trust in his holy ones,[^4] and even the heavens are not pure in his sight,
הֵ֣ן *בקדשו **בִּ֭קְדֹשָׁיו לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ין וְ֝שָׁמַ֗יִם לֹא־זַכּ֥וּ בְעֵינָֽיו׃
how much less one who is detestable and corrupt, a man who drinks wickedness like water!
אַ֭ף כִּֽי־נִתְעָ֥ב וְֽנֶאֱלָ֑ח אִישׁ־שֹׁתֶ֖ה כַמַּ֣יִם עַוְלָֽה׃
I will explain to you; listen to me, and let me tell what I have seen,
אֲחַוְךָ֥ שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י וְזֶֽה־חָ֝זִ֗יתִי וַאֲסַפֵּֽרָה׃
what wise men have declared, and have not hidden, what came from their fathers,
אֲשֶׁר־חֲכָמִ֥ים יַגִּ֑ידוּ וְלֹ֥א כִֽ֝חֲד֗וּ מֵאֲבוֹתָֽם׃
to whom alone the land was given, when no stranger passed among them.
לָהֶ֣ם לְ֭בַדָּם נִתְּנָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלֹא־עָ֖בַר זָ֣ר בְּתוֹכָֽם׃
The wicked man writhes in pain all his days, through all the years that are stored up for the ruthless.
כָּל־יְמֵ֣י רָ֭שָׁע ה֣וּא מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל וּמִסְפַּ֥ר שָׁ֝נִ֗ים נִצְפְּנ֥וּ לֶעָרִֽיץ׃
The sound of terrors is in his ears; in time of peace the destroyer comes upon him.
קוֹל־פְּחָדִ֥ים בְּאָזְנָ֑יו בַּ֝שָּׁל֗וֹם שׁוֹדֵ֥ד יְבוֹאֶֽנּוּ׃
He does not believe he will come back out of darkness; he is marked out for the sword.
לֹא־יַאֲמִ֣ין שׁ֭וּב מִנִּי־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ *וצפו **וְצָפ֖וּי ה֣וּא אֱלֵי־חָֽרֶב׃
He wanders about for bread: 'Where is it?'[^5] He knows that a day of darkness is ready at hand.
נֹ֘דֵ֤ד ה֣וּא לַלֶּ֣חֶם אַיֵּ֑ה יָדַ֓ע ׀ כִּֽי־נָכ֖וֹן בְּיָד֣וֹ יֽוֹם־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for the attack.[^6]
יְֽ֭בַעֲתֻהוּ צַ֣ר וּמְצוּקָ֑ה תִּ֝תְקְפֵ֗הוּ כְּמֶ֤לֶךְ ׀ עָתִ֬יד לַכִּידֽוֹר׃
For he has stretched out his hand against God and defied the Almighty,[^7]
כִּֽי־נָטָ֣ה אֶל־אֵ֣ל יָד֑וֹ וְאֶל־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יִתְגַּבָּֽר׃
charging at him headlong,[^8] with the thick bosses of his shields.
יָר֣וּץ אֵלָ֣יו בְּצַוָּ֑אר בַּ֝עֲבִ֗י גַּבֵּ֥י מָֽגִנָּֽיו׃
For he has covered his face with his fat and put rolls of fat on his loins,
כִּֽי־כִסָּ֣ה פָנָ֣יו בְּחֶלְבּ֑וֹ וַיַּ֖עַשׂ פִּימָ֣ה עֲלֵי־כָֽסֶל׃
and he has lived in ruined cities, in houses no one should live in, which are destined to become heaps of rubble.
וַיִּשְׁכּ֤וֹן ׀ עָ֘רִ֤ים נִכְחָד֗וֹת בָּ֭תִּים לֹא־יֵ֣שְׁבוּ לָ֑מוֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר הִתְעַתְּד֣וּ לְגַלִּֽים׃
He will not grow rich, and his wealth will not last; his possessions will not spread over the land.[^9]
לֹֽא־יֶ֭עְשַׁר וְלֹא־יָק֣וּם חֵיל֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יִטֶּ֖ה לָאָ֣רֶץ מִנְלָֽם׃
He will not escape the darkness; a flame will wither his shoots, and he will be swept away by the breath of his mouth.[^10]
לֹֽא־יָס֨וּר ׀ מִנִּי־חֹ֗שֶׁךְ יֹֽ֭נַקְתּוֹ תְּיַבֵּ֣שׁ שַׁלְהָ֑בֶת וְ֝יָס֗וּר בְּר֣וּחַ פִּֽיו׃
Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness will be his reward.
אַל־יַאֲמֵ֣ן *בשו **בַּשָּׁ֣יו נִתְעָ֑ה כִּי־שָׁ֝֗וְא תִּהְיֶ֥ה תְמוּרָתֽוֹ׃
It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not be green.
בְּֽלֹא־י֭וֹמוֹ תִּמָּלֵ֑א וְ֝כִפָּת֗וֹ לֹ֣א רַעֲנָֽנָה׃
He will be like a vine that drops its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.
יַחְמֹ֣ס כַּגֶּ֣פֶן בִּסְר֑וֹ וְיַשְׁלֵ֥ךְ כַּ֝זַּ֗יִת נִצָּתֽוֹ׃
For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
כִּֽי־עֲדַ֣ת חָנֵ֣ף גַּלְמ֑וּד וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ אָכְלָ֥ה אָֽהֳלֵי־שֹֽׁ֥חַד׃
They conceive trouble and give birth to wickedness; their womb prepares deceit."
הָרֹ֣ה עָ֭מָל וְיָלֹ[t]ד אָ֑וֶן וּ֝בִטְנָ֗ם תָּכִ֥ין מִרְמָֽה׃ ס

n.1: Literally "fear".
n.2: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. *Council* is Hebrew *sod*, the inner circle of God's advisers, or its secret counsel.
n.3: Hebrew *razam*, a verb found only here, perhaps "flash" or "wink".
n.4: The Hebrew text is written "his holy one" but read "his holy ones": heavenly beings (compare 5:1).
n.5: The Greek Septuagint reads "he is appointed as food for vultures", reading *ayyah*, "kite, bird of prey", for *ayyeh*, "where?".
n.6: Hebrew *kidor*, a word found only here, perhaps "attack" or "battle".
n.7: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.8: Literally "with neck", that is, with head down or neck stiffened.
