n.9: Hebrew *minlam*, a word found only here and of uncertain meaning: perhaps "their possessions" or "their ears of grain". Literally "and their *minlam* will not bend to the earth".
n.10: Probably the breath of God's mouth (compare 4:9). The Hebrew vowel points read "he will turn away". With a small change, the line reads "his blossom will be swept away by the wind".

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"I have heard many things like these; you are all miserable comforters.
שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי כְאֵ֣לֶּה רַבּ֑וֹת מְנַחֲמֵ֖י עָמָ֣ל כֻּלְּכֶֽם׃
Is there no end to windy words? What drives you to keep answering?
הֲקֵ֥ץ לְדִבְרֵי־ר֑וּחַ א֥וֹ מַה־יַּ֝מְרִֽיצְךָ֗ כִּ֣י תַעֲנֶֽה׃
I too could talk as you do, if you were in my place.[^1] I could string together words against you and shake my head at you.
גַּ֤ם ׀ אָנֹכִי֮ כָּכֶ֢ם אֲדַ֫בֵּ֥רָה ל֤וּ־יֵ֪שׁ נַפְשְׁכֶ֡ם תַּ֤חַת נַפְשִׁ֗י אַחְבִּ֣ירָה עֲלֵיכֶ֣ם בְּמִלִּ֑ים וְאָנִ֥יעָה עֲ֝לֵיכֶ֗ם בְּמ֣וֹ רֹאשִֽׁי׃
I could strengthen you with my mouth, and the comfort of my lips would bring you relief.
אֲאַמִּצְכֶ֥ם בְּמוֹ־פִ֑י וְנִ֖יד שְׂפָתַ֣י יַחְשֹֽׂךְ׃
If I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I hold back, how much of it leaves me?
אִֽם־אֲ֭דַבְּרָה לֹא־יֵחָשֵׂ֣ךְ כְּאֵבִ֑י וְ֝אַחְדְּלָ֗ה מַה־מִנִּ֥י יַהֲלֹֽךְ׃
But now he has worn me out. You have devastated my whole household.[^2]
אַךְ־עַתָּ֥ה הֶלְאָ֑נִי הֲ֝שִׁמּ֗וֹתָ כָּל־עֲדָתִֽי׃
You have shriveled me up,[^3] and it has become a witness; my gauntness rises up against me and testifies to my face.
וַֽ֭תִּקְמְטֵנִי לְעֵ֣ד הָיָ֑ה וַיָּ֥קָם בִּ֥י כַ֝חֲשִׁ֗י בְּפָנַ֥י יַעֲנֶֽה׃
His anger has torn me, and he hates me; he gnashes his teeth at me. My enemy sharpens his eyes against me.
אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף ׀ וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֵ֗נִי חָרַ֣ק עָלַ֣י בְּשִׁנָּ֑יו צָרִ֓י ׀ יִלְט֖וֹשׁ עֵינָ֣יו לִֽי׃
They open their mouths wide against me; they strike my cheeks in contempt; they mass together against me.
פָּעֲר֬וּ עָלַ֨י ׀ בְּפִיהֶ֗ם בְּ֭חֶרְפָּה הִכּ֣וּ לְחָיָ֑י יַ֝֗חַד עָלַ֥י יִתְמַלָּאֽוּן׃
God hands me over to the unjust[^4] and throws me into the hands of the wicked.
יַסְגִּירֵ֣נִי אֵ֭ל אֶ֣ל עֲוִ֑יל וְעַל־יְדֵ֖י רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִרְטֵֽנִי׃
I was at ease, but he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces. He set me up as his target;
שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי ׀ וַֽיְפַרְפְּרֵ֗נִי וְאָחַ֣ז בְּ֭עָרְפִּי וַֽיְפַצְפְּצֵ֑נִי וַיְקִימֵ֥נִי ל֝֗וֹ לְמַטָּרָֽה׃
his archers[^5] surround me. He pierces my kidneys and does not spare; he pours out my gall on the ground.
יָ֘סֹ֤בּוּ עָלַ֨י ׀ רַבָּ֗יו יְפַלַּ֣ח כִּ֭לְיוֹתַי וְלֹ֣א יַחְמ֑וֹל יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ לָ֝אָ֗רֶץ מְרֵרָֽתִי׃
He breaks through me, breach after breach; he charges at me like a warrior.
יִפְרְצֵ֣נִי פֶ֭רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵי־פָ֑רֶץ יָרֻ֖ץ עָלַ֣י כְּגִבּֽוֹר׃
I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and buried my horn[^6] in the dust.
שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי עֲלֵ֣י גִלְדִּ֑י וְעֹלַ֖לְתִּי בֶעָפָ֣ר קַרְנִֽי׃
My face is red with weeping, and deep darkness[^7] is on my eyelids,
פָּנַ֣י *חמרמרה **חֳ֭מַרְמְרוּ מִנִּי־בֶ֑כִי וְעַ֖ל עַפְעַפַּ֣י צַלְמָֽוֶת׃
although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
עַ֭ל לֹא־חָמָ֣ס בְּכַפָּ֑י וּֽתְפִלָּתִ֥י זַכָּֽה׃
O earth, do not cover my blood; let my cry find no resting place.
אֶ֭רֶץ אַל־תְּכַסִּ֣י דָמִ֑י וְֽאַל־יְהִ֥י מָ֝ק֗וֹם לְזַעֲקָתִֽי׃
Even now, look, my witness is in heaven, and the one who testifies for me[^8] is on high.
גַּם־עַ֭תָּה הִנֵּה־בַשָּׁמַ֣יִם עֵדִ֑י וְ֝שָׂהֲדִ֗י בַּמְּרוֹמִֽים׃
My friends scorn me;[^9] my eye pours out tears to God.[^10]
מְלִיצַ֥י רֵעָ֑י אֶל־אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ דָּלְפָ֥ה עֵינִֽי׃
Let him argue a man's case with God, as a person does for his friend.[^11]
וְיוֹכַ֣ח לְגֶ֣בֶר עִם־אֱל֑וֹהַּ וּֽבֶן־אָדָ֥ם לְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃
For only a few years will pass, and I will go the way of no return.
כִּֽי־שְׁנ֣וֹת מִסְפָּ֣ר יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ וְאֹ֖רַח לֹא־אָשׁ֣וּב אֶהֱלֹֽךְ׃

n.1: Literally "if your soul were in place of my soul".
n.2: Literally "my whole company". In verses 7–14 Job speaks of God as "he" and to him as "you", moving between the two.
n.3: Hebrew *qamat*, a rare verb: perhaps "shrivel" or "seize".
n.4: Hebrew *awil*, probably "the unjust". In 19:18 and 21:11 the same word means "young child".
n.5: Or "his many", "his troops".
n.6: A symbol of strength and dignity.
n.7: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.8: Hebrew *sahadi*, an Aramaic word for "my witness".
n.9: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "my scorners, my friends". Hebrew *melitsai* can also mean "my spokesmen" or "my intercessors": "My intercessor is my friend". Who the witness of verse 19 is, and who would argue for Job in verse 21, is not said.
n.10: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 21.
n.11: Literally "and a son of man for his friend".

v: "My spirit is broken; my days are snuffed out; the grave awaits me.[^1]
רוּחִ֣י חֻ֭בָּלָה יָמַ֥י נִזְעָ֗כוּ קְבָרִ֥ים לִֽי׃
Surely mockers are all around me, and my eye must dwell on their provocation.
אִם־לֹ֣א הֲ֭תֻלִים עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝בְהַמְּרוֹתָ֗ם תָּלַ֥ן עֵינִֽי׃
Give a pledge for me, please, with yourself.[^2] Who else will shake hands to guarantee me?[^3]
שִֽׂימָה־נָּ֭א עַ[t]רְבֵ֣נִי עִמָּ֑ךְ מִֽ[m]י ה֝֗וּא לְיָדִ֥י יִתָּקֵֽעַ׃
For you have closed their minds to understanding;[^4] so you will not let them triumph.
כִּֽי־לִ֭בָּם צָפַ֣נְתָּ מִ[t]שָּׂ֑כֶל עַל־כֵּ֝֗ן לֹ֣א תְרֹמֵֽם׃
One who denounces his friends for gain,[^5] the eyes of his children will fail.
לְ֭חֵלֶק יַגִּ֣יד רֵעִ֑ים וְעֵינֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו תִּכְלֶֽנָה׃
He has made me a byword among the peoples; I have become one in whose face people spit.[^6]
וְֽ֭הִצִּגַנִי לִמְשֹׁ֣ל עַמִּ֑ים וְתֹ֖פֶתּ לְפָנִ֣ים אֶֽהְיֶֽה׃
My eye has grown dim with grief, and all my limbs are like a shadow.
וַתֵּ֣כַהּ מִכַּ֣עַשׂ עֵינִ֑י וִֽיצֻרַ֖י כַּצֵּ֣ל כֻּלָּֽם׃
The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent are stirred up against the godless.
יָשֹׁ֣מּוּ יְשָׁרִ֣ים עַל־זֹ֑את וְ֝נָקִ֗י עַל־חָנֵ֥ף יִתְעֹרָֽר׃
Yet the righteous hold to their way, and those with clean hands grow stronger and stronger.
וְיֹאחֵ֣ז צַדִּ֣יק דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּֽטֳהָר־יָ֝דַ֗יִם יֹסִ֥יף אֹֽמֶץ׃
But as for all of you, come back again, please! I will not find a wise man among you.
וְֽאוּלָ֗ם כֻּלָּ֣ם תָּ֭שֻׁבוּ וּבֹ֣אוּ נָ֑א וְלֹֽא־אֶמְצָ֖א בָכֶ֣ם חָכָֽם׃
My days are past; my plans are broken off, the desires of my heart.[^7]
יָמַ֣י עָ֭בְרוּ זִמֹּתַ֣י נִתְּק֑וּ מ֖וֹרָשֵׁ֣י לְבָבִּֽי׃
They turn night into day: 'Light is near,' they say, in the face of darkness.[^8]
לַ֭יְלָה לְי֣וֹם יָשִׂ֑ימוּ א֝֗וֹר קָר֥וֹב מִפְּנֵי־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
If I look to Sheol[^9] as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
אִם־אֲ֭קַוֶּה שְׁא֣וֹל בֵּיתִ֑י בַּ֝חֹ֗שֶׁךְ רִפַּ֥דְתִּי יְצוּעָֽי׃
if I say to the pit,[^10] 'You are my father,' and to the worm, 'My mother,' or 'My sister,'
לַשַּׁ֣חַת קָ֭רָאתִי אָ֣בִי אָ֑תָּה אִמִּ֥י וַ֝אֲחֹתִ֗י לָֽרִמָּֽה׃
where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
וְ֭אַיֵּה אֵפ֣וֹ תִקְוָתִ֑י וְ֝תִקְוָתִ֗י מִ֣י יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃
Will it go down to the bars of Sheol?[^11] Shall we rest together in the dust?"
בַּדֵּ֣י שְׁאֹ֣ל תֵּרַ֑דְנָה אִם־יַ֖חַד עַל־עָפָ֣ר נָֽחַת׃ ס

n.1: Literally "graves are for me".
n.2: Job speaks to God. Literally "Set, please, pledge me with yourself".
n.3: Literally "Who is he who will strike my hand?", a gesture of guaranteeing someone's debt (Proverbs 6:1; 17:18).
n.4: Literally "hidden their heart from insight".
n.5: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "For a portion he informs on friends". Or "He invites friends to share his portion, while the eyes of his own children fail".
n.6: Hebrew *tofet*, "spitting". Literally "I will be a spitting in the face". The Hebrew of this phrase is uncertain.
n.7: Literally "the possessions of my heart".
n.8: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "light is near from the face of darkness". Or "light is nearer than darkness".
n.9: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. Also in verse 16.
n.10: Or "to corruption". Hebrew *shachat*.
n.11: Literally "They will go down to the bars of Sheol", that is, his hopes. The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. *Bars* may instead mean "limbs" or "parts".

v: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשֻּׁחִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"How long will you hunt for words?[^1] Show some sense, and then we can talk.
עַד־אָ֤נָה ׀ תְּשִׂימ֣וּן קִנְצֵ֣י לְמִלִּ֑ין תָּ֝בִ֗ינוּ וְאַחַ֥ר נְדַבֵּֽר׃
Why are we counted as cattle, considered stupid[^2] in your sight?
מַ֭דּוּעַ נֶחְשַׁ֣בְנוּ כַבְּהֵמָ֑ה נִ֝טְמִ֗ינוּ בְּעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃
You who tear yourself apart in your anger, is the earth to be abandoned for your sake, or the rock moved from its place?
טֹֽרֵ֥ף נַפְשׁ֗וֹ בְּאַ֫פּ֥וֹ הֲ֭לְמַּעַנְךָ תֵּעָ֣זַב אָ֑רֶץ וְיֶעְתַּק־צ֝֗וּר מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃
Yes, the light of the wicked is put out, and the flame of his fire does not shine.
גַּ֤ם א֣וֹר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־יִ֝גַּ֗הּ שְׁבִ֣יב אִשּֽׁוֹ׃
The light grows dark in his tent, and his lamp above him is put out.
א֖[d]וֹר חָשַׁ֣ךְ בְּאָהֳל֑וֹ וְ֝נֵר֗וֹ עָלָ֥יו יִדְעָֽךְ׃
His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes bring him down.
יֵֽ֭צְרוּ צַעֲדֵ֣י אוֹנ֑וֹ וְֽתַשְׁלִיכֵ֥הוּ עֲצָתֽוֹ׃
For his own feet throw him into a net, and he walks onto its mesh.
כִּֽי־שֻׁלַּ֣ח בְּרֶ֣שֶׁת בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וְעַל־שְׂ֝בָכָ֗ה יִתְהַלָּֽךְ׃
A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare holds him fast.
יֹאחֵ֣ז בְּעָּקֵ֣ב פָּ֑ח יַחֲזֵ֖ק עָלָ֣יו צַמִּֽים׃
A noose is hidden for him on the ground, a trap for him on the path.
טָמ֣וּן בָּאָ֣רֶץ חַבְל֑וֹ וּ֝מַלְכֻּדְתּ֗וֹ עֲלֵ֣י נָתִֽיב׃
Terrors frighten him on every side and chase him at every step.
סָ֭בִיב בִּֽעֲתֻ֣הוּ בַלָּה֑וֹת וֶהֱפִיצֻ֥הוּ לְרַגְלָֽיו׃
His strength is starved,[^3] and disaster is ready at his side.
יְהִי־רָעֵ֥ב אֹנ֑וֹ וְ֝אֵ֗יד נָכ֥וֹן לְצַלְעֽוֹ׃
It eats away the parts of his skin; the firstborn of Death[^4] devours his limbs.
יֹ֭אכַל בַּדֵּ֣י עוֹר֑וֹ יֹאכַ֥ל בַּ֝דָּ֗יו בְּכ֣וֹר מָֽוֶת׃
He is torn from the tent he trusted in and marched off to the king of terrors.[^5]
יִנָּתֵ֣ק מֵ֭אָהֳלוֹ מִבְטַח֑וֹ וְ֝תַצְעִדֵ֗הוּ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בַּלָּהֽוֹת׃
What is not his lives in his tent;[^6] sulfur is scattered over his home.
תִּשְׁכּ֣וֹן בְּ֭אָהֳלוֹ מִבְּלִי־ל֑וֹ יְזֹרֶ֖ה עַל־נָוֵ֣הוּ גָפְרִֽית׃
His roots dry up beneath, and his branches wither above.
מִ֭תַּחַת שָֽׁרָשָׁ֣יו יִבָ֑שׁוּ וּ֝מִמַּ֗עַל יִמַּ֥ל קְצִירֽוֹ׃
The memory of him perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the land.[^7]
זִֽכְרוֹ־אָ֭בַד מִנִּי־אָ֑רֶץ וְלֹא־שֵׁ֥ם ל֝֗וֹ עַל־פְּנֵי־חֽוּץ׃
He is driven out of light into darkness and chased out of the world.
יֶ֭הְדְּפֻהוּ מֵא֣וֹר אֶל־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וּֽמִתֵּבֵ֥ל יְנִדֻּֽהוּ׃
He has no offspring or descendant among his people, and no survivor where he used to live.
לֹ֘א נִ֤ין ל֣וֹ וְלֹא־נֶ֣כֶד בְּעַמּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֥ין שָׂ֝רִ֗יד בִּמְגוּרָֽיו׃
Those in the west are appalled at his fate, and those in the east are seized with horror.[^8]
עַל־י֭וֹמוֹ נָשַׁ֣מּוּ אַחֲרֹנִ֑ים וְ֝קַדְמֹנִ֗ים אָ֣חֲזוּ שָֽׂעַר׃
Surely such are the dwellings of the unjust, and this is the place of one who does not know God."
אַךְ־אֵ֭לֶּה מִשְׁכְּנ֣וֹת עַוָּ֑ל וְ֝זֶ֗ה מְק֣וֹם לֹא־יָדַֽע־אֵֽל׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *kintse*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "snares": literally "How long will you set snares for words?" Or "How long before you put an end to words?" The Hebrew "you" is plural here and in verse 3.
n.2: Or "unclean".
n.3: Or "Calamity is hungry for him". Hebrew *on*, "strength", may be read *awen*, "trouble".
n.4: Probably a deadly disease. Death (Hebrew *mavet*) may be pictured as a person, as in Canaanite myth, where Mot (Death) is a god.
n.5: Death, pictured as a king.
n.6: Literally "from without to him". The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Or "Nothing of his remains in his tent".
n.7: Literally "on the face of the outside", perhaps "in the streets" or "in the open country".
n.8: Or "Later generations are appalled at his day, and earlier ones are seized with horror". Literally "those after" and "those before".

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"How long will you torment me and crush me with words?
עַד־אָ֭נָה תּוֹגְי֣וּן נַפְשִׁ֑י וּֽתְדַכּאוּנַ֥נִי בְמִלִּֽים׃
Ten times now you have insulted me; are you not ashamed to wrong me?[^1]
זֶ֤ה עֶ֣שֶׂר פְּ֭עָמִים תַּכְלִימ֑וּנִי לֹֽא־תֵ֝בֹ֗שׁוּ תַּהְכְּרוּ־לִֽי׃
Even if it is true that I have gone astray, my error remains my own concern.[^2]
וְאַף־אָמְנָ֥ם שָׁגִ֑יתִי אִ֝תִּ֗י תָּלִ֥ין מְשׁוּגָתִֽי׃
If you really want to exalt yourselves over me and use my disgrace as an argument against me,
אִם־אָ֭מְנָם עָלַ֣י תַּגְדִּ֑ילוּ וְתוֹכִ֥יחוּ עָ֝לַ֗י חֶרְפָּתִּֽ[t][t]י׃
then know that God[^3] has put me in the wrong[^4] and closed his net around me.
דְּֽעוּ־אֵ֭פוֹ כִּי־אֱל֣וֹהַּ עִוְּתָ֑נִי וּ֝מְצוּד֗וֹ עָלַ֥י הִקִּֽיף׃
Look, I cry out, 'Violence!' but I get no answer; I call for help, but there is no justice.
הֵ֤ן אֶצְעַ֣ק חָ֭מָס וְלֹ֣א אֵעָנֶ֑ה אֲ֝שַׁוַּ֗ע וְאֵ֣ין מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
He has walled up my way so that I cannot pass, and he has set darkness on my paths.
אָרְחִ֣י גָ֭דַר וְלֹ֣א אֶעֱב֑וֹר וְעַ֥ל נְ֝תִיבוֹתַ֗י חֹ֣שֶׁךְ יָשִֽׂים׃
He has stripped me of my honor and taken the crown from my head.
כְּ֭בוֹדִי מֵעָלַ֣י הִפְשִׁ֑יט וַ֝יָּ֗סַר עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשִֽׁי׃
He tears me down on every side, and I am gone; he has uprooted my hope like a tree.
יִתְּצֵ֣נִי סָ֭בִיב וָאֵלַ֑ךְ וַיַּסַּ֥ע כָּ֝עֵ֗ץ תִּקְוָתִֽי׃
He has kindled his anger against me and counts me as one of his enemies.
וַיַּ֣חַר עָלַ֣י אַפּ֑וֹ וַיַּחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי ל֣וֹ כְצָרָֽיו׃
His troops advance together; they build up a siege ramp against me[^5] and camp around my tent.
יַ֤חַד ׀ יָ֘בֹ֤אוּ גְדוּדָ֗יו וַיָּסֹ֣לּוּ עָלַ֣י דַּרְכָּ֑ם וַיַּחֲנ֖וּ סָבִ֣יב לְאָהֳלִֽי׃
He has put my brothers far from me; those who know me are wholly estranged from me.
אַ֭חַי מֵעָלַ֣י הִרְחִ֑יק וְ֝יֹדְעַ֗י אַךְ־זָ֥רוּ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
My relatives have failed me; my close friends have forgotten me.
חָדְל֥וּ קְרוֹבָ֑י וּֽמְיֻדָּעַ֥י שְׁכֵחֽוּנִי׃
The guests in my house and my female servants count me as a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their eyes.
גָּ֘רֵ֤י בֵיתִ֣י וְ֭אַמְהֹתַי לְזָ֣ר תַּחְשְׁבֻ֑נִי נָ֝כְרִ֗י הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃
I call my servant, but he does not answer, though I plead with him with my own mouth.
לְעַבְדִּ֣י קָּ֭רָאתִי וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֑ה בְּמוֹ־פִ֗[t]‍֝י אֶתְחַנֶּן־לֽוֹ׃
My breath is repulsive to my wife; I am loathsome to my own brothers.[^6]
ר֭וּחִֽי זָ֣רָה לְאִשְׁתִּ֑י וְ֝חַנֹּתִ֗י לִבְנֵ֥י בִטְנִֽי׃
Even young children despise me; when I get up, they speak against me.
גַּם־עֲ֭וִילִים מָ֣אֲסוּ בִ֑י אָ֝ק֗וּמָה וַיְדַבְּרוּ־בִֽי׃
All my intimate friends[^7] detest me; those I love have turned against me.
תִּֽ֭עֲבוּנִי כָּל־מְתֵ֣י סוֹדִ֑י וְזֶֽה־אָ֝הַ֗בְתִּי נֶהְפְּכוּ־בִֽי׃
My bones cling to my skin and my flesh; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.[^8]
בְּעוֹרִ֣י וּ֭בִבְשָׂרִי דָּבְקָ֣ה עַצְמִ֑י וָ֝אֶתְמַלְּטָ֗ה בְּע֣וֹר שִׁנָּֽי׃
Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has struck me!
חָנֻּ֬נִי חָנֻּ֣נִי אַתֶּ֣ם רֵעָ֑י כִּ֥י יַד־אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ נָ֣גְעָה בִּֽי׃
Why do you pursue me as God does? Will you never have enough of my flesh?[^9]
לָ֭מָּה תִּרְדְּפֻ֣נִי כְמוֹ־אֵ֑ל וּ֝מִבְּשָׂרִ֗י לֹ֣א תִשְׂבָּֽעוּ׃
Oh, that my words were written down! Oh, that they were inscribed in a scroll,[^10]
מִֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן אֵ֭פוֹ וְיִכָּתְב֣וּן מִלָּ֑י מִֽי־יִתֵּ֖ן בַּסֵּ֣פֶר וְיֻחָֽקוּ׃
with an iron pen and lead, carved in the rock forever!
בְּעֵט־בַּרְזֶ֥ל וְעֹפָ֑רֶת לָ֝עַ֗ד בַּצּ֥וּר יֵחָצְבֽוּן׃
But I know that my redeemer[^11] lives, and that at the last he will rise up upon the earth.[^12]
וַאֲנִ֣י יָ֭דַעְתִּי גֹּ֣אֲלִי חָ֑י וְ֝אַחֲר֗וֹן עַל־עָפָ֥ר יָקֽוּם׃
And after my skin has been stripped off like this,[^13] yet in my flesh I will see God.[^14]
וְאַחַ֣ר ע֭וֹרִֽי נִקְּפוּ־זֹ֑את וּ֝מִבְּשָׂרִ֗י אֶֽחֱזֶ֥ה אֱלֽוֹהַּ׃
I myself will see him, with my own eyes, I and not a stranger.[^15] My heart faints within me![^16]
אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִ֨י ׀ אֶֽחֱזֶה־לִּ֗י וְעֵינַ֣י רָא֣וּ וְלֹא־זָ֑ר כָּל֖וּ כִלְיֹתַ֣י בְּחֵקִֽי׃
If you say, 'How we will hound him!' and that the root of the trouble is found in me,[^17]
כִּ֣י תֹ֭[t]אמְרוּ מַה־נִּרְדָּף־ל֑וֹ וְשֹׁ֥רֶשׁ דָּ֝בָ֗ר נִמְצָא־בִֽי׃
be afraid of the sword yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword,[^18] so that you may know there is a judgment."[^19]
גּ֤וּרוּ לָכֶ֨ם ׀ מִפְּנֵי־חֶ֗רֶב כִּֽי־חֵ֭מָה עֲוֺנ֣וֹת חָ֑רֶב לְמַ֖עַן תֵּדְע֣וּן *שדין **שַׁדּֽוּן׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *tahkeru*, a verb found only here. Its meaning is uncertain: perhaps "wrong", "attack" or "be hard on".
n.2: Literally "my error lodges with me".
n.3: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verses 21 and 26.
n.4: The verb Bildad used in 8:3: "Does God pervert justice?"
n.5: Literally "they have cast up their way against me".
n.6: Literally "the sons of my womb", probably the sons of the same mother, his brothers. Job's own children had died (1:19).
n.7: Literally "the men of my council".
n.8: The meaning of this phrase is uncertain. It may mean that he has barely escaped with his life, or that nothing is left of him but his gums.
n.9: To "eat someone's flesh" is an idiom for slandering them (compare Daniel 3:8, in Aramaic).
n.10: Or "on an inscription". Verse 24 may picture letters cut in the rock and filled with lead.
n.11: Hebrew *go'el*: the nearest relative, whose duty was to stand up for a family member in need, buying back property or a relative sold into slavery (Leviticus 25:25, 47–49), avenging a killing (Numbers 35:19), and taking up a relative's cause (Proverbs 23:10–11). Here the word may also be rendered "defender" or "vindicator": one who will take up Job's case and clear his name. Job does not say who his *go'el* is. Interpreters have understood God himself, or a heavenly witness or advocate like the ones Job longs for in 9:33 and 16:19–21. Traditionally "my Redeemer".
n.12: Literally "and last upon the dust he will stand". *At the last* (Hebrew *acharon*) may mean "in the end", "afterward", or "as the last one", the one who has the final word. *Rise up* may be the legal term for a witness standing to testify (Deuteronomy 19:15–16). *The earth* is literally "the dust", which may mean the ground, or the dust of the grave (17:16).
n.13: The Hebrew of verses 26–27 is very difficult. The first line of verse 26 is literally "and after my skin they have struck off (or "torn") this".
n.14: Literally "and from my flesh I will see God". *From my flesh* may mean "from within my flesh", still in the body, or "away from my flesh", without the body. So the verse may speak of seeing God in this life, after his disease has done its work, or after death.
n.15: Or "and not as a stranger", "and not another". *I myself will see him* may also be read "I will see him on my side".
n.16: Literally "my kidneys fail within my bosom". The kidneys were thought of as the seat of the deepest feelings.
n.17: Literally "and the root of the matter is found in me". Many interpreters read "in him", as the friends' own words.
n.18: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "for wrath is iniquities of the sword".
n.19: The Hebrew text is written *shedin*, "that there is judgment", but read *shaddun*, a form of uncertain meaning: perhaps also "that there is a judgment", or a play on *Shaddai*, "the Almighty".

v: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַנַּֽעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"So my troubled thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.[^1]
לָ֭כֵן שְׂעִפַּ֣י יְשִׁיב֑וּנִי וּ֝בַעֲב֗וּר ח֣וּשִׁי בִֽי׃
I hear a rebuke that insults me, and a spirit from my understanding answers me.[^2]
מוּסַ֣ר כְּלִמָּתִ֣י אֶשְׁמָ֑ע וְ֝ר֗וּחַ מִֽבִּינָתִ֥י יַעֲנֵֽנִי׃
Do you not know this from of old, ever since humankind was placed on the earth,
הֲזֹ֣את יָ֭דַעְתָּ מִנִּי־עַ֑ד מִנִּ֤י שִׂ֖ים אָדָ֣ם עֲלֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
that the shout of joy of the wicked is short, and the gladness of the godless lasts only a moment?
כִּ֤י רִנְנַ֣ת רְ֭שָׁעִים מִקָּר֑וֹב וְשִׂמְחַ֖ת חָנֵ֣ף עֲדֵי־רָֽגַע׃
Though his pride reaches up to the heavens and his head touches the clouds,
אִם־יַעֲלֶ֣ה לַשָּׁמַ֣יִם שִׂיא֑וֹ וְ֝רֹאשׁ֗וֹ לָעָ֥ב יַגִּֽיעַ׃
he will perish forever like his own dung; those who saw him will say, 'Where is he?'
כְּֽ֭גֶלֲלוֹ לָנֶ֣צַח יֹאבֵ֑ד רֹ֝אָ֗יו יֹאמְר֥וּ אַיּֽוֹ׃
He flies away like a dream and cannot be found; he is chased away like a vision of the night.
כַּחֲל֣וֹם יָ֭עוּף וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָא֑וּהוּ וְ֝יֻדַּ֗ד כְּחֶזְי֥וֹן לָֽיְלָה׃
The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.
עַ֣יִן שְׁ֭זָפַתּוּ וְלֹ֣א תוֹסִ֑יף וְלֹא־ע֝֗וֹד תְּשׁוּרֶ֥נּוּ מְקוֹמֽוֹ׃
His children will seek the favor of the poor,[^3] and his own hands will give back his wealth.
בָּ֭נָיו יְרַצּ֣וּ דַלִּ֑ים וְ֝יָדָ֗יו תָּשֵׁ֥בְנָה אוֹנֽוֹ׃
His bones are full of youthful vigor, but it will lie down with him in the dust.
עַ֭צְמוֹתָיו מָלְא֣וּ *עלומו **עֲלוּמָ֑יו וְ֝עִמּ֗וֹ עַל־עָפָ֥ר תִּשְׁכָּֽב׃
Though evil is sweet in his mouth, and he hides it under his tongue,
אִם־תַּמְתִּ֣יק בְּפִ֣יו רָעָ֑ה יַ֝כְחִידֶ֗נָּה תַּ֣חַת לְשׁוֹנֽוֹ׃
though he savors it and will not let it go, but holds it in his mouth,
יַחְמֹ֣ל עָ֭לֶיהָ וְלֹ֣א יַֽעַזְבֶ֑נָּה וְ֝יִמְנָעֶ֗נָּה בְּת֣וֹךְ חִכּֽוֹ׃
his food turns sour in his stomach; it becomes the venom of cobras within him.[^4]
לַ֭חְמוֹ בְּמֵעָ֣יו נֶהְפָּ֑ךְ מְרוֹרַ֖ת פְּתָנִ֣ים בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
He swallows riches and vomits them up; God makes his belly throw them out.
חַ֣יִל בָּ֭לַע וַיְקִאֶ֑נּוּ מִ֝בִּטְנ֗וֹ יוֹרִשֶׁ֥נּוּ אֵֽל׃
He will suck the poison of cobras; the tongue of the viper will kill him.
רֹאשׁ־פְּתָנִ֥ים יִינָ֑ק תַּֽ֝הַרְגֵ֗הוּ לְשׁ֣וֹן אֶפְעֶֽה׃
He will not look on the streams, the rivers, the torrents of honey and curds.
אַל־יֵ֥רֶא בִפְלַגּ֑וֹת נַהֲרֵ֥י נַ֝חֲלֵ֗י דְּבַ֣שׁ וְחֶמְאָֽה׃
He will give back what he toiled for and not swallow it; he will not enjoy the profit of his trading.[^5]
מֵשִׁ֣יב יָ֭גָע וְלֹ֣א יִבְלָ֑ע כְּחֵ֥יל תְּ֝מוּרָת֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲלֹֽס׃
For he has crushed and abandoned the poor; he has seized a house that he did not build.
כִּֽי־רִ֭צַּץ עָזַ֣ב דַּלִּ֑ים בַּ֥יִת גָּ֝זַ֗ל וְלֹ֣א יִבֶנֵֽהוּ׃
Because his greed knew no rest,[^6] he will not escape with anything he desired.
כִּ֤י ׀ לֹא־יָדַ֣ע שָׁלֵ֣ו בְּבִטְנ֑וֹ בַּ֝חֲמוּד֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּֽט׃
Nothing was left that he did not devour; that is why his prosperity will not last.
אֵין־שָׂרִ֥יד לְאָכְל֑וֹ עַל־כֵּ֝֗ן לֹא־יָחִ֥יל טוּבֽוֹ׃
In the fullness of his plenty he will be in distress; the full force of misery will come upon him.[^7]
בִּמְלֹ֣אות שִׂ֭פְקוֹ יֵ֣צֶר ל֑וֹ כָּל־יַ֖ד עָמֵ֣ל תְּבוֹאֶֽנּוּ׃
When he has filled his belly, God[^8] will send his burning anger against him and rain it down on him as his food.[^9]
יְהִ֤י ׀ לְמַלֵּ֬א בִטְנ֗וֹ יְֽשַׁלַּח־בּ֭וֹ חֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ וְיַמְטֵ֥ר עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ בִּלְחוּמֽוֹ׃
He may flee from an iron weapon, but a bronze arrow[^10] will pierce him.
יִ֭בְרַח מִנֵּ֣שֶׁק בַּרְזֶ֑ל תַּ֝חְלְפֵ֗הוּ קֶ֣שֶׁת נְחוּשָֽׁה׃
He pulls it out, and it comes out of his back, the glittering point[^11] out of his gall; terrors come upon him.
שָׁלַף֮ וַיֵּצֵ֢א מִגֵּ֫וָ֥ה וּ֭בָרָק מִֽמְּרֹרָת֥וֹ יַהֲלֹ֗ךְ עָלָ֥יו אֵמִֽים׃
Total darkness lies in wait for his treasures. A fire not fanned by anyone will consume him; it will devour what is left in his tent.
כָּל־חֹשֶׁךְ֮ טָמ֢וּן לִצְפּ֫וּנָ֥יו תְּ֭אָכְלֵהוּ אֵ֣שׁ לֹֽא־נֻפָּ֑ח יֵ֖רַע שָׂרִ֣יד בְּאָהֳלֽוֹ׃
The heavens will reveal his guilt, and the earth will rise up against him.
יְגַלּ֣וּ שָׁמַ֣יִם עֲוֺנ֑וֹ וְ֝אֶ֗רֶץ מִתְקוֹמָ֘מָ֥ה לֽוֹ׃
The produce of his house will be carried off, flowing away on the day of God's anger.[^12]
יִ֭גֶל יְב֣וּל בֵּית֑וֹ נִ֝גָּר֗וֹת בְּי֣וֹם אַפּֽוֹ׃
This is the portion of the wicked from God, the inheritance appointed for him by God."[^13]
זֶ֤ה ׀ חֵֽלֶק־אָדָ֣ם רָ֭שָׁע מֵאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְנַחֲלַ֖ת אִמְר֣וֹ מֵאֵֽל׃ פ

n.1: Literally "because of my haste within me".
n.2: Or "and my understanding inspires me to answer".
n.3: Or "The poor will crush his children". The verb *yeratsu* may come from *ratsah*, "seek favor", or *ratsats*, "crush".
n.4: Literally "the gall of cobras is within him".
n.5: Literally "according to the wealth of his exchange, and he will not rejoice". The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.
n.6: Literally "Because he did not know quiet in his belly".
n.7: Literally "every hand of the wretched will come upon him". The same consonants can be read *amal*, "misery", for *amel*, "the wretched".
n.8: Literally "he". God is meant.
n.9: Hebrew *bilchumo*, a word of uncertain meaning: perhaps "as his food" or "into his flesh".
n.10: Literally "a bow of bronze".
n.11: Literally "the lightning", that is, the flashing arrowhead.
n.12: Literally "his anger". Or "A flood will carry off his house, torrents on the day of his anger".
n.13: Literally "the inheritance of his word (or decree) from God". The first line has *Elohim*, the second *El*.

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Listen carefully to my words, and let this be the comfort you give me.
שִׁמְע֣וּ שָׁ֭מוֹעַ מִלָּתִ֑י וּתְהִי־זֹ֝֗את תַּנְח֥וּמֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃
Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken, mock on.[^1]
שָׂ֭אוּנִי וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְאַחַ֖ר דַּבְּרִ֣י תַלְעִֽיג׃
As for me, is my complaint against a human being? Why should I not be impatient?[^2]
הֶ֭אָנֹכִי לְאָדָ֣ם שִׂיחִ֑י וְאִם־מַ֝דּ֗וּעַ לֹא־תִקְצַ֥ר רוּחִֽי׃
Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.
פְּנוּ־אֵלַ֥י וְהָשַׁ֑מּוּ וְשִׂ֖ימוּ יָ֣ד עַל־פֶּֽה׃
When I think about it I am terrified, and trembling seizes my body.
וְאִם־זָכַ֥רְתִּי וְנִבְהָ֑לְתִּי וְאָחַ֥ז בְּ֝שָׂרִ֗י פַּלָּצֽוּת׃
Why do the wicked live on, grow old, and even grow mighty in power?
מַדּ֣וּעַ רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִחְי֑וּ עָ֝תְק֗וּ גַּם־גָּ֥בְרוּ חָֽיִל׃
Their offspring are established in their presence, and their descendants before their eyes.
זַרְעָ֤ם נָכ֣וֹן לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם עִמָּ֑ם וְ֝צֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֗ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃
Their houses are safe from fear, and the rod of God[^3] is not upon them.
בָּתֵּיהֶ֣ם שָׁל֣וֹם מִפָּ֑חַד וְלֹ֤א שֵׁ֖בֶט אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
Their bull breeds without fail; their cow gives birth and does not miscarry.
שׁוֹר֣וֹ עִ֭בַּר וְלֹ֣א יַגְעִ֑ל תְּפַלֵּ֥ט פָּ֝רָת֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א תְשַׁכֵּֽל׃
They send out their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.
יְשַׁלְּח֣וּ כַ֭צֹּאן עֲוִילֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝יַלְדֵיהֶ֗ם יְרַקֵּדֽוּן׃
They sing to the tambourine and the lyre, and rejoice to the sound of the pipe.
יִ֭שְׂאוּ כְּתֹ֣ף וְכִנּ֑וֹר וְ֝יִשְׂמְח֗וּ לְק֣וֹל עוּגָֽב׃
They spend their days in prosperity,[^4] and go down to Sheol[^5] in an instant.[^6]
*יבלו **יְכַלּ֣וּ בַטּ֣וֹב יְמֵיהֶ֑ם וּ֝בְרֶ֗גַע שְׁא֣וֹל יֵחָֽתּוּ׃
Yet they say to God, 'Leave us alone! We do not want to know your ways.
וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לָ֭אֵל ס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְדַ֥עַת דְּ֝רָכֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א חָפָֽצְנוּ׃
Who is the Almighty,[^7] that we should serve him? What would we gain if we prayed to him?'
מַה־שַׁדַּ֥י כִּֽי־נַֽעַבְדֶ֑נּוּ וּמַה־נּ֝וֹעִ֗יל כִּ֣י נִפְגַּע־בּֽוֹ׃
Look, their prosperity is not in their own hands.[^8] The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
הֵ֤ן לֹ֣א בְיָדָ֣ם טוּבָ֑ם עֲצַ֥ת רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים רָ֣חֲקָה מֶֽנִּי׃
How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? How often does disaster come upon them? How often does he deal out pains[^9] in his anger?
כַּמָּ֤ה ׀ נֵר־רְשָׁ֘עִ֤ים יִדְעָ֗ךְ וְיָבֹ֣א עָלֵ֣ימוֹ אֵידָ֑ם חֲ֝בָלִ֗ים יְחַלֵּ֥ק בְּאַפּֽוֹ׃
How often are they like straw before the wind, like chaff that the storm carries away?
יִהְי֗וּ כְּתֶ֥בֶן לִפְנֵי־ר֑וּחַ וּ֝כְמֹ֗ץ גְּנָבַ֥תּוּ סוּפָֽה׃
God stores up his punishment for his children?[^10] Let him repay the man himself, so that he knows it!
אֱל֗וֹהַּ יִצְפֹּן־לְבָנָ֥יו אוֹנ֑וֹ יְשַׁלֵּ֖ם אֵלָ֣יו וְיֵדָֽע׃
Let his own eyes[^11] see his ruin, and let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
יִרְא֣וּ *עינו **עֵינָ֣יו כִּיד֑וֹ וּמֵחֲמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יִשְׁתֶּֽה׃
For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has been cut off?
כִּ֤י מַה־חֶפְצ֣וֹ בְּבֵית֣וֹ אַחֲרָ֑יו וּמִסְפַּ֖ר חֳדָשָׁ֣יו חֻצָּֽצוּ׃
Can anyone teach God knowledge, since he judges even those on high?
הַלְאֵ֥ל יְלַמֶּד־דָּ֑עַת וְ֝ה֗וּא רָמִ֥ים יִשְׁפּֽוֹט׃
One person dies in full vigor, completely at ease and secure.
זֶ֗ה יָ֭מוּת בְּעֶ֣צֶם תֻּמּ֑וֹ כֻּ֝לּ֗וֹ שַׁלְאֲנַ֥ן וְשָׁלֵֽיו׃
His pails are full of milk,[^12] and the marrow of his bones is moist.
עֲ֭טִינָיו מָלְא֣וּ חָלָ֑ב וּמֹ֖חַ עַצְמוֹתָ֣יו יְשֻׁקֶּֽה׃
Another dies with a bitter soul, never having tasted anything good.
וְזֶ֗ה יָ֭מוּת בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ מָרָ֑ה וִ[t]לֹֽא־אָ֝כַ֗ל בַּטּוֹבָֽה׃
They lie down alike in the dust, and worms cover them both.
יַ֭חַד עַל־עָפָ֣ר יִשְׁכָּ֑בוּ וְ֝רִמָּ֗ה תְּכַסֶּ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
Look, I know your thoughts, the schemes by which you would wrong me.
הֵ֣ן יָ֭דַעְתִּי מַחְשְׁבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וּ֝מְזִמּ֗וֹת עָלַ֥י תַּחְמֹֽסוּ׃
For you say, 'Where is the house of the noble? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?'
כִּ֤י תֹֽאמְר֗וּ אַיֵּ֥ה בֵית־נָדִ֑יב וְ֝אַיֵּ֗ה אֹ֤הֶל ׀ מִשְׁכְּנ֬וֹת רְשָׁעִֽים׃
Have you not asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their accounts,[^13]
הֲלֹ֣א שְׁ֭אֶלְתֶּם ע֣וֹבְרֵי דָ֑רֶךְ וְ֝אֹתֹתָ֗ם לֹ֣א תְנַכֵּֽרוּ׃
that the wicked are spared on the day of disaster, and are rescued on the day of wrath?[^14]
כִּ֤י לְי֣וֹם אֵ֭יד יֵחָ֣שֶׂךְ רָ֑ע לְי֖וֹם עֲבָר֣וֹת יוּבָֽלוּ׃
Who denounces his way to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?
מִֽי־יַגִּ֣יד עַל־פָּנָ֣יו דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְהֽוּא־עָ֝שָׂ֗ה מִ֣י יְשַׁלֶּם־לֽוֹ׃
He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
וְ֭הוּא לִקְבָר֣וֹת יוּבָ֑ל וְֽעַל־גָּדִ֥ישׁ יִשְׁקֽוֹד׃
The clods of the valley are sweet to him. All humankind follows after him, and those who went before him are without number.
מָֽתְקוּ־ל֗וֹ רִגְבֵ֫י נָ֥חַל וְ֭אַחֲרָיו כָּל־אָדָ֣ם יִמְשׁ֑וֹךְ וּ֝לְפָנָ֗יו אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר׃
How then can you comfort me with empty words?[^15] Nothing is left of your answers but falsehood."
וְ֭אֵיךְ תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי הָ֑בֶל וּ֝תְשׁ֥וּבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם נִשְׁאַר־מָֽעַל׃ ס

n.1: The Hebrew "you" is singular here, though plural in verse 2.
n.2: Literally "Why should my spirit not be short?"
n.3: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 19.
n.4: The Hebrew text is written "they wear out their days" but read "they complete their days".
n.5: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.6: That is, quickly, without a long illness. Or "in peace".
n.7: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verse 20.
n.8: Or "Is not their prosperity in their own hands?" The Hebrew of this verse is difficult.
n.9: Hebrew *chavalim*, "pains", especially of labor. Or "portions", measured out by a cord.
n.10: Job seems to quote the friends' view (compare 5:4; 20:10). Many translations add "You say". Literally "God stores up his iniquity for his children".
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "his eye" but read "his eyes".
n.12: Hebrew *atinav*, a word found only here. Perhaps "his pails" or "his loins"; with different vowels, "full of fat" (*chelev*) instead of "full of milk" (*chalav*).
n.13: Literally "their signs".
n.14: Or "that the wicked are kept for the day of disaster, and brought to the day of wrath".
n.15: Literally "with breath". Hebrew *hevel*.

v: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Can a man be of use to God? Even a wise man is of use only to himself.
הַלְאֵ֥ל יִסְכָּן־גָּ֑בֶר כִּֽי־יִסְכֹּ֖ן עָלֵ֣ימוֹ מַשְׂכִּֽיל׃
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty[^1] if you are righteous? Is it any gain to him if you make your ways blameless?
הַחֵ֣פֶץ לְ֭שַׁדַּי כִּ֣י תִצְדָּ֑ק וְאִם־בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי־תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ׃
Is it because of your fear of God[^2] that he rebukes you and enters into judgment with you?
הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ יֹכִיחֶ֑ךָ יָב֥וֹא עִ֝מְּךָ֗ בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?
הֲלֹ֣א רָעָֽתְךָ֣ רַבָּ֑ה וְאֵֽין־קֵ֝֗ץ לַעֲוֺנֹתֶֽיךָ׃
For you took pledges from your brothers for no reason[^3] and stripped the naked of their clothing.
כִּֽי־תַחְבֹּ֣ל אַחֶ֣יךָ חִנָּ֑ם וּבִגְדֵ֖י עֲרוּמִּ֣ים תַּפְשִֽׁיט׃
You gave no water to the weary to drink, and you withheld bread from the hungry,
לֹא־מַ֭יִם עָיֵ֣ף תַּשְׁקֶ֑ה וּ֝מֵרָעֵ֗ב תִּֽמְנַֽע־לָֽחֶם׃
while the man with power owned the land, and the man of rank lived in it.[^4]
וְאִ֣ישׁ זְ֭רוֹעַ ל֣וֹ הָאָ֑רֶץ וּנְשׂ֥וּא פָ֝נִ֗ים יֵ֣שֶׁב בָּֽהּ׃
You sent widows away empty-handed, and the arms of orphans were crushed.
אַ֭לְמָנוֹת שִׁלַּ֣חְתָּ רֵיקָ֑ם וּזְרֹע֖וֹת יְתֹמִ֣ים יְדֻכָּֽא׃
That is why snares are all around you, and sudden dread terrifies you,
עַל־כֵּ֭ן סְבִיבוֹתֶ֣יךָ פַחִ֑ים וִֽ֝יבַהֶלְךָ פַּ֣חַד פִּתְאֹֽם׃
or darkness, so that you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
אוֹ־חֹ֥שֶׁךְ לֹֽא־תִרְאֶ֑ה וְֽשִׁפְעַת־מַ֥יִם תְּכַסֶּֽךָּ׃
Is not God[^5] in the height of heaven? See the highest stars, how lofty they are!
הֲ‍ֽלֹא־אֱ֭לוֹהַּ גֹּ֣בַהּ שָׁמָ֑יִם וּרְאֵ֤ה רֹ֖[t]אשׁ כּוֹכָבִ֣ים כִּי־רָֽמּוּ׃
Yet you say, 'What does God know? Can he judge through thick darkness?
וְֽ֭אָמַרְתָּ מַה־יָּ֣דַֽע אֵ֑ל הַבְעַ֖ד עֲרָפֶ֣ל יִשְׁפּֽוֹט׃
Thick clouds veil him, so that he does not see, as he walks on the vault of heaven.'
עָבִ֣ים סֵֽתֶר־ל֭וֹ וְלֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֑ה וְח֥וּג שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם יִתְהַלָּֽךְ׃
Will you keep to the ancient path that wicked men have walked,
הַאֹ֣רַח עוֹלָ֣ם תִּשְׁמֹ֑ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר דָּרְכ֣וּ מְתֵי־אָֽוֶן׃
who were snatched away before their time, whose foundations were washed away by a river?[^6]
אֲשֶֽׁר־קֻמְּט֥וּ וְלֹא־עֵ֑ת נָ֝הָ֗ר יוּצַ֥ק יְסוֹדָֽם׃
They said to God, 'Leave us alone!' and 'What can the Almighty do to us?'[^7]
הָאֹמְרִ֣ים לָ֭אֵל ס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וּמַה־יִּפְעַ֖ל שַׁדַּ֣י לָֽמוֹ׃
Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things. But the counsel of the wicked is far from me.[^8]
וְה֤וּא מִלֵּ֣א בָתֵּיהֶ֣ם ט֑וֹב וַעֲצַ֥ת רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים רָ֣חֲקָה מֶֽנִּי׃
The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them:
יִרְא֣וּ צַדִּיקִ֣ים וְיִשְׂמָ֑חוּ וְ֝נָקִ֗י יִלְעַג־לָֽמוֹ׃
'Surely our adversaries[^9] are cut off, and fire has consumed what they left.'
אִם־לֹ֣א נִכְחַ֣ד קִימָ֑נוּ וְ֝יִתְרָ֗ם אָ֣כְלָה אֵֽשׁ׃
Come to terms with him,[^10] and be at peace; in this way good will come to you.
הַסְכֶּן־נָ֣א עִמּ֑וֹ וּשְׁלם[c] בָּ֝הֶ֗ם תְּֽבוֹאַתְךָ֥ טוֹבָֽה׃
Accept instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.
קַח־נָ֣א מִפִּ֣יו תּוֹרָ֑ה וְשִׂ֥ים אֲ֝מָרָ֗יו בִּלְבָבֶֽךָ׃
If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored.[^11] If you remove injustice far from your tents,
אִם־תָּשׁ֣וּב עַד־שַׁ֭דַּי תִּבָּנֶ֑ה תַּרְחִ֥יק עַ֝וְלָ֗ה מֵאָהֳלֶֽךָ׃
if you lay your gold[^12] in the dust, the gold of Ophir[^13] among the stones of the wadis,
וְשִׁית־עַל־עָפָ֥ר בָּ֑צֶר וּ[t]בְצ֖וּר נְחָלִ֣ים אוֹפִֽיר׃
then the Almighty will be your gold and your choicest silver.[^14]
וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ וְכֶ֖סֶף תּוֹעָפ֣וֹת לָֽ[t]ךְ׃
For then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
כִּי־אָ֭ז עַל־שַׁדַּ֣י תִּתְעַנָּ֑ג וְתִשָּׂ֖א אֶל־אֱל֣וֹהַּ פָּנֶֽיךָ׃
You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
תַּעְתִּ֣יר אֵ֭לָיו וְיִשְׁמָעֶ֑ךָּ וּנְדָרֶ֥יךָ תְשַׁלֵּֽם׃
You will decide on a matter, and it will be done for you, and light will shine on your ways.
וְֽתִגְזַר־א֖[d]וֹמֶר וְיָ֣קָם לָ֑ךְ וְעַל־דְּ֝רָכֶ֗יךָ נָ֣גַֽהּ אֽ[t]וֹר׃
When people are brought low, and you say, 'Lift them up!' he will save the downcast.[^15]
כִּֽי־הִ֭שְׁפִּילוּ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּוָ֑ה וְשַׁ֖ח עֵינַ֣יִם יוֹשִֽׁעַ׃
He will rescue even someone who is not innocent;[^16] he will be rescued through the cleanness of your hands."
יְ[t]מַלֵּ֥ט אִֽי־נָקִ֑י וְ֝נִּמְלַ֗ט בְּבֹ֣ר כַּפֶּֽיךָ׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verses 17, 23, 25 and 26.
n.2: Literally "your fear".
n.3: Hebrew *chinnam*, the word in 1:9 and 2:3.
n.4: Literally "the man of arm, the land is his, and the lifted of face lives in it". Eliphaz may mean Job himself.
n.5: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 26.
n.6: Literally "a river was poured out on their foundation". Some see here an allusion to the flood (Genesis 6–8).
n.7: Literally "to them".
n.8: Eliphaz repeats Job's words in 21:16.
n.9: Hebrew *qimanu*, a word found only here, probably "those who rise against us".
n.10: Hebrew *hasken*, the verb translated "be of use" in verse 2.
n.11: Literally "you will be built up".
n.12: Hebrew *betser*, "precious ore". Also in verse 25.
n.13: A land famous for its fine gold, probably in southern Arabia or East Africa.
n.14: Literally "silver of heaps (or peaks)". Hebrew *to'afot*, a word of uncertain meaning.
n.15: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Literally "When they make low, and you say 'Lifting up!', and the lowly of eyes he will save".
n.16: Hebrew *i-naqi*, "not innocent", a rare form. Some take it as "the innocent".

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Even today my complaint is defiant;[^1] the hand on me is heavy in spite of my groaning.[^2]
גַּם־הַ֭יּוֹם מְרִ֣י שִׂחִ֑י יָ֝דִ֗י כָּבְדָ֥ה עַל־אַנְחָתִֽ[t]י׃
If only I knew where to find him, so that I could come to his dwelling place![^3]
מִֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן יָ֭דַעְתִּי וְאֶמְצָאֵ֑הוּ אָ֝ב֗וֹא עַד־תְּכוּנָתֽ[t]וֹ׃
I would set out my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
אֶעֶרְכָ֣ה לְפָנָ֣יו מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝פִ֗י אֲמַלֵּ֥א תוֹכָחֽ[t]וֹת׃
I would learn the words he would answer me, and understand what he would say to me.
אֵ֭דְעָה מִלִּ֣ים יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְ֝אָבִ֗ינָה מַה־יֹּ֥אמַר לִֽי׃
Would he contend with me with his great power? No, he would surely pay attention to me.[^4]
הַבְּרָב־כֹּ֭חַ יָרִ֣יב עִמָּדִ֑י לֹ֥א אַךְ־ה֝֗וּא יָשִׂ֥ם בִּֽי׃
There an upright person could reason with him, and I would escape from my judge forever.[^5]
שָׁ֗ם יָ֭שָׁר נוֹכָ֣ח עִמּ֑וֹ וַאֲפַלְּטָ֥ה לָ֝נֶ֗צַח מִשֹּׁפְטִֽי׃
Look, I go forward, and he is not there; backward, and I do not perceive him.[^6]
הֵ֤ן קֶ֣דֶם אֶהֱלֹ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְ֝אָח֗וֹר וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃
When he is at work on the left, I cannot catch hold of him;[^7] he turns aside to the right,[^8] and I do not see him.
שְׂמֹ֣אול בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ וְלֹא־אָ֑חַז יַעְטֹ֥ף יָ֝מִ֗ין וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶֽה׃
But he knows the way I take.[^9] When he has tested me, I will come out like gold.
כִּֽי־יָ֭דַע דֶּ֣רֶךְ עִמָּדִ֑י בְּ֝חָנַ֗נִי כַּזָּהָ֥ב אֵצֵֽא׃
My foot has held fast to his steps; I have kept to his way and have not turned aside.
בַּ֭אֲשֻׁרוֹ אָחֲזָ֣ה רַגְלִ֑י דַּרְכּ֖וֹ שָׁמַ֣רְתִּי וְלֹא־אָֽט׃
I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily food.[^10]
מִצְוַ֣ת שְׂ֭פָתָיו וְלֹ֣א אָמִ֑ישׁ מֵ֝חֻקִּ֗י צָפַ֥נְתִּי אִמְרֵי־פִֽיו׃
But he is one,[^11] and who can turn him back? What he desires, he does.[^12]
וְה֣וּא בְ֭אֶחָד וּמִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ אִוְּתָ֣ה וַיָּֽעַשׂ׃
For he will carry out what he has decreed for me,[^13] and he has many such things in mind.[^14]
כִּ֭י יַשְׁלִ֣ים חֻקִּ֑י וְכָהֵ֖נָּה רַבּ֣וֹת עִמּֽוֹ׃
That is why I am terrified in his presence; when I think about it, I am in dread of him.
עַל־כֵּ֭ן מִפָּנָ֣יו אֶבָּהֵ֑ל אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן וְאֶפְחַ֥ד מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
God has made my heart faint; the Almighty[^15] has terrified me.
וְ֭אֵל הֵרַ֣ךְ לִבִּ֑י וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י הִבְהִילָֽנִי׃
Yet I have not been silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.[^16]
כִּֽי־לֹ֣א נִ֭צְמַתִּי מִפְּנֵי־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וּ֝מִפָּנַ֗י כִּסָּה־אֹֽפֶל׃

n.1: Hebrew *meri*, "rebellion, defiance".
n.2: Literally "my hand is heavy on my groaning". *My hand* may mean the blow that has fallen on me (compare 19:21). Or "I hold down my groaning with a heavy hand". The Greek Septuagint reads "his hand".
n.3: Hebrew *tekhunah*, "his fixed place": his seat or throne.
n.4: Literally "No, only he would set (his mind) on me".
n.5: That is, from his charges against me. Or "I would be acquitted by my judge forever".
n.6: Or "east … west". The Hebrew words for "forward" and "backward" also mean "east" and "west", and "left" and "right" in verse 9 also mean "north" and "south": Job searches in every direction.
n.7: Literally "and I do not grasp".
n.8: Or "he hides himself on the right".
n.9: Literally "the way with me".
n.10: Literally "more than my portion". Hebrew *chuqqi*, "what is allotted to me", probably food (compare Proverbs 30:8). The Greek Septuagint reads "in my bosom".
n.11: Literally "he is in one": he is unique, or unchanging, or of one mind. Some scholars read *bachar*, "he has chosen", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.12: Literally "His soul desires, and he does it".
n.13: Literally "he completes my decree". Hebrew *chuqqi*, the word in verse 12.
n.14: Literally "and like these, many are with him".
n.15: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.16: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Literally "For I have not been silenced (or destroyed) before darkness, and from my face he has covered thick darkness". Or "For I was not cut off before the darkness came, and he did not hide the thick darkness from me".

v: "Why are times not stored up by the Almighty?[^1] Why do those who know him[^2] never see his days?[^3]
מַדּ֗וּעַ מִ֭שַׁדַּי[t] לֹא־נִצְפְּנ֣וּ עִתִּ֑ים *וידעו **וְ֝יֹדְעָ֗יו לֹא־חָ֥זוּ יָמָֽיו׃
Some move boundary stones;[^4] they seize flocks and pasture them.
גְּבֻל֥וֹת יַשִּׂ֑יגוּ עֵ֥דֶר גָּ֝זְל֗וּ וַיִּרְעֽוּ׃
They drive away the orphans' donkey; they take the widow's ox as a pledge.[^5]
חֲמ֣וֹר יְתוֹמִ֣ים יִנְהָ֑גוּ יַ֝חְבְּל֗וּ שׁ֣וֹר אַלְמָנָֽה׃
They push the needy off the road; the poor of the land all hide themselves together.
יַטּ֣וּ אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים מִדָּ֑רֶךְ יַ֥חַד חֻ֝בְּא֗וּ עֲנִיֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃
Look, like wild donkeys in the wilderness, they go out to their work, searching for food;[^6] the desert gives them bread for their children.[^7]
הֵ֤ן פְּרָאִ֨ים ׀ בַּ֥מִּדְבָּ֗ר יָצְא֣וּ בְּ֭פָעֳלָם מְשַׁחֲרֵ֣י לַטָּ֑רֶף עֲרָבָ֥ה ל֥וֹ לֶ֝֗חֶם לַנְּעָרִֽים׃
They harvest fodder[^8] in the field, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
בַּ֭שָּׂדֶה בְּלִיל֣וֹ *יקצירו **יִקְצ֑וֹרוּ וְכֶ֖רֶם רָשָׁ֣ע יְלַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃
They spend the night naked, without clothing; they have no covering in the cold.
עָר֣וֹם יָ֭לִינוּ מִבְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת בַּקָּרָֽה׃
They are drenched by the mountain downpours; with no shelter, they hug the rock.
מִזֶּ֣רֶם הָרִ֣ים יִרְטָ֑בוּ וּֽמִבְּלִ֥י מַ֝חְסֶ֗ה חִבְּקוּ־צֽוּר׃
Some snatch the orphan from the breast,[^9] and they take pledges from the poor.[^10]
יִ֭גְזְלוּ מִשֹּׁ֣ד יָת֑וֹם וְֽעַל־עָנִ֥י יַחְבֹּֽלוּ׃
They go about naked, without clothing; hungry, they carry the sheaves.
עָר֣וֹם הִ֭לְּכוּ בְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וּ֝רְעֵבִ֗ים נָ֣שְׂאוּ עֹֽמֶר׃
Between their terraces[^11] they press out oil; they tread the winepresses, yet they are thirsty.
בֵּין־שׁוּרֹתָ֥ם יַצְהִ֑ירוּ יְקָבִ֥ים דָּ֝רְכ֗וּ וַיִּצְמָֽאוּ׃
From the city men groan,[^12] and the wounded[^13] cry for help, yet God[^14] does not count it as wrong.[^15]
מֵ֘עִ֤יר מְתִ֨ים ׀ יִנְאָ֗קוּ וְנֶֽפֶשׁ־חֲלָלִ֥ים תְּשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וֶ֝אֱל֗וֹהַּ לֹא־יָשִׂ֥ים תִּפְלָֽה׃
These are among those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways, and they do not stay in its paths.
הֵ֤מָּה ׀ הָיוּ֮ בְּֽמֹרְדֵ֫י־א֥וֹר לֹֽא־הִכִּ֥ירוּ דְרָכָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יָ֝שְׁב֗וּ בִּנְתִיבֹתָֽיו׃
The murderer rises at daybreak;[^16] he kills the poor and the needy, and in the night he is like a thief.
לָא֡וֹר יָ֘ק֤וּם רוֹצֵ֗חַ יִֽקְטָל־עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְי֑וֹן וּ֝בַלַּ֗יְלָה יְהִ֣י כַגַּנָּֽב׃
The eye of the adulterer watches for the twilight. He says, 'No eye will see me,' and he puts a covering over his face.
וְעֵ֤ין נֹאֵ֨ף ׀ שָׁ֤מְרָֽה נֶ֣שֶׁף לֵ֭אמֹר לֹא־תְשׁוּרֵ֣נִי עָ֑יִן וְסֵ֖תֶר פָּנִ֣ים יָשִֽׂים׃
In the dark they break into houses;[^17] by day they shut themselves in; they do not know the light.
חָתַ֥ר בַּחֹ֗שֶׁךְ בָּ֫תִּ֥ים יוֹמָ֥ם חִתְּמוּ־לָ֗מוֹ לֹא־יָ֥דְּעוּ אֽוֹר׃
For to all of them the morning is deep darkness,[^18] for they are well acquainted with the terrors of deep darkness.[^19]
כִּ֤י יַחְדָּ֨ו ׀ בֹּ֣קֶר לָ֣מוֹ צַלְמָ֑וֶת כִּֽי־יַ֝כִּ֗יר בַּלְה֥וֹת צַלְמָֽוֶת׃
He is swift on the surface of the waters;[^20] their portion in the land is cursed; he does not turn toward the vineyards.[^21]
קַֽל־ה֤וּא ׀ עַל־פְּנֵי־מַ֗יִם תְּקֻלַּ֣ל חֶלְקָתָ֣ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ לֹֽא־יִ֝פְנֶה דֶּ֣רֶךְ כְּרָמִֽים׃
Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters; so does Sheol[^22] those who have sinned.
צִיָּ֤ה גַם־חֹ֗ם יִגְזְל֥וּ מֵֽימֵי־שֶׁ֗לֶג שְׁא֣וֹל חָטָֽאוּ׃
The womb forgets him; the worm feeds on him with relish;[^23] he is remembered no more, and wickedness is broken like a tree.
יִשְׁכָּ֘חֵ֤הוּ רֶ֨חֶם ׀ מְתָ֘ק֤וֹ רִמָּ֗ה ע֥וֹד לֹֽא־יִזָּכֵ֑ר וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֖ר כָּעֵ֣ץ עַוְלָֽה׃
He feeds on[^24] the barren woman who bears no child, and does no good to the widow.
רֹעֵ֣[t]ה עֲ֭קָרָה לֹ֣א תֵלֵ֑ד וְ֝אַלְמָנָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְיֵטִֽיב׃
Yet by his power he prolongs the life of the mighty;[^25] they rise up when they had no hope of living.[^26]
וּמָשַׁ֣ךְ אַבִּירִ֣ים בְּכֹח֑וֹ יָ֝ק֗וּם וְֽלֹא־יַאֲמִ֥ין בַּֽחַיִּֽין׃
He lets them rest secure,[^27] and they are supported, and his eyes are on their ways.
יִתֶּן־ל֣וֹ לָ֭בֶטַח וְיִשָּׁעֵ֑ן וְ֝עֵינֵ֗יהוּ עַל־דַּרְכֵיהֶֽם׃
They are exalted for a little while, and then they are gone. They are brought low and gathered up like everyone else;[^28] they are cut off like the heads of grain.
ר֤וֹמּוּ מְּעַ֨ט ׀ וְֽאֵינֶ֗נּוּ וְֽהֻמְּכ֗וּ כַּכֹּ֥ל יִקָּפְצ֑וּן וּכְרֹ֖אשׁ שִׁבֹּ֣לֶת יִמָּֽלוּ׃
If it is not so, who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?"
וְאִם־לֹ֣א אֵ֭פוֹ מִ֣י יַכְזִיבֵ֑נִי וְיָשֵׂ֥ם לְ֝אַ֗ל מִלָּתִֽי׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. The *times* are probably times of judgment, when God would call the wicked to account.
n.2: The Hebrew text is written "and they know" but read "and those who know him".
n.3: That is, the days when he judges.
n.4: Literally "They move boundaries". The subject is not stated; the wicked are meant. Boundary stones marked a family's land (Deuteronomy 19:14).
n.5: A pledge was something taken as security for a debt (compare Deuteronomy 24:17).
n.6: Literally "seeking early for prey". From here to verse 8, *they* are the poor of verse 4.
n.7: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "the desert, to him, bread for the young ones".
n.8: Hebrew *belilo*, "his fodder", perhaps the wicked man's. Some scholars divide the word as *beli lo*, "not his": "they reap in a field that is not theirs".
n.9: Literally "They snatch the orphan from the breast": the wicked, as in verses 2–4.
n.10: Literally "and against the poor they take pledges".
n.11: Hebrew *shurot*, "walls" or "rows": perhaps the terrace walls of olive groves, or rows of olive trees.
n.12: Or "the dying groan": the same Hebrew consonants read with different vowels.
n.13: Literally "the soul of the wounded".
n.14: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.15: Hebrew *tiflah*, "what is unfitting", the word in 1:22. The same consonants can be read *tefillah*, "prayer": "yet God does not heed their prayer".
n.16: Literally "at the light". Some take it to mean "before the light" or "at dusk". Some scholars read *lo or*, "when there is no light", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.17: Literally "he digs through houses", through their walls of mud brick.
n.18: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death". Also later in the verse.
n.19: Literally "for he recognizes the terrors of deep darkness".
n.20: Verses 18–24 describe the swift end of the wicked, as the friends do (compare 18:5–21 and 20:4–29), though Job has just said that God does not call them to account (verses 1 and 12; 21:7–34). Interpreters explain this in different ways: Job is quoting the friends' view in order to reject it (verse 25), or wishing it were true ("Let him be swift …"), or these verses belong to a speech of Bildad or Zophar in this third round of speeches (see the note at 25:1). The Hebrew has no marker, and they are translated here as they stand, as part of Job's speech. The picture in this line is of the wicked man swept away like foam on the water.
n.21: Literally "he does not turn the way of the vineyards": he will not go out to enjoy them.
n.22: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.24: Literally "He grazes on", that is, he devours what she has.
n.25: Literally "he draws out the mighty by his power". *He* is probably God, as in verse 23, though the Hebrew does not say. Or "he drags away the mighty by his power", of the wicked man.
n.26: Literally "he rises and does not believe in life".
n.28: Literally "like all". The Greek Septuagint reads "like mallow (in the heat)", a plant that wilts quickly.

v: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:[^1]
וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשֻּׁחִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Dominion and dread are his; he makes peace in his high places.[^2]
הַמְשֵׁ֣ל וָפַ֣חַד עִמּ֑וֹ עֹשֶׂ֥ה שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם בִּמְרוֹמָֽיו׃
Can his troops be counted?[^3] On whom does his light not rise?
הֲיֵ֣שׁ מִ֭סְפָּר לִגְדוּדָ֑יו וְעַל־מִ֝֗י לֹא־יָק֥וּם אוֹרֵֽהוּ׃
How then can a mortal be in the right before God? How can one born of a woman be pure?[^4]
וּמַה־יִּצְדַּ֣ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם־אֵ֑ל וּמַה־יִּ֝זְכֶּ֗ה יְל֣וּד אִשָּֽׁה׃
Look, even the moon is not bright,[^5] and the stars are not pure in his eyes;
הֵ֣ן עַד־יָ֭רֵחַ וְלֹ֣א יַאֲהִ֑יל וְ֝כוֹכָבִ֗ים לֹא־זַכּ֥וּ בְעֵינָֽיו׃
how much less a mortal, who is a maggot, and a human being,[^6] who is a worm!"
אַ֭ף כִּֽי־אֱנ֣וֹשׁ רִמָּ֑ה וּבֶן־אָ֝דָ֗ם תּוֹלֵעָֽה׃ פ

n.1: Bildad's third speech is very short, and Zophar, who spoke after Bildad in the first two rounds of speeches (chapters 11 and 20), has no third speech. Many interpreters think that parts of chapters 24–27 have been moved from their original speakers: some, for example, give 26:5–14 to Bildad and 27:13–23 to Zophar. The text is translated here as it stands.
n.2: Literally "Ruling and dread are with him". *His high places* are the heavens.
n.3: Literally "Is there a number to his troops?": probably the stars, or the heavenly beings who serve him.
n.4: Compare Eliphaz's words in 4:17–19 and 15:14–16.
n.5: Literally "Look, as far as the moon, and it does not shine". Hebrew *ya'ahil*, a verb found only here, probably "shine".
n.6: Literally "a son of *adam*", that is, of humankind.

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"How you have helped the powerless![^1] How you have saved the arm that has no strength!
מֶה־עָזַ֥רְתָּ לְלֹא־כֹ֑חַ ה֝וֹשַׁ֗עְתָּ זְר֣וֹעַ לֹא־עֹֽז׃
How you have counseled one who has no wisdom, and what a wealth of sound wisdom[^2] you have made known!
מַה־יָּ֭עַצְתָּ לְלֹ֣א חָכְמָ֑ה וְ֝תוּשִׁיָּ֗ה לָרֹ֥ב הוֹדָֽעְתָּ׃
With whose help have you uttered these words?[^3] Whose breath[^4] has come out of you?
אֶת־מִ֭י הִגַּ֣דְתָּ מִלִּ֑ין וְנִשְׁמַת־מִ֝י יָצְאָ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ׃
The shades of the dead[^5] writhe beneath the waters, and so do those who live in them.
הָרְפָאִ֥ים יְחוֹלָ֑לוּ מִתַּ֥חַת מַ֝֗יִם וְשֹׁכְנֵיהֶֽם׃
Sheol[^6] is naked before him, and Abaddon[^7] has no covering.
עָר֣וֹם שְׁא֣וֹל נֶגְדּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָֽאֲבַדּֽוֹן׃
He stretches out the north over empty space[^8] and hangs the earth on nothing.
נֹטֶ֣ה צָפ֣וֹן עַל־תֹּ֑הוּ תֹּ֥לֶה אֶ֝֗רֶץ עַל־בְּלִי־מָֽה׃
He wraps up the waters in his clouds, and the cloud does not burst under them.
צֹרֵֽר־מַ֥יִם בְּעָבָ֑יו וְלֹא־נִבְקַ֖ע עָנָ֣ן תַּחְתָּֽם׃
He covers the face of his throne,[^9] spreading his cloud over it.
מְאַחֵ֥ז פְּנֵי־כִסֵּ֑ה פַּרְשֵׁ֖ז עָלָ֣יו עֲנָנֽוֹ׃
He has marked out a circle on the face of the waters,[^10] at the boundary between light and darkness.
חֹֽק־חָ֭ג עַל־פְּנֵי־מָ֑יִם עַד־תַּכְלִ֖ית א֣וֹר עִם־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
The pillars of heaven tremble and are astounded at his rebuke.
עַמּוּדֵ֣י שָׁמַ֣יִם יְרוֹפָ֑פוּ וְ֝יִתְמְה֗וּ מִגַּעֲרָתֽוֹ׃
By his power he stilled[^11] the sea; by his understanding he shattered Rahab.[^12]
בְּ֭כֹחוֹ רָגַ֣ע הַיָּ֑ם *ובתובנתו **וּ֝בִתְבוּנָת֗וֹ מָ֣חַץ רָֽהַב׃
By his breath[^13] the heavens became clear; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.[^14]
בְּ֭רוּחוֹ שָׁמַ֣יִם שִׁפְרָ֑ה חֹֽלֲלָ֥ה יָ֝ד֗וֹ נָחָ֥שׁ בָּרִֽיחַ׃
Look, these are only the edges of his ways;[^15] how faint is the whisper we hear of him![^16] But the thunder of his mighty deeds,[^17] who can understand?"
הֶן־אֵ֤לֶּה ׀ קְצ֬וֹת *דרכו **דְּרָכָ֗יו וּמַה־שֵּׁ֣מֶץ דָּ֭בָר נִשְׁמַע־בּ֑וֹ וְרַ֥עַם *גבורתו **גְּ֝בוּרוֹתָ֗יו מִ֣י יִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃ ס

n.1: Job is being sarcastic. In verses 2–4, *you* is singular: Job speaks to Bildad.
n.2: Hebrew *tushiyyah*, "sound wisdom", as in 5:12.
n.3: Literally "Whom have you told words?": either "To whom" or "With whose help".
n.4: Or "Whose spirit". Hebrew *neshamah*.
n.5: Hebrew *repha'im*, the dead in the world below (Psalm 88:11 (88:10 in most English Bibles); Isaiah 14:9). Some interpreters think verses 5–14 belong to Bildad's speech in chapter 25 (see the note at 25:1).
n.6: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.7: Hebrew *Abaddon*, "Destruction", a name for the realm of the dead (28:22; 31:12; Proverbs 15:11).
n.8: Hebrew *tohu*, "emptiness, formlessness", the word in Genesis 1:2. *The north* (Hebrew *tsafon*) may be the northern sky, or the mountain of the gods in the far north (compare Isaiah 14:13).
n.9: Hebrew *kisseh*, a spelling of *kisse*, "throne". The same consonants can be read *keseh*, "full moon": "He covers the face of the full moon".
n.10: Literally "He has circled a limit on the face of the waters". The horizon is pictured as a circle drawn on the waters at the edge of the world (compare Proverbs 8:27).
n.11: Or "he stirred up". The Hebrew verb *raga* can mean either.
n.12: A sea monster, a figure of chaos (see 9:13).
n.13: Or "By his wind". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.14: Or "the gliding serpent". Isaiah 27:1 uses the same words of Leviathan.
n.15: The Hebrew text is written "his way" but read "his ways".
n.16: Literally "how small a whisper of a word is heard of him".
n.17: The Hebrew text is written "his might" but read "his mighty deeds".

v: Job took up his discourse again:[^1]
וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"As surely as God lives, who has denied me justice,[^2] and the Almighty,[^3] who has made my soul bitter,
חַי אֵ֭ל הֵסִ֣יר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י הֵמַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃
as long as my breath is in me, and the breath of God[^4] is in my nostrils,
כִּֽי־כָל־ע֣וֹד נִשְׁמָתִ֣י בִ֑י וְר֖וּחַ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּאַפִּֽי׃
my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.[^5]
אִם־תְּדַבֵּ֣רְנָה שְׂפָתַ֣י עַוְלָ֑ה וּ֝לְשׁוֹנִ֗י אִם־יֶהְגֶּ֥ה רְמִיָּֽה׃
Far be it from me to declare that you are right![^6] Until I breathe my last, I will not give up my integrity.
חָלִ֣ילָה לִּי֮ אִם־אַצְדִּ֢יק אֶ֫תְכֶ֥ם עַד־אֶגְוָ֑ע לֹא־אָסִ֖יר תֻּמָּתִ֣י מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
I hold fast to my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
בְּצִדְקָתִ֣י הֶ֭חֱזַקְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אַרְפֶּ֑הָ לֹֽא־יֶחֱרַ֥ף לְ֝בָבִ֗י מִיָּמָֽי׃
May my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who rises against me like the unjust.
יְהִ֣י כְ֭רָשָׁע אֹ֣יְבִ֑י וּמִתְקוֹמְמִ֥י כְעַוָּֽל׃
For what hope does the godless have when he is cut off,[^7] when God takes away his life?[^8]
כִּ֤י מַה־תִּקְוַ֣ת חָ֭נֵף כִּ֣י יִבְצָ֑ע כִּ֤י יֵ֖שֶׁל אֱל֣וֹהַּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
Will God hear his cry when trouble comes upon him?
הַֽ֭צַעֲקָתוֹ יִשְׁמַ֥ע ׀ אֵ֑ל כִּֽי־תָב֖וֹא עָלָ֣יו צָרָֽה׃
Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at all times?
אִם־עַל־שַׁדַּ֥י יִתְעַנָּ֑ג יִקְרָ֖א אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּכָל־עֵֽת׃
I will teach you about the power[^9] of God; I will not hide what is with the Almighty.
אוֹרֶ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֣ם בְּיַד־אֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י לֹ֣א אֲכַחֵֽד׃
Look, all of you have seen it yourselves. Why then do you talk such empty nonsense?[^10]
הֵן־אַתֶּ֣ם כֻּלְּכֶ֣ם חֲזִיתֶ֑ם וְלָמָּה־זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל תֶּהְבָּֽלוּ׃
This is the portion of a wicked person from God, the inheritance that the ruthless receive from the Almighty:[^11]
זֶ֤ה ׀ חֵֽלֶק־אָדָ֖ם רָשָׁ֥ע ׀ עִם־אֵ֑ל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת עָ֝רִיצִ֗ים מִשַׁדַּ֥י יִקָּֽחוּ׃
If his children are many, it is for the sword, and his offspring will not have enough bread.
אִם־יִרְבּ֣וּ בָנָ֣יו לְמוֹ־חָ֑רֶב וְ֝צֶאֱצָאָ֗יו לֹ֣א יִשְׂבְּעוּ־לָֽחֶם׃
Those who survive him[^12] will be buried by the plague,[^13] and his widows will not weep.[^14]
*שרידו **שְׂ֭רִידָיו בַּמָּ֣וֶת יִקָּבֵ֑רוּ וְ֝אַלְמְנֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּֽינָה׃
Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay,
אִם־יִצְבֹּ֣ר כֶּעָפָ֣ר כָּ֑סֶף וְ֝כַחֹ֗מֶר יָכִ֥ין מַלְבּֽוּשׁ׃
he may pile it up, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
יָ֭כִין וְצַדִּ֣יק יִלְבָּ֑שׁ וְ֝כֶ֗סֶף נָקִ֥י יַחֲלֹֽק׃
He builds his house like a moth,[^15] like a hut that a watchman makes.
בָּנָ֣ה כָעָ֣שׁ בֵּית֑וֹ וּ֝כְסֻכָּ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה נֹצֵֽר׃
He lies down rich, but will not do so again;[^16] he opens his eyes, and it is gone.[^17]
עָשִׁ֣יר יִ֭שְׁכַּב וְלֹ֣א יֵאָסֵ֑ף עֵינָ֖יו פָּקַ֣ח וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃
Terrors overtake him like a flood;[^18] in the night a storm wind carries him off.
תַּשִּׂיגֵ֣הוּ כַ֭מַּיִם בַּלָּה֑וֹת לַ֝֗יְלָה גְּנָבַ֥תּוּ סוּפָֽה׃
The east wind lifts him up, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
יִשָּׂאֵ֣הוּ קָדִ֣ים וְיֵלַ֑ךְ וִֽ֝ישָׂעֲרֵ֗הוּ מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃
It hurls itself at him without pity;[^19] he flees headlong from its power.
וְיַשְׁלֵ֣ךְ עָ֭לָיו וְלֹ֣א יַחְמֹ֑ל מִ֝יָּד֗וֹ בָּר֥וֹחַ יִבְרָֽח׃
It claps its hands at him and hisses at him from its place.[^20]
יִשְׂפֹּ֣ק עָלֵ֣ימוֹ כַפֵּ֑ימוֹ וְיִשְׁרֹ֥ק עָ֝לָ֗יו מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃

n.1: Literally "And Job again lifted up his *mashal* and said". Hebrew *mashal* usually means a proverb or a poem; here, a solemn speech. Also in 29:1. This new heading, at the point where Zophar would be expected to speak, is one reason some think the order of this third round of speeches has been disturbed (see the note at 25:1).
n.2: Literally "who has taken away my justice". Hebrew *mishpat*: justice, the right owed to me in my case. *As surely as God lives* is the form of an oath (literally "God lives").
n.3: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verses 10, 11 and 13.
n.4: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verses 8 and 10. *Breath* is Hebrew *ruach*, "breath, spirit".
n.5: Literally "if my lips speak wickedness, if my tongue utters deceit …", the form of a solemn oath: "may God punish me if I do".
n.6: Literally "to declare you righteous". Here *you* is plural: Job speaks to the three friends.
n.7: Hebrew *yivtsa*, "he cuts off" or "he makes gain". Or "however much he has gained".
n.8: Literally "when God draws out his soul". Hebrew *yeshel*, a rare verb, perhaps "draws out" or "takes away".
n.9: Literally "the hand".
n.10: Literally "Why then do you become empty with emptiness?" Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor": what has no substance.
n.11: Compare Zophar's words in 20:29. Some interpreters think verses 13–23 are Zophar's third speech, which is otherwise missing (see the note at 25:1). Others take them as Job turning his friends' teaching back on them, or as Job's own view of what the wicked deserve. In the Hebrew text they stand within Job's speech.
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "his survivor" but read "his survivors".
n.13: Literally "will be buried in death". *Death* here probably means plague (compare Jeremiah 15:2).
n.14: Perhaps because no proper mourning rites can be held (compare Psalm 78:64).
n.15: Hebrew *ash*, "moth", perhaps meaning its cocoon.
n.16: Literally "he will not be gathered". The Greek Septuagint reads "he will not add (to it)", that is, he lies down rich for the last time.
n.17: Literally "and he is not": either his wealth is gone, or he himself.
n.18: Literally "like waters".
n.19: Or "He (God) hurls at him without pity". The subject is not stated.
n.20: Clapping the hands and hissing were gestures of scorn (Lamentations 2:15). The subject may be the wind, or people who see his fall: "People clap their hands at him and hiss at him from his place".

v: "Surely there is a mine for silver,[^1] and a place for the gold that people refine.
כִּ֤י יֵ֣שׁ לַכֶּ֣סֶף מוֹצָ֑א וּ֝מָק֗וֹם לַזָּהָ֥ב יָזֹֽקּוּ׃
Iron is taken from the dust, and copper[^2] is smelted from stone.
בַּ֭רְזֶל מֵעָפָ֣ר יֻקָּ֑ח וְ֝אֶ֗בֶן יָצ֥וּק נְחוּשָֽׁה׃
People put an end to darkness;[^3] they search out the farthest limits, for the stone that lies in gloom and deep darkness.[^4]
קֵ֤ץ ׀ שָׂ֤ם לַחֹ֗שֶׁךְ וּֽלְכָל־תַּ֭כְלִית ה֣וּא חוֹקֵ֑ר אֶ֖בֶן אֹ֣פֶל וְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃
They open a shaft far from where anyone lives, in places forgotten by any foot; far from other people they dangle and sway.[^5]
פָּ֤רַץ נַ֨חַל ׀ מֵֽעִם־גָּ֗ר הַֽנִּשְׁכָּחִ֥ים מִנִּי־רָ֑גֶל דַּ֖לּוּ מֵאֱנ֣וֹשׁ נָֽעוּ׃
The earth, from which bread comes, is turned upside down beneath, as if by fire.[^6]
אֶ֗רֶץ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יֵֽצֵא־לָ֑חֶם וְ֝תַחְתֶּ֗יהָ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ כְּמוֹ־אֵֽשׁ׃
Its stones are the place of sapphires,[^7] and it holds dust of gold.[^8]
מְקוֹם־סַפִּ֥יר אֲבָנֶ֑יהָ וְעַפְרֹ֖ת זָהָ֣ב לֽוֹ׃
No bird of prey knows that path; the falcon's eye has not seen it.
נָ֭תִיב לֹֽא־יְדָ֣עוֹ עָ֑יִט וְלֹ֥א שְׁ֝זָפַ֗תּוּ עֵ֣ין אַיָּֽה׃
Proud beasts[^9] have not trodden it; no lion has passed over it.
לֹֽא־הִדְרִיכֻ֥הוּ בְנֵי־שָׁ֑חַץ לֹֽא־עָדָ֖ה עָלָ֣יו שָֽׁחַל׃
People put their hand to the flint and overturn mountains from their roots.
בַּֽ֭חַלָּמִישׁ שָׁלַ֣ח יָד֑וֹ הָפַ֖ךְ מִשֹּׁ֣רֶשׁ הָרִֽים׃
They cut channels[^10] through the rocks, and their eyes see every precious thing.
בַּ֭צּוּרוֹת יְאֹרִ֣ים בִּקֵּ֑עַ וְכָל־יְ֝קָ֗ר רָאֲתָ֥ה עֵינֽוֹ׃
They dam up the sources of the rivers[^11] and bring hidden things out into the light.
מִ֭בְּכִי נְהָר֣וֹת חִבֵּ֑שׁ וְ֝תַעֲלֻמָ֗הּ יֹ֣צִא אֽוֹר׃ פ
But wisdom, where can it be found? Where is the place of understanding?
וְֽ֭הַחָכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תִּמָּצֵ֑א וְאֵ֥י זֶ֝ה מְק֣וֹם בִּינָֽה׃
No mortal knows its worth;[^12] it is not found in the land of the living.
לֹא־יָדַ֣ע אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עֶרְכָּ֑הּ וְלֹ֥א תִ֝מָּצֵ֗א בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הֽ͏ַחַיִּֽים׃
The deep[^13] says, 'It is not in me,' and the sea says, 'It is not with me.'
תְּה֣וֹם אָ֭מַר לֹ֣א בִי־הִ֑יא וְיָ֥ם אָ֝מַ֗ר אֵ֣ין עִמָּדִֽי׃
It cannot be bought with solid gold,[^14] and its price cannot be weighed out in silver.
לֹא־יֻתַּ֣ן סְג֣וֹר תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יִ֝שָּׁקֵ֗ל כֶּ֣סֶף מְחִירָֽהּ׃
It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir,[^15] in precious onyx[^16] or sapphire.
לֹֽא־תְ֭סֻלֶּה בְּכֶ֣תֶם אוֹפִ֑יר בְּשֹׁ֖הַם יָקָ֣ר וְסַפִּֽיר׃
Gold and glass[^17] cannot compare with it, nor can it be exchanged for vessels of fine gold.
לֹא־יַעַרְכֶ֣נָּה זָ֭הָב וּזְכוֹכִ֑ית וּתְמ֖וּרָתָ֣הּ כְּלִי־פָֽז׃
Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is above pearls.[^18]
רָאמ֣וֹת וְ֭גָבִישׁ לֹ֣א יִזָּכֵ֑ר וּמֶ֥שֶׁךְ חָ֝כְמָ֗ה מִפְּנִינִֽים׃
The topaz of Cush[^19] cannot compare with it; it cannot be valued in pure gold.
לֹֽא־יַ֭עַרְכֶנָּה פִּטְדַת־כּ֑וּשׁ בְּכֶ֥תֶם טָ֝ה֗וֹר לֹ֣א תְסֻלֶּֽה׃ פ
Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
וְֽ֭הַחָכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תָּב֑וֹא וְאֵ֥י זֶ֝֗ה מְק֣וֹם בִּינָֽה׃
It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, concealed even from the birds of the sky.
וְֽ֭נֶעֶלְמָה מֵעֵינֵ֣י כָל־חָ֑י וּמֵע֖וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם נִסְתָּֽרָה׃
Abaddon[^20] and Death say, 'With our ears we have heard a rumor of it.'
אֲבַדּ֣וֹן וָ֭מָוֶת אָ֣מְר֑וּ בְּ֝אָזְנֵ֗ינוּ שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ שִׁמְעָֽהּ׃
God understands the way to it; he knows its place.
אֱ֭לֹהִים הֵבִ֣ין דַּרְכָּ֑הּ וְ֝ה֗וּא יָדַ֥ע אֶת־מְקוֹמָֽהּ׃
For he looks to the ends of the earth; he sees everything under the heavens.
כִּי־ה֭וּא לִקְצוֹת־הָאָ֣רֶץ יַבִּ֑יט תַּ֖חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם יִרְאֶֽה׃
When he gave the wind its weight and measured out the waters,
לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָר֣וּחַ מִשְׁקָ֑ל וּ֝מַ֗יִם תִּכֵּ֥ן בְּמִדָּֽה׃
when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,[^21]
בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ לַמָּטָ֣ר חֹ֑ק וְ֝דֶ֗רֶךְ לַחֲזִ֥יז קֹלֽוֹת׃
then he saw it and declared it;[^22] he established it and searched it out.
אָ֣ז רָ֭אָהּ וַֽיְסַפְּרָ֑הּ הֱ֝כִינָ֗הּ וְגַם־חֲקָרָֽהּ׃
And he said to humankind, 'Look, the fear of the Lord,[^23] that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.'"[^24]
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר ׀ לָֽאָדָ֗ם הֵ֤ן יִרְאַ֣ת אֲ֭דֹנָי הִ֣יא חָכְמָ֑ה וְס֖וּר מֵרָ֣ע בִּינָֽה׃ ס

n.1: Chapter 28 is a poem on wisdom. It has no heading of its own, so in the text as it stands it continues Job's speech from chapter 27 (compare 29:1). Its calm, reflective tone has led many interpreters to think of it as an independent poem, perhaps spoken by the narrator. *Mine* is literally "a place where it comes out" (Hebrew *motsa*).
n.2: Or "bronze". Hebrew *nechushah*.
n.3: Literally "He sets an end to darkness": the miner, who brings light into the dark.
n.4: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.5: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Literally "He breaks open a wadi away from the sojourner; the ones forgotten by the foot, they hang low; away from mortals they sway". It probably describes miners lowered on ropes into the shafts.
n.6: Perhaps the fire used to crack rock in mining.
n.7: Hebrew *sappir*, probably lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone flecked with gold. Also in verse 16.
n.8: Or "and it (the sapphire) has flecks of gold".
n.9: Literally "the sons of pride", probably the great wild animals (compare 41:26 (41:34 in most English Bibles)).
n.10: Hebrew *ye'orim*, a word used of the channels of the Nile; here tunnels or water channels in a mine.
n.11: The Hebrew vowel points read "From the weeping of the rivers he binds", that is, he stops the water from seeping into the mine. The same consonants can be read "the sources of the rivers" (compare "the springs of the sea", 38:16).
n.12: Or "its place in order". The Greek Septuagint reads "its way".
n.13: Hebrew *tehom*, the deep waters under the earth (Genesis 1:2).
n.14: Hebrew *segor*, a rare word for gold, probably "pure" or "solid" gold. Verses 15–19 use several words for gold and precious stones, some of which cannot be identified with certainty.
n.15: A region famous for its fine gold, perhaps in southern Arabia or East Africa (1 Kings 9:28).
n.16: Hebrew *shoham*, a precious stone that cannot be identified with certainty.
n.17: Hebrew *zekhukhit*, a word found only here. Glass was costly in the ancient world.
n.18: Hebrew *ramot*, *gavish* and *peninim*, precious things that cannot be identified with certainty. *Peninim* may be red coral (Lamentations 4:7) or pearls. *Price* is literally "drawing out", perhaps the acquiring of it.
n.19: Hebrew *pitdah*, a precious stone, perhaps topaz or chrysolite. *Cush* is usually the region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia).
n.20: Hebrew *Abaddon*, "Destruction", a name for the realm of the dead (see 26:6).
n.21: Literally "for the flash of the thunders".
n.23: Hebrew *Adonai*, "Lord", used of God only here in Job.
n.24: The words echo the description of Job in 1:1: he "feared God and turned away from evil". Compare Proverbs 1:7; 9:10.

v: Job took up his discourse again:[^1]
וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"If only I were as in the months gone by, as in the days when God[^2] watched over me,
מִֽי־יִתְּנֵ֥נִי כְיַרְחֵי־קֶ֑דֶם כִּ֝ימֵ֗י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יִשְׁמְרֵֽנִי׃
when his lamp shone above my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;
בְּהִלּ֣וֹ נֵ֭רוֹ עֲלֵ֣י רֹאשִׁ֑י לְ֝אוֹרוֹ אֵ֣לֶךְ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
as I was in the days of my prime,[^3] when the friendship[^4] of God was over my tent;
כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הָ֭יִיתִי בִּימֵ֣י חָרְפִּ֑י בְּס֥וֹד אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ עֲלֵ֣י אָהֳלִֽי׃
when the Almighty[^5] was still with me, and my children[^6] were all around me;
בְּע֣וֹד שַׁ֭דַּי עִמָּדִ֑י סְבִ֖יבוֹתַ֣י נְעָרָֽי׃
when my steps were bathed in cream,[^7] and the rock poured out streams of oil for me!
בִּרְחֹ֣ץ הֲלִיכַ֣י בְּחֵמָ֑ה וְצ֥וּר יָצ֥וּק עִ֝מָּדִ֗י פַּלְגֵי־שָֽׁמֶן׃
When I went out to the gate of the city[^8] and set up my seat in the square,
בְּצֵ֣אתִי שַׁ֣עַר עֲלֵי־קָ֑רֶת בָּ֝רְח֗וֹב אָכִ֥ין מוֹשָׁבִֽי׃
the young men saw me and drew back,[^9] and the old men rose and stood;
רָא֣וּנִי נְעָרִ֣ים וְנֶחְבָּ֑אוּ וִֽ֝ישִׁישִׁים קָ֣מוּ עָמָֽדוּ׃
officials stopped talking[^10] and put their hands over their mouths;
שָׂ֭רִים עָצְר֣וּ בְמִלִּ֑ים וְ֝כַ֗ף יָשִׂ֥ימוּ לְפִיהֶֽם׃
the voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.
קוֹל־נְגִידִ֥ים נֶחְבָּ֑אוּ וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם לְחִכָּ֥ם דָּבֵֽקָה׃
For any ear that heard me called me blessed, and any eye that saw me spoke well of me,[^11]
כִּ֤י אֹ֣זֶן שָׁ֭מְעָה וַֽתְּאַשְּׁרֵ֑נִי וְעַ֥ין רָ֝אֲתָ֗ה וַתְּעִידֵֽנִי׃
because I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the orphan who had no one to help him.
כִּֽי־אֲ֭מַלֵּט עָנִ֣י מְשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וְ֝יָת֗וֹם וְֽלֹא־עֹזֵ֥ר לֽוֹ׃
The blessing of the one who was perishing came upon me, and I made the widow's heart sing for joy.
בִּרְכַּ֣ת אֹ֭בֵד עָלַ֣י תָּבֹ֑א וְלֵ֖ב אַלְמָנָ֣ה אַרְנִֽן׃
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me;[^12] my justice was like a robe and a turban.
צֶ֣דֶק לָ֭בַשְׁתִּי וַיִּלְבָּשֵׁ֑נִי כִּֽמְעִ֥יל וְ֝צָנִ֗יף מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
עֵינַ֣יִם הָ֭יִיתִי לַֽעִוֵּ֑ר וְרַגְלַ֖יִם לַפִּסֵּ֣חַ אָֽנִי׃
I was a father to the needy, and I looked into the case of the stranger.[^13]
אָ֣ב אָ֭נֹכִֽי לָֽאֶבְיוֹנִ֑ים וְרִ֖ב לֹא־יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶחְקְרֵֽהוּ׃
I broke the jaws of the unjust and made them drop their prey from their teeth.
וָֽ֭אֲשַׁבְּרָה מְתַלְּע֣וֹת עַוָּ֑ל וּ֝מִשִּׁנָּ֗יו אַשְׁלִ֥יךְ טָֽרֶף׃
Then I thought, 'I will die in my nest,[^14] and I will multiply my days like the sand.[^15]
וָ֭אֹמַר עִם־קִנִּ֣י אֶגְוָ֑ע וְ֝כַח֗וֹל אַרְבֶּ֥ה יָמִֽים׃
My roots will be open to the water, and the dew will lie all night on my branches.
שָׁרְשִׁ֣י פָת֣וּחַ אֱלֵי־מָ֑יִם וְ֝טַ֗ל יָלִ֥ין בִּקְצִירֽ͏ִי׃
My glory will stay fresh with me,[^16] and my bow will be renewed in my hand.'
כְּ֭בוֹדִי חָדָ֣שׁ עִמָּדִ֑י וְ֝קַשְׁתִּ֗י בְּיָדִ֥י תַחֲלִֽיף׃
People listened to me and waited; they kept silent for my counsel.
לִֽי־שָׁמְע֥וּ וְיִחֵ֑לּוּ וְ֝יִדְּמ֗וּ לְמ֣וֹ עֲצָתִֽי׃
After I had spoken, they did not speak again; my words fell on them drop by drop.[^17]
אַחֲרֵ֣י דְ֭בָרִי לֹ֣א יִשְׁנ֑וּ וְ֝עָלֵ֗ימוֹ תִּטֹּ֥ף מִלָּתִֽי׃
They waited for me as for the rain; they opened their mouths as for the spring rain.[^18]
וְיִֽחֲל֣וּ כַמָּטָ֣ר לִ֑י וּ֝פִיהֶ֗ם פָּעֲר֥וּ לְמַלְקֽוֹשׁ׃
When I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it;[^19] they did not let the light of my face fall.[^20]
אֶשְׂחַ֣ק אֲ֭לֵהֶם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ינוּ וְא֥וֹר פָּ֝נַ֗י לֹ֣א יַפִּילֽוּן׃
I chose the way for them and sat as their chief; I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.
אֶֽבֲחַ֣ר דַּרְכָּם֮ וְאֵשֵׁ֢ב רֹ֥אשׁ וְ֭אֶשְׁכּוֹן כְּמֶ֣לֶךְ בַּגְּד֑וּד כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲבֵלִ֣ים יְנַחֵֽם׃

n.1: Literally "And Job again lifted up his *mashal* and said" (see 27:1).
n.2: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 4.
n.3: Literally "the days of my autumn", the season of harvest and fullness.
n.4: Hebrew *sod*, "intimate counsel, close friendship".
n.5: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.6: Or "my young men", "my servants". Hebrew *ne'arim*, as in 1:19.
n.7: Hebrew *chemah*, "curds, butter": a picture of great abundance.
n.8: Literally "to the gate, up to the city". Elders sat at the city gate to hear cases and give judgment.
n.9: Literally "hid themselves".
n.10: Literally "held back words".
n.11: Literally "testified for me".
n.12: Literally "and it clothed itself with me".
n.13: Literally "and the case I did not know I searched out": either the case of someone I did not know, or a case I did not yet understand.
n.14: That is, at home among my family.
n.15: Or "like the phoenix". Hebrew *chol* usually means "sand", but an ancient Jewish tradition takes it here as the name of a long-lived bird, the phoenix.
n.16: Literally "My glory is new with me". Hebrew *kavod*: honor, dignity, vigor.
n.17: Literally "and my word dripped on them", like rain.
n.18: The late rain of spring, which ripened the crops before harvest.
n.19: Literally "I laughed toward them; they did not believe". Or "I smiled at them when they had lost confidence".
n.20: The meaning of this line is uncertain. Perhaps "they did not cast down the light of my face", that is, they did nothing to lose my favor.

v: "But now they laugh at me, those younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with the dogs of my flock.
וְעַתָּ֤ה ׀ שָֽׂחֲק֣וּ עָלַי֮ צְעִירִ֥ים מִמֶּ֗נִּי לְיָ֫מִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־מָאַ֥סְתִּי אֲבוֹתָ֑ם לָ֝שִׁ֗ית עִם־כַּלְבֵ֥י צֹאנִֽי׃
What use to me was the strength of their hands? Their vigor[^1] had perished.
גַּם־כֹּ֣חַ יְ֭דֵיהֶם לָ֣מָּה לִּ֑י עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ אָ֣בַד כָּֽלַח׃
Gaunt from want and hunger, they gnaw the dry ground,[^2] in the gloom of desolation and waste.[^3]
בְּחֶ֥סֶר וּבְכָפָ֗ן גַּ֫לְמ֥וּד הַֽעֹרְקִ֥ים צִיָּ֑ה אֶ֝֗מֶשׁ שׁוֹאָ֥ה וּמְשֹׁאָֽה׃
They pluck saltwort[^4] among the bushes, and the root of the broom bush is their food.[^5]
הַקֹּטְפִ֣ים מַלּ֣וּחַ עֲלֵי־שִׂ֑יחַ וְשֹׁ֖רֶשׁ רְתָמִ֣ים לַחְמָֽם׃
They are driven out from the community;[^6] people shout after them as after a thief.
מִן־גֵּ֥ו יְגֹרָ֑שׁוּ יָרִ֥יעוּ עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ כַּגַּנָּֽב׃
They have to live in the gullies of the wadis, in holes in the ground and among the rocks.
בַּעֲר֣וּץ נְחָלִ֣ים לִשְׁכֹּ֑ן חֹרֵ֖י עָפָ֣ר וְכֵפִֽים׃
Among the bushes they bray;[^7] under the nettles they huddle together.
בֵּין־שִׂיחִ֥ים יִנְהָ֑קוּ תַּ֖חַת חָר֣וּל יְסֻפָּֽחוּ׃
A senseless brood, a nameless brood,[^8] they were whipped out of the land.
בְּֽנֵי־נָ֭בָל גַּם־בְּנֵ֣י בְלִי־שֵׁ֑ם נִ֝כְּא֗וּ מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
And now I have become their song;[^9] I have become a byword to them.
וְ֭עַתָּה נְגִינָתָ֣ם הָיִ֑יתִי וָאֱהִ֖י לָהֶ֣ם לְמִלָּֽה׃
They detest me; they keep their distance from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
תִּֽ֭עֲבוּנִי רָ֣חֲקוּ מֶ֑נִּי וּ֝מִפָּנַ֗י לֹא־חָ֥שְׂכוּ רֹֽק׃
Because he has loosened my cord[^10] and humbled me, they have thrown off all restraint before me.[^11]
כִּֽי־*יתרו **יִתְרִ֣י פִ֭תַּח וַיְעַנֵּ֑נִי וְ֝רֶ֗סֶן מִפָּנַ֥י שִׁלֵּֽחוּ׃
On my right the rabble[^12] rise up; they push my feet away[^13] and build their roads of ruin against me.[^14]
עַל־יָמִין֮ פִּרְחַ֢ח יָ֫ק֥וּמוּ רַגְלַ֥י שִׁלֵּ֑חוּ וַיָּסֹ֥לּוּ עָ֝לַ֗י אָרְח֥וֹת אֵידָֽם׃
They tear up my path; they profit from my disaster;[^15] no one holds them back.[^16]
נָתְס֗וּ נְֽתִיבָ֫תִ֥י לְהַוָּתִ֥י יֹעִ֑ילוּ לֹ֖א עֹזֵ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃
As through a wide breach they come; amid the crash[^17] they roll in.
כְּפֶ֣רֶץ רָחָ֣ב יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ תַּ֥חַת שֹׁ֝אָ֗ה הִתְגַּלְגָּֽלוּ׃
Terrors are turned against me; they chase away my dignity[^18] like the wind, and my safety has passed away like a cloud.
הָהְפַּ֥ךְ עָלַ֗י בַּלָּ֫ה֥וֹת תִּרְדֹּ֣ף כָּ֭רוּחַ נְדִבָתִ֑י וּ֝כְעָ֗ב עָבְרָ֥ה יְשֻׁעָתִֽי׃
And now my life is poured out within me;[^19] days of affliction have taken hold of me.
וְעַתָּ֗ה עָ֭לַי תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ נַפְשִׁ֑י יֹ֭אחֲז֣וּנִי יְמֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
At night my bones are pierced within me,[^20] and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
לַ֗יְלָה עֲ֭צָמַי נִקַּ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְ֝עֹרְקַ֗י לֹ֣א יִשְׁכָּבֽוּן׃
With great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.[^21]
בְּרָב־כֹּ֭חַ יִתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ לְבוּשִׁ֑י כְּפִ֖י כֻתָּנְתִּ֣י יַֽאַזְרֵֽנִי׃
He has thrown me into the mud,[^22] and I have become like dust and ashes.[^23]
הֹרָ֥נִי לַחֹ֑מֶר וָ֝אֶתְמַשֵּׁ֗ל כֶּעָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר׃
I cry to you for help, but you do not answer me; I stand up, and you just look at me.[^24]
אֲשַׁוַּ֣ע אֵ֭לֶיךָ וְלֹ֣א תַעֲנֵ֑נִי עָ֝מַ֗דְתִּי וַתִּתְבֹּ֥נֶן בִּֽי׃
You have turned cruel to me; with the might of your hand you attack me.[^25]
תֵּהָפֵ֣ךְ לְאַכְזָ֣ר לִ֑י בְּעֹ֖צֶם יָדְךָ֣ תִשְׂטְמֵֽנִי׃
You lift me up on the wind and make me ride it; you melt me away, and all my success.[^26]
תִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי אֶל־ר֖[d]וּחַ תַּרְכִּיבֵ֑נִי וּ֝תְמֹגְגֵ֗נִי *תשוה **תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃
For I know you will bring me back to death,[^27] to the house appointed for all the living.
כִּֽי־יָ֭דַעְתִּי מָ֣וֶת תְּשִׁיבֵ֑נִי וּבֵ֖ית מוֹעֵ֣ד לְכָל־חָֽי׃
Yet does not one in ruins stretch out a hand, and in his disaster cry for help?[^28]
אַ֣ךְ לֹא־בְ֭עִי יִשְׁלַח־יָ֑ד אִם־בְּ֝פִיד֗וֹ לָהֶ֥ן שֽׁוּעַ׃
Did I not weep for the one whose life was hard?[^29] Was my soul not grieved for the needy?
אִם־לֹ֣א בָ֭כִיתִי לִקְשֵׁה־י֑וֹם עָֽגְמָ֥ה נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י לָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃
Yet when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness came.
כִּ֤י ט֣וֹב קִ֭וִּיתִי וַיָּ֣בֹא רָ֑ע וַֽאֲיַחֲלָ֥ה לְ֝א֗וֹר וַיָּ֥בֹא אֹֽפֶל׃
My insides are in turmoil and never still;[^30] days of affliction confront me.
מֵעַ֖י רֻתְּח֥וּ וְלֹא־דָ֗מּוּ קִדְּמֻ֥נִי יְמֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
I go about darkened, but not by the sun;[^31] I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
קֹדֵ֣ר הִ֭לַּכְתִּי בְּלֹ֣א חַמָּ֑ה קַ֖מְתִּי בַקָּהָ֣ל אֲשַׁוֵּֽעַ׃
I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.[^32]
אָ֭ח הָיִ֣יתִי לְתַנִּ֑ים וְ֝רֵ֗עַ לִבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃
My skin has turned black and peels from me;[^33] my bones burn with fever.[^34]
ע֭וֹרִי שָׁחַ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְעַצְמִי־חָ֝֗רָה מִנִּי־חֹֽרֶב׃
My lyre is turned to mourning, and my pipe to the sound of weeping.
וַיְהִ֣י לְ֭אֵבֶל כִּנֹּרִ֑י וְ֝עֻגָבִ֗י לְק֣וֹל בֹּכִֽים׃

n.1: Hebrew *kelach*, a rare word, perhaps "full vigor" or "ripe old age", as in 5:26.
n.2: Or "they flee to the dry ground". Hebrew *orqim*, a rare word.
n.3: Literally "the yesterday (or "night") of ruin and devastation". The meaning of this line is uncertain.
n.4: Hebrew *malluach*, a salty plant that grows in the desert.
n.5: Literally "their bread". Broom roots are bitter and were mostly used as fuel (Psalm 120:4). The same consonants can be read "to warm themselves".
n.6: Literally "from the midst". Hebrew *gev*, a rare word.
n.7: Like hungry wild donkeys (compare 6:5).
n.8: Literally "sons of a fool, also sons of no name".
n.9: That is, a mocking song.
n.10: *He* is God, though the Hebrew does not name him. *My cord* is perhaps my bowstring (compare 29:20) or my tent cord (compare 4:21). The Hebrew text is written "his cord" but read "my cord". With "his cord", the line may mean "each of them has loosened his cord (his restraint) and humbled me".
n.11: Literally "they have let loose the bridle before me".
n.12: Hebrew *pirchach*, a word found only here, perhaps "brood" or "rabble".
n.13: Literally "they send away my feet". The meaning is uncertain.
n.14: Like an army building siege ramps against a city (19:12).
n.15: Literally "they help toward my disaster".
n.16: Literally "there is no helper for them": perhaps "they need no one's help". The meaning is uncertain.
n.17: Hebrew *sho'ah*, "ruin, storm", the word translated "desolation" in verse 3.
n.18: Hebrew *nedivah*, "nobility, honor".
n.19: Literally "my soul pours itself out upon me".
n.20: Literally "The night pierces my bones from upon me".
n.21: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. *Is disfigured* is literally "disguises itself". Some scholars read "seizes my garment", with a small change to the Hebrew, with God as the subject: "With great force he seizes my garment; he grips me by the collar of my tunic".
n.23: The same pair of words, "dust and ashes", is used in 42:6 (compare Genesis 18:27).
n.25: Hebrew *satam*, "bear a grudge against, persecute", a verb close to *satan*, "accuser".
n.26: The Hebrew text is written *teshuwwah*, "(in) the roar of the storm", but read *tushiyyah*, "success" or "sound wisdom", as in 5:12. With the written form: "you toss me about in the roar of the storm".
n.27: Literally "you will return me to death".
n.28: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Literally "Surely not into a heap of ruins does he stretch out a hand; if in his disaster, to them a cry for help". Or "Surely no one strikes a ruined man when he cries for help in his disaster".
n.30: Literally "My bowels boil and are not silent".
n.31: Literally "I go about dark, without the sun" (Hebrew *chammah*, "heat, sun"): darkened, perhaps in mourning, but not by the sun. Some scholars read *nechamah*, "comfort", for *chammah*, with a small change to the Hebrew: "I go about mourning, without comfort".
n.32: Hebrew *benot ya'anah*, perhaps "ostriches" or "eagle owls". Both jackals and these birds make mournful cries in desolate places (Micah 1:8).
n.33: Literally "My skin is black from upon me".

v: "I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze at a young woman?[^1]
בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י וּמָ֥ה אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן עַל־בְּתוּלָֽה׃
